title: Operator CLI: derive receive addresses and read the vault balance — the vault cannot be funded today
description:
FILED 2026-07-30 from the codex+Fable bead review (Fable, coverage gap #1). DEPENDS ON the mby core substrate.

THE GAP: the operator CLI's verb list is spend / refresh / pending / escape / recover. It omits the operator's FIRST operation -- getting coins in. There is no way to derive a receive address from a sealed descriptor, verify that address independently, or see a balance. This is the R9 pattern one layer earlier than R9 found it: not 'the vault can be sealed but not spent from', but 'the vault can be sealed and not FUNDED'.

OTHER BEADS ALREADY ASSUME THIS EXISTS. btc-policy-cod requires that 'stage deposit addresses are retired with the stage'. ROLLOUT-PLAN's Path suite step 6 requires 'a fresh deposit made to the locked-down vault after Lockdown' -- which needs an address for a vault whose federation can no longer sign. Every stage of the rollout ladder begins by funding a vault.

DELIVER: (a) derive receive addresses from the sealed descriptor at a stated derivation index, with the index tracked so addresses are not silently reused; (b) an INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION step -- re-derive the same address with the user's own cyberkrill and compare, the same bug-not-adversary correctness check btc-policy-wdu establishes for the timelock, because a derivation bug sends funds somewhere unrecoverable and is invisible until it does; (c) balance and UTXO listing from a chain view, including per-coin confirmation height (btc-policy-msj needs exactly this for per-UTXO maturity, so expose it rather than making msj recompute it); (d) address retirement -- mark an address as no longer to be used, which cod requires per stage.

CONSTRAINT: deriving an address must NOT require the federation to be live or the coordinator to be trusted. A deposit address for a locked-down vault is a real requirement, not an edge case.

VERIFY: an address derived by this tool and by cyberkrill match, byte for byte; funds sent to it appear in the balance; an address derived for a LOCKED-DOWN vault still works (the straggler-deposit case ROLLOUT-PLAN step 6 depends on); index tracking survives a restart.

title: V0-11: hot-spend bound (per-tx cap + velocity ledger)
description: Enforce the Hot budget (ADR-0014): a per-tx amount cap + rolling-window velocity cap on hot-class outflow, so the V0-4b duress residual (a coordinator censoring the freeze from a sub-quorum -> a pending hot spend completes) is BOUNDED to ~2V/window instead of an unbounded vault drain. Design: docs/adr/0014-hot-spend-bound.md + ~/.gstack/projects/btc-policy/user-douglaz-design-hot-spend-bound-20260720.md (grilled). Approach B: a RAMDISK HotBudgetLedger with reserve(commitment_id,outflow) at accept + release(commitment_id) on terminal-pre-broadcast; window >= max_commitment_age_secs; outflow = non-vault(non-change) outputs, fee excluded; federation-uniform caps pinned in the manifest; HOT_BUDGET_EXCEEDED/HOT_VELOCITY_EXCEEDED refusals before signing (policy-core per-tx + vault-node velocity). Must land BESIDE the V0-4b arming (btc-policy-axm) so the residual is bounded the moment the arming lands. Tests: per-tx over cap refused every node; N pending spends summing over window -> the over-line one refused while all prior pending; release frees a failed spend's budget; window roll recovers; mismatched caps fail startup; escape/refresh never consume; a fully-censored duress freeze on a pending hot spend -> total completable <= ~2V.
close_reason: V0-11 hot-spend bound merged to main: per-tx cap + velocity ledger (reserve/release, monotonic aging, federation-uniform manifest-pinned caps). Bounds the V0-4b duress residual to ~2V/window. Dual review BOTH CLEAN (codex+Fable): HOT-SPEND BOUND SOUND. 40 policy-core + 330 vault-node tests, demos exit 0.

title: Normative rules are copy-pasted across 4-8 documents with no per-rule authority: every correction reveals more stale twins
description:
FOUND 2026-08-05 during the btc-policy-9zs/ADR-0016 review loop, where it was the single largest
source of findings: TWELVE separate "same claim, two places, one updated" defects across twenty
review passes. Filed as the structural cause rather than continuing to fix instances.

## The measurement

Normative statements are duplicated across the doc set with no designated authority per rule:

- THE TRANSACTION-CLASS PREDICATE (what makes a spend escape/hot/refresh-class) is stated normatively
  in CONTEXT.md, ADR-0012, ADR-0013 §3 and docs/V0-PLAN.md -- and 21 files mention the classes.
- THE MANIFEST CANONICAL PREIMAGE (base_manifest_bytes field list + order) is enumerated in ADR-0013
  §4, PROTOCOL-VECTORS.md, UPGRADE-AND-ROTATION-POLICY.md, DESIGN.md, THREAT-MODEL.md, V0-PLAN.md,
  SETUP-CEREMONY.md and ADR-0007 -- eight-plus copies of a BYTE-EXACT list.
- SpendRequest'S FIELD LIST appears in ADR-0012, ADR-0013 §2, DESIGN.md, TEST-PLAN.md, V0-PLAN.md.

## Why it is worse than ordinary doc debt

These are not descriptions, they are SPECIFICATIONS an implementer follows literally, and the copies
drift in ways that change behaviour:

- ADR-0013 §4's preimage list was TWO FIELDS SHORT of what channel.rs hashes, while instructing
  reimplementers to work "from THIS list + order". Following it yields WRONG_MANIFEST at startup.
- CONTEXT.md's class predicate said "every output" where policy-core says "every DESTINATION output
  (vault change allowed alongside)". Under the glossary reading, the runbook's own partial-sweep
  clawback -- the thing a coerced user is told to run -- is hot-class and waits out a 24h Hold.
- One correction pass fixed the predicate in three files and MISSED further copies inside two of
  those same files. The duplication defeats sweeping, not just memory.

## Deliver

A per-rule AUTHORITY, and copies that cannot silently drift from it. Options, none evaluated:
(a) name one authoritative location per rule and reduce every other copy to a link;
(b) generate the duplicated lists from code (the preimage list especially -- it is derivable from
    `base_manifest_bytes` and a golden test already exists);
(c) a doc test / CI check that greps the known duplicated rules and fails when copies disagree.
(c) is the cheapest and catches drift rather than preventing it; (b) is the only one that makes the
byte-exact preimage list impossible to get wrong. Decide, do not do all three.

## Verify

Introduce a deliberate contradiction in one copy of each of the three rules above and confirm the
chosen mechanism catches it. A mechanism nobody has seen fail is not known to work (same standard as
btc-policy-9yf's launch gate).

## Non-goals

Rewriting the docs for style, or collapsing documents. The problem is duplicated NORMATIVE claims,
not prose volume.

title: /sign is the only blocking-pool surface without admission control: add a bulkhead semaphore
description:
SPLIT OUT of btc-policy-9zs 2026-08-03 after an over-specification audit (codex: CUT; Fable: DOWNGRADE) established that this is NOT part of that bead's correctness fix and that its exposure is PRE-EXISTING - the 9zs reorder changes which lock is held, not blocking-pool occupancy.

WHAT THIS IS NOT. It does NOT bound the delay to Lockdown at T, and must never be justified that way. `work_lock` (pin.rs:95/126) serializes ALL request-time Argon2 node-wide, so admission control cannot change the memory-hard service rate - it only decides whether an excess request queues or is rejected, and a rejected request retries. On an unfair std::sync::Mutex a sustained authenticated flood barges a waiting acquisition at ANY permit count. A semaphore bounds SIMULTANEOUS jobs, not SUCCESSIVE ones. Moreover the threat is already covered: ADR-0012 line 81's release gate is symmetric and per-carrier, so a node whose arming is merely DELAYED is CLOSED, not unfrozen - delay alone forms no quorum, and a request stuck mid-ingress has not signed. The theft class belongs to SILENT receipt loss, which 9zs closes. Anyone re-justifying this bead by Lockdown-at-T should read btc-policy-9zs's AUDIT-1 section first.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY IS. /sign is the node's only BLOCKING-POOL HTTP SURFACE WITHOUT ADMISSION CONTROL - stated that precisely because the looser 'only admission-free surface' is false: /events and /healthz are also admission-free but never touch the blocking pool. /pending caps at 1 (server.rs:138, acquired server.rs:468) and /channel at its configured max_concurrent_channel_requests (default 64, channel.rs:234 - a default, not a fixed cap; server.rs:535), both shedding with owned permits; the sign handler (server.rs:338-357) acquires nothing. Every request parks a DETACHED blocking-pool thread that outlives the 10s handler timeout (server.rs:34, 380-387), and that same pool runs the fire preflight (lib.rs:2760), the combine (lib.rs:2858) and the watchtower pass (watchtower.rs:560). So sustained /sign pressure can starve the FIRING and ALERT tracks. That is a real resource-isolation gap, at P2.

SPEC (fully derived in 9zs; carried over intact). `const SIGN_MAX_CONCURRENCY: usize = 2` in server.rs beside PENDING_MAX_CONCURRENCY (server.rs:138). tokio::sync::Semaphore, try_acquire_owned - SHED, never queue. Acquired after the body is parsed and wiped, before tokio::spawn. The permit MUST be MOVED INTO the blocking closure passed to blocking_with_lockdown_net, which is what makes it survive the HTTP timeout's detach - the pattern /pending (server.rs:479-491) and /channel (server.rs:570-581) already use. Refresh consumes a permit. Saturation answers HTTP 429 with a FIXED body - never a new SignResponse variant, never RATE_LIMITED (that is /channel-protocol vocabulary). Hardcoded constant: not a config key, not manifest-sealed (ADR-0005 makes sealed values permanent for the vault's life), not adaptive (that hands the flood author influence over the bound).

WHY 2. Permits above 1 buy no memory-hard throughput (work_lock serializes it; pin.rs:243-245, lib.rs:1751-1754, pinned by an Arc::ptr_eq test at pin.rs:1288-1293) and almost no ordinary throughput either, since PSBT decode, rung validation, signing and registration all serialize under the post-preflight sign_state hold (lib.rs:5014/5360/5444/5475) - only the out-of-lock chain preflight parallelizes. On the demand side no demo or driver ever issues two concurrent legitimate /sign requests to one node (demo.rs:669-675 relays to ONE node and lets propagation cover the rest; demo.rs:494-501 is a sequential blocking loop; fed.rs:1335-1346 is one synchronous round trip). But the handler's OWN contract invites exactly one overlap: HANDLER_TIMEOUT is 10s (server.rs:34) and on timeout the detached job continues and "commits its verdict for an idempotent resubmit" (server.rs:380-387), so an honest coordinator's resubmit races its own still-running predecessor whose permit may be pinned for a full chain preflight. 1 in-flight + 1 resubmit-or-refresh = 2. Capacity 1 would 429 the documented resubmit path for the whole duration of a slow preflight.

SCOPE: per-surface, /sign only. A relayed request through /channel runs the same handle_sign_after_lock path and the same Argon2 for a fresh nonce (lib.rs:4325-4327, 4795, 4822), and most nodes receive the carrier from a PEER rather than the coordinator (lib.rs:4332-4338), so a /sign-only bound would be decorative FOR A NODE-WIDE ARGON2 CLAIM. There is no such claim here. As a per-surface bulkhead the argument is local: /channel already caps its own pool occupancy at 64, /sign caps nothing, and closing that gap needs no ceiling argument about other paths and no fan-out arithmetic.

SILENCE: admission happens after the body is parsed (so the PIN field HAS been read) but BEFORE the pin is evaluated or classified, and the decision depends on nothing but permit availability - so the 429 cannot vary by pin class - but that is an argument, not a test. Assert it: the saturation response must be byte-identical and the admission decision must not depend on request content beyond size.

GATES: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; full workspace tests; all three demos; attack all (btc-policy-rt0's escape-class-sequences is EXPECTED red on a loaded box - report, do not tune). Plus a test proving the permit SURVIVES the handler timeout (i.e. a timed-out request still holds its permit until the detached job finishes) - that is the property the whole design turns on and it is easy to get wrong.

title: Alert consumption: make watchtower alerts actually reach a human
description:
FILED 2026-07-30 from the codex+Fable bead review (BOTH reviewers, independently). DEPENDS ON the mby core substrate.

THE GAP: the nodes generate alerts and nothing consumes them. ADR-0012 calls recovery-path detection 'the most important watchtower job -- stolen recovery keys are otherwise silent'. Delivery is coordinator-pull via GET /events (ADR-0002). But btc-policy-mby's NON-GOALS explicitly exclude 'monitoring/alerting integration', btc-policy-msj covers refresh maturity only, and btc-policy-57g is a declared non-gate. So nothing anywhere makes a RECOVERY_PATH_SPEND or UNRECOGNIZED_SPEND alert reach a person. On a bad day this is the operator's only sense organ and it is unbuilt.

DELIVER: (a) poll GET /events on every node with correct cursor semantics (no loss, no duplication across restarts); (b) correlate across nodes -- an alert from one node and silence from four is a different situation from all five agreeing, and the difference matters; (c) reconcile pulled sign-logs against the operator's own authorization journal, which ADR-0002 already specifies and nothing implements -- 'a sign event it did not originate means someone else is driving the vault'; (d) actually NOTIFY, through a channel the operator will see when not at the terminal, and say plainly in the deliverable what happens if the notification channel is down; (e) a documented response for each alert class, pointing at the runbook.

STATE THE TRUST LIMIT HONESTLY: delivery is coordinator-pull, so a compromised coordinator can suppress alerts. ADR-0012 accepts this because the coordinator is trusted pre-wrench and during a wrench you already know. That reasoning does NOT extend to the recovery-key alert, which fires when there is no wrench and no reason to suspect anything -- so this bead must say whether recovery-path alerts need a delivery path independent of the coordinator, and if the answer is yes, that is a design question to raise rather than silently implement.

VERIFY: a recovery-path spend on regtest produces a notification an operator actually receives; a spend refused by one node and accepted by four surfaces the disagreement; cursor state survives a restart without replaying or skipping; a node unreachable for an hour does not silently drop out of the correlation.

OWNERSHIP BOUNDARY (bead-polish 2026-07-30): THE AUTHORIZATION JOURNAL BELONGS TO btc-policy-pjl, NOT HERE. Both beads were filed needing 'the spends this operator authorized' -- pjl to diff against GET /pending, this bead to reconcile against pulled sign-logs -- and as written both would have built it. pjl owns designing it (its location, format, and trust properties under ADR-0010's untrusted coordinator); this bead CONSUMES it and must not define a second one. If pjl's design turns out not to serve sign-log reconciliation, that is a finding to raise against pjl rather than a licence to fork the record.

title: Production key-custody lifecycle: holders, backups, drills, and compromise-triggered rotation
description:
FILED 2026-07-30 from the codex+Fable bead review (BOTH reviewers). docs/OPERATIONS-RUNBOOK.md explicitly excludes custody logistics; btc-policy-cod item (8) covers stage-vault realism only, not the alpha's actual custody policy.

THE GAP: this design distributes keys across people and machines -- 5 node keys, a user key, a coordinator auth key, an escape-wallet key, and 2-of-3 recovery keys held by THIRD PARTIES as the inheritance mechanism -- and no bead owns the lifecycle of any of them.

DELIVER a written, drilled custody policy covering: (a) HOLDER ASSIGNMENT and failure-domain checks -- who holds what, and a check that no single event (one house fire, one hostile relative, one subpoena) reaches 2-of-3 recovery keys; (b) THE ESCAPE-WALLET KEY, which is the gap with the sharpest edge: after a duress sweep fires, EVERY coin's safety reduces to that one wallet's custody, and ADR-0012 already notes that if the escape key is attacker-held then duress IS theft. Nothing owns its backup or its independence check; (c) COORDINATOR AUTH-KEY BACKUP AND RESTORE -- ADR-0012 makes losing it fatal to the normal path (rotation means a whole new vault) and specifies a backup procedure that nothing drills; (d) RECOVERY-HOLDER AVAILABILITY DRILLS -- contact them, confirm they still have the key and can still use it, on a stated cadence, because an inheritance key nobody has touched in three years is a guess; (e) HARDWARE-KEY LOSS, once btc-policy-bq6 lands; (f) COMPROMISE-TRIGGERED ROTATION -- which signal forces which rotation, wired to the migration tooling.

NON-GOAL: choosing specific hardware or a specific safe-deposit arrangement. This bead defines the policy and the drills; the owner picks the physical instantiation.

VERIFY: a restore drill actually performed from backups alone, with the primary artifacts set aside -- not a documented procedure, a performed one; the failure-domain check run against the real assignment and its result recorded; each recovery holder confirmed reachable and capable within the stated cadence.

BOUNDARY vs btc-policy-h22 (bead-polish 2026-07-30): h22's destructive drill restores a NODE (reboot-death, re-provisioning, quorum loss). This bead's restore drill covers KEY MATERIAL and the human arrangements around it. Different backups, different failure modes -- do not merge them into one harness.

title: Rollout stage 3: five machines on one provider, MAINNET under the ADR-0015 dust cap
description:
SPLIT 2026-07-30 (codex+Fable bead review): THIS BEAD IS NOW ROLLOUT STAGE 3 ONLY -- five nodes on five separate machines at ONE hosting provider, open (not yet sealed), on MAINNET, first real funds, under the ADR-0015 dust cap and waiver. Stage 2 (the same topology on SIGNET) is its own bead and blocks this one.

WHY THE SPLIT: this bead used to carry stages 2 AND 3, so its stage-3-only blockers -- btc-policy-4y3 (coordinator hardening), btc-policy-cod (funding caps) and btc-policy-zzv (fire-path mempool fix) -- also gated stage 2, which is SIGNET and holds no funds. All three authorities scope those gates to stage 3: ADR-0015 'What the waiver does NOT cover' says 'by the time stage 3 (first mainnet funds) is reached'; ROLLOUT-PLAN's ladder table puts 4y3+zzv on the stage-3 row; cod's own rationale is 'stage 3 cannot be FUNDED before a cap exists'. Stage 2 is the longest-lead engineering in the early ladder (real transport, the channel.rs loopback teardown) and was serialized behind a coordinator-host build and a funding-policy document it does not need. A second reason: one bead spanning 'first networked run' and 'first mainnet funds' hands a drain agent mainnet funding as a sub-step of a signet task, with no stage boundary for cod's abort and descent rules to attach to.

WHY IT IS ITS OWN RUNG: stage 2 is where the loopback assumptions die. Channel endpoints are hard-wired loopback today (crates/vault-node/src/channel.rs ~2934) and every test to date runs five processes on one box, so real transport, real clock skew (the CHANNEL_FRESHNESS_REJECT surface), real latency against the combine window, and real backend independence are all first exercised here. Moving to mainnet in the SAME configuration (stage 3) isolates 'the network changed' from 'the topology changed'.

DEPENDS ON btc-policy-imb (independent federation runtime) for the transport and correlation work, and on stage 1 being complete.

VERIFY: full Path suite on both vaults at each stage; the per-peer freshness/quota surfaces behave on real links.

CORRECTED 2026-07-30 (codex spec review): this VERIFY used to end with "a deliberately co-located federation is still refused (imb's diversity enforcement)" -- which THIS STAGE CANNOT SATISFY, because stages 2-3 ARE the co-located federation. ADR-0015 section 3 resolves it: imb's enforcement gains an explicit test-mode bypass, and USING IT MUST BE RECORDED IN THE STAGE'S ARTIFACTS. So verify instead: (a) the bypass is engaged deliberately and its use is recorded, never silently defaulted; (b) WITHOUT the bypass, imb's enforcement does refuse this exact topology (that is the real assertion, and it belongs to imb); (c) the recorded artifacts are machine-readably tainted as non-promotable, per ADR-0015. The bypass must be compiled out of stage-6+ binaries -- a runtime "which stage am I" check is operator-controlled and therefore no control at all.

title: Coordinator host hardening (the unbuilt half of the ADR-0012 Direction 3 mitigation)
description:
FROM THE 2026-07-29 STATE REVIEW (both reviewers' FIRST or SECOND attack target). ADR-0012 Direction 3 accepts permanently that a coordinator compromised BEFORE the wrench reads the normal PIN and substitutes it for the duress PIN: the escape never arms, no node locks down, and — because every observable is pin-uniform BY DESIGN — the user sees exactly what a working duress path would show. The coerced spend completes after the Hold. This is the only accepted conditional-THEFT residual in the system.

The ADR names two mitigations: a hardened dedicated host, and reproducible builds. NEITHER EXISTS. Reproducible builds are btc-policy-gbw (an earlier draft of this bead cited a nonexistent 'btc-policy-rel'); this bead is the host.

SCOPE CORRECTION 2026-07-30 (codex+Fable spec review): those two mitigations do NOT cover the same vector, and this bead must not be written up as closing R8b. ADR-0012's residual names four vectors -- persistent malware, poisoned build, tampered dependency, and a wrench beginning mid-spend while the normal pin is still in RAM. Reproducible builds (gbw) close the middle two. THIS BEAD REDUCES THE PROBABILITY OF THE FIRST AND REMOVES NO CAPABILITY: resident malware needs no modified binary, since an OS-level keylogger or memory read gets the pin out of a byte-identical vault-cli. NOTHING mitigates the fourth. So the controls that carry weight here are the runtime-targeted ones -- dedicated single-purpose host, no remote administration, verified/measured boot, strict network allowlists, process sandboxing, minimal installed software, frequent clean re-image, controlled updates -- and the acceptance criteria must test those, not disk encryption (little use against live resident malware). The true fix is Direction 1 (device-bound, coordinator-opaque pin), which is hardware-gated and deliberately unplanned.

DELIVER: a documented, reproducible coordinator-host build/deploy — minimal base, no ambient network egress beyond what the relay needs, no other tenants, verified/measured boot, no remote administration, process sandboxing, frequent clean re-image, an update story, and an explicit statement of what an attacker who owns this host still gets (which is: the plaintext PIN, hence duress nullification, bounded by allowlist + Hot budget). NOTE ON THE USER KEY: today it is software and would sit on this same host, which merges this residual with adversary A3. btc-policy-bq6 (hardware signing) is what eventually separates them, but it is NOT part of this bead's completion and MUST NOT BLOCK IT -- this bead gates rollout stage 3, where ADR-0015 deliberately accepts the software user key under the dust cap (owner decision 2026-07-30: hardware signing is optional and postponed; it gates only the stage-9 freeze). Say plainly in the deliverable what an attacker who owns this host still gets -- the plaintext PIN, hence duress nullification, plus the user key while it remains software -- bounded by allowlist + Hot budget.

BE HONEST ABOUT THE CEILING: hardening reduces the probability of pre-wrench compromise; it does not remove the capability. ADR-0012's Direction 1 (a device-bound PIN the coordinator never sees in plaintext) is the actual fix and is deferred to hardware. This bead must not be written up as closing the residual — say what it buys and what it leaves.

VERIFY: the host build is reproducible and documented end-to-end; a written argument, reviewable by an external auditor, for what compromise of this host still yields.

title: reconcile ADR-0012/DESIGN/V0-PLAN duress narrative to the release-gate
description: The V0-4b re-drain wrote a confirmation-gating-is-un-splittable narrative into ADR-0012 + DESIGN.md + V0-PLAN.md. Per the 2026-07-20 dual review the ACTUAL safety is the signer/partial coupling + release-gate (invariant vii); the confirmation count schedules timing, not safety (codex q>=n impossibility). CONTEXT.md Duress PIN already corrected. Reconcile the three docs to lead with the release-gate, keeping the confirmation-gating as the timing/liveness mechanism it is, and cite ADR-0014 for the bounded residual.
close_reason: ADR-0012 + V0-PLAN.md + CONTEXT.md now lead with the signer/partial coupling + release-gate as the un-splittability mechanism (not the confirmation count); Hot-budget-bounded residual cited (ADR-0014).

title: FUTURE HARDENING: operational fault suite (not a gate)
description:
FUTURE HARDENING — deliberately NOT a blocker of any rollout stage, and not a gate on the core-proven milestone or the alpha. Classified as future work on 2026-07-29. Recorded only so the analysis is not lost.

codex's plan review proposed a separate Fault suite alongside the two-vault Path suite, on the argument that the Path suite covers the semantic branches while these are the operational failures that break them. Recorded verbatim in case it becomes relevant later:

- Kill one node, then two, mid-Hold / at T / after partial release / after Lockdown; asymmetric partitions, not just clean shutdown.
- Inject clock skew, rollback and forward jumps: Hold expiry, dynamic T, request expiry, channel freshness, the wall/monotonic split. A bad clock already silently removes a node from the combine set.
- Reorg confirmed hot spends, Refreshes, escapes and recovery spends, including a reorg below the wallet completion anchor (THREAT-MODEL R5/R6 admit this is unmeasured on a real chain).
- Drive the whole escape RBF ladder under fee escalation, mempool eviction, backend disagreement and package/ancestor pressure.
- Crash and restart the coordinator between fan-out, acceptance, polling and retry; verify idempotency and conflicting responses from different node subsets.
- Restore from cold artifacts; lose the coordinator key; migrate to a successor vault; recover with fewer than three live nodes.
- A deposit or Refresh confirming DURING the Hold, followed by a reorg — it changes the escape's live input set.

Fable's additions in the same vein: degraded-quorum operation (spend from a 4-of-5 federation, and verify 2-of-5 refuses everything with Recovery as the only exit); coordinator restore-from-backup onto a fresh machine; a stuck BROADCAST hot spend under a fee spike (hot spends have no bump path, only the escape has a ladder); and asserting that Alerts actually surface, not merely that refusal codes are right.

Both reviewers agreed live reorg testing is NOT worth chasing on signet or mainnet (unschedulable) — deterministic regtest/scripted-backend faults are the right vehicle for most of the above.

title: Network parameter: thread signet/mainnet/regtest through the ceremony and every driver
description:
SPLIT OUT OF btc-policy-wdu 2026-07-30 (bead-polish, codex sizing finding). wdu opened with the words 'TWO sealed-parameter jobs' and carried both; they share only the category 'sealed parameter' and are independently testable. wdu keeps the configurable recovery timelock; this bead is the network parameter.

THE PROBLEM: NetworkKind::Test is hardcoded on the PRODUCTION key path (crates/vault-cli/src/setup.rs:1188); addresses are per-driver Network::{Regtest,Signet} constants; docs/SETUP-CEREMONY.md concedes there is no network parameter anywhere in the codebase yet. The rollout ladder needs signet at stages 1, 2, 4, 6 and 7 and MAINNET at 3, 5, 8 and 9, alternating -- so this is not a constant to flip once at the end, it is a parameter that must be chosen per vault and enforced.

DELIVER: one network parameter threaded through the ceremony and every driver, validated at load, and RECORDED IN THE SEALED ARTIFACTS so a node cannot boot against a backend on a different chain. Manifest-bound and federation-uniform, so a disagreement is a startup failure rather than a silent split -- the same treatment escape_feerate_floor already gets.

WHY IT IS ITS OWN BEAD AND NOT A ONE-LINE FLAG: getting this wrong is a class of loss with no recovery. A vault sealed for signet whose nodes talk to mainnet, or addresses derived under the wrong network, produce coins nobody can spend. It touches the ceremony, the manifest, every driver, and address derivation.

VERIFY: a ceremony sealed for one network REFUSES to boot against another (assert the refusal, not merely that the happy path works); addresses derived under each network match an INDEPENDENT tool (the user's own cyberkrill) -- vault-cli imports vault-node's own manifest code, so an internal-only check proves consistency, not correctness; a manifest whose network field disagrees across nodes fails at startup.

title: Armed-escape Confirmed branch skips the hot-conflict invalidation scan (k0t follow-up)
description: codex k0t review [P2]. When a confirmed duress escape spends inputs also used by hot candidates OTHER than its paired request, production takes the ArmedEscapeState::Confirmed branch (crates/vault-node/src/lib.rs ~2881), which removes only commitment_id and its paired sibling from state.pending. It never calls channel.mark_broadcast, so the input-overlap invalidation scan (channel.rs ~4470, added by btc-policy-k0t) never runs for those other defeated candidates. They therefore stay in GET /pending until expiry even though the node has already observed the conflicting sweep on-chain — contradicting the endpoint's documented settlement semantics ('an id disappears once the candidate is observed on the network') and leaving their Hot-budget reservations metered. FIX SHAPE: extract the overlap scan + release_if_unexposed + mark from mark_broadcast into a separate method (e.g. invalidate_hot_conflicts(spender_id) -> Vec<String>) that does NOT touch the spender candidate itself, then call it from BOTH mark_broadcast and the Confirmed branch, removing the returned ids from state.pending. CARE REQUIRED — this is why it was not done inline: mark_broadcast takes the channel STORE lock while the Confirmed branch already holds SIGN_STATE, so a naive call introduces a lock-order inversion in crown-jewel fire-path code. Establish and document the ordering (or restructure so the store lock is taken outside the sign_state hold) rather than nesting them by accident. The armed escape itself must still be RETAINED through the fire window for in-window reorg recovery. title: attack all: a genuinely racing spend/refresh preflight scenario (f91 follow-up)
description: Fable f91 review [P1], recorded rather than silently dropped. btc-policy-f91's acceptance said 'attack all still passes incl. a new spend-refresh-race scenario'. title: V0-4a: dual PINs (both-Argon2 constant-time) + attempt budget + Lockdown
description:
## V0-4a: dual Argon2id pins + attempt budget with embedded transition table (terminal backoff explicit; max_attempts>=1 + nonempty backoff_schedule validated), same-shaped mutation, deployment-death reboot. Folded audit r3.

FULL TASK SPEC (self-contained; source task file gitignored):

# V0-4a: dual PINs (both-Argon2 constant-time) + per-node attempt budget + Lockdown

## Environment — read first
- No system C compiler. Run cargo/bitcoind via `nix develop -c ...`.
- **Node-local, NO channel** — buildable in parallel with V0-8b (does not depend
  on it). Authoritative: `docs/adr/0012-...` (invariants: "Pin-compare is
  constant-cost", "Fail-closed lockout"), `docs/adr/0013-...` §7 (pin-attempt
  budget), `docs/adr/0008-duress-pins-and-lockdown.md` (Lockdown, RAMDISK),
  `CONTEXT.md` (Duress PIN, Lockdown). The config already has
  `pin_normal_hash`/`pin_duress_hash` (currently plain SHA-256 placeholders —
  this task moves them to Argon2id).

## Outcome
The node verifies the per-request PIN against two enrolled Argon2id digests
**without leaking which pin (or wrong-pin) was submitted through timing**, guards
online guessing with a per-node attempt budget, and can enter the terminal
**Lockdown** state. This task builds the pin/lockdown SUBSTRATE (verification +
budget + lockdown state + FRAUD_SUSPECTED refusal); it does NOT build the duress
arming/sweep state machine (that is V0-4b, which consumes this).

## Why this exists
The duress mechanism (V0-4b) is only as silent as its pin comparison. ADR-0012's
final review found that different Argon2 salts + a short-circuit compare make a
duress pin cost one extra Argon2 (~100ms), measurable by a coordinator-attacker.
And a valid duress pin must arm even under wrong-pin lockout (fail-closed). This
task gets those load-bearing timing/lockout semantics right in isolation, so
V0-4b builds duress logic on a sound pin substrate.

## Required changes (`crates/vault-node`, config)
### 1. Argon2id pin digests + constant-cost compare (ADR-0012 invariant)
- `pin_normal_hash`/`pin_duress_hash` become **Argon2id PHC strings** (own
  salts). **Validate both at startup** as Argon2id with acceptable parameters
  and DISTINCT salts (fatal config error otherwise).
- **On every `SpendRequest`** (NOT RefreshRequest — codex C2: refresh is
  pin-less, ADR-0013 §2, performs NO pin compare and cannot touch the budget),
  **compute BOTH digests unconditionally and constant-time-select the outcome**
  — normal / duress / wrong-pin all cost exactly two Argon2 evaluations and the
  same work. A short-circuit ("try normal; if match stop") is FORBIDDEN — it
  makes duress cost one extra Argon2. "Constant-time byte-compare of the hash"
  alone is NOT sufficient; both Argon2 evaluations must always run.
- The compare yields an internal enum `{Normal, Duress, Wrong}` via a
  constant-time select. Use a **secret PIN newtype** and **zeroize every owned
  copy** of the pin (request buffers + error paths, not just logs). The pin is
  ephemeral, never logged/persisted anywhere (ADR-0008).

### 2. Per-node attempt budget (ADR-0013 §7) — with a NORMATIVE transition table
- RAMDISK/node-lifetime state (tmpfs reboot-death — not durable; a reboot
  destroys the budget AND the signing key alike, so no reset-by-reboot).
- Config: `pin_attempt_budget { max_attempts, window_secs, backoff_schedule,
  lockout_secs }`. **Implement EXACTLY this normative transition table (codex C1
  — embedded here so two implementations cannot diverge). State: `fails`
  (wrong-pin count in the current `window_secs`), `locked_until` (unix secs).**

  | Current state | Event | Action | Next |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | not locked, `fails = k < max_attempts−1` | wrong pin | `fails += 1`; sleep `backoff_schedule[min(k, len−1)]` | not locked, `fails = k+1` |
  | not locked, `fails = max_attempts−1` | wrong pin (**the `max_attempts`-th**) | **sleep `backoff_schedule[min(max_attempts−1, len−1)]` (the terminal backoff — every wrong pin including this one sleeps first), THEN** `fails = max_attempts`; `locked_until = now + lockout_secs` | **locked** |
  | not locked | correct **normal** pin | no budget change (does NOT reset `fails`) | not locked |
  | not locked | correct **duress** pin | no budget change; invoke arm-hook | not locked |
  | not locked | oldest wrong-pin older than `window_secs` | that failure drops out of `fails` (sliding window) | not locked |
  | **locked** (`now < locked_until`) | ANY SpendRequest (normal/duress/wrong) | refuse to sign; **a wrong pin does NOT extend `locked_until`** (no infinite-extension); **a correct DURESS pin STILL invokes the arm-hook** (fail-closed) | locked |
  | locked, `now ≥ locked_until` | any | `fails = 0`; `locked_until` cleared | not locked |

  So: **every wrong pin sleeps its backoff first**, and the `max_attempts`-th
  one then enters lockout (no off-by-one, and "backoff THEN lockout" is
  consistent between the table and the tests). A wrong-pin flood during lockout
  cannot extend it. **Config validation (fatal at startup):** `max_attempts ≥ 1`
  and `backoff_schedule` non-empty (otherwise `max_attempts−1` / `len−1` are
  undefined). No cross-node accounting (per-node suffices — the pin is the same
  value everywhere).
- **Same-shaped budget work (codex C3 — ADR-0012 checklist):** every
  `SpendRequest` performs the **same lock acquisition and the same-shaped state
  update**, with the logical next budget value chosen by **constant-time
  select** — only the *logical* wrong-count changes, never the observable work
  shape. (Not just "two Argon2 evaluations": the budget mutation must also be
  timing-uniform across normal/duress/wrong.)
- **Lockout ≠ Lockdown**: lockout is a transient rate-limit; a locked-out node
  refuses to sign (denial), then recovers after `lockout_secs`.
- **Fail-closed (ADR-0012 invariant):** a valid **duress** pin is a *matching*
  compare — it does NOT consume the attempt budget and (the arming it triggers,
  built in V0-4b) must fire regardless of lockout state. The budget rate-limits
  ONLY wrong pins. A locked-out node signs nothing, so lockout produces denial,
  never an unfrozen signing quorum. (V0-4a exposes the budget verdict + a hook
  V0-4b uses to arm-even-when-locked-out.)

### 3. Lockdown state (ADR-0008, terminal)
- A node-lifetime **Lockdown** state (RAMDISK — never durable disk; reboot =
  node death is strictly stronger; `/unseal` rejected so no durable flag). While
  in Lockdown, every spend/refresh request → `FRAUD_SUSPECTED`; no reset on
  sealed nodes; the only exit is the recovery path.
- V0-4a builds the STATE + the FRAUD_SUSPECTED refusal + the enter-Lockdown
  entry point; V0-4b drives WHEN it is entered (at T under duress).

## Tests
- **Structural constant-cost (PRIMARY — codex improvement):** an injectable
  verifier asserts EXACTLY two Argon2 evaluations run in a fixed order per
  SpendRequest, and budget instrumentation asserts identical state touches
  (lock + same-shaped update) across normal/duress/wrong. A statistical
  wall-clock latency test is SUPPLEMENTAL (keep it coarse to avoid flaky CI).
- **Attempt budget (per the transition table):** reaching `max_attempts` wrong
  pins within `window_secs` → backoff then lockout; a locked-out node refuses to
  sign; recovers after `lockout_secs`; a correct (normal) pin does NOT consume
  the budget; **a valid NORMAL pin is still refused during lockout while a valid
  DURESS pin still invokes the arm hook** (codex improvement).
- **Fail-closed**: a valid duress pin is a matching compare that does NOT consume
  the budget, and the arm-hook fires even when the node is locked out on
  wrong-pin floods; a pin-less RefreshRequest never mutates the budget.
- **Lockdown**: entering Lockdown → every subsequent spend/refresh →
  FRAUD_SUSPECTED; no reset; the pin is never logged/persisted AND request
  buffers/error paths are zeroized (a secret-newtype + zeroize check, not just a
  log grep).
- **Reboot-death = DEPLOYMENT death (codex C5):** the reboot test must destroy
  the simulated RAMDISK/config (incl. `node_seckey`), then assert the node
  CANNOT restart or rejoin (bare machine) — NOT "restart the same binary against
  the same TOML and return an HTTP refusal" (that resurrects the node). The
  budget + Lockdown are gone with everything else; capacity to sign is gone too.

## Scope guard
- Touch `crates/vault-node/` + config + **narrowly-scoped `crates/vault-cli`
  demo/config fixtures** (codex C4 — moving the config pins to Argon2 PHC strings
  requires updating the demo-generated configs/fixtures so `demo first-light`
  still passes). Do NOT build the duress state machine (arming/freeze/sweep/
  Firing — V0-4b), the channel, or broadcast. Do NOT persist the pin or any
  duress signal to durable disk (RAMDISK only).
- **Sequencing:** this rides on V0-8b's final tagged-request shape (both rewrite
  the request handler) — build AFTER V0-8b establishes the stable protocol, then
  attach pin handling to it (codex dependency conclusion).
- Non-goals: device-bound duress tokens (Direction 1/2 rejected), PAKE, pin
  transport hardening (v1). Build the simplest correct substrate.
- Do not run `rb-lite`, signal your own process tree, or touch `.rb-lite/`,
  `.ralph-burning/`, `.git/ralph-burning-live/`, `.beads/`.

## Acceptance criteria
- fmt/clippy -D warnings/test --workspace pass; `demo first-light` exits 0.
- Both Argon2 digests always computed + constant-time-selected (timing test
  passes); per-node budget rate-limits wrong pins and never a valid duress pin;
  Lockdown is terminal + RAMDISK + FRAUD_SUSPECTED. The pin substrate is ready
  for V0-4b to build arming/sweep on.

R1 the k0t gap, ranked attack-this-first list), docs/SBOM-AND-DEPENDENCY-POLICY.md (direct deps w/ rationale, 146 transitive, crypto-critical pinned, dep policy), docs/UPGRADE-AND-ROTATION-POLICY.md (3 categories; any sealed-param change or key rotation = NEW VAULT), docs/PROTOCOL-VECTORS.md (frozen byte-level vectors, transcriptions verified against source), docs/OPERATIONS-RUNBOOK.md (routine checks, refusal codes, Lockdown, incidents, backups). STILL OPEN for (2): the full matrix run with recorded toolchain/binary-hash/config artifacts, and a REPRODUCIBLE RELEASE (none exists; signet-record hashes are debug builds from one machine). Also open: no cargo audit/deny in CI.
(3) OPEN — NEEDS THE USER. Requires a genuine external HUMAN security review. The artifacts in (2) exist largely to make that review possible: an auditor should start with docs/THREAT-MODEL.md, which ends with a ranked list of what to attack first.

LEAVE THE PATH SUITE RE-RUNNABLE (bead-polish 2026-07-30). Every later rung -- cg6, 4wx, s12, qbt, u5r, yt7 -- says 'full Path suite on both vaults', so this bead is where that suite first exists. title: CI runs now, but the launch gate has never been shown to FAIL: no negative control, debug-vs-release profile undecided, recovery-drill ungated
description:
FILED 2026-07-31 while diagnosing btc-policy-rt0. This is the reason nobody noticed rt0, and it is worse than rt0.

ESTABLISHED BY QUERY, not inferred:
- gh run list --workflow=ci.yml --limit 60: 44 runs recorded, 44 FAILURES, ZERO successes, going back to 2026-07-25 (the oldest run retained).
- Every job in every run reports steps=0 and completes in 2-12 SECONDS: 'launch gate (attack all + both demos)', fmt, clippy, test, regtest-backend. Example run 30655779435 (head 2185b68): all five jobs failed between 18:35:51Z and 18:36:03Z with no steps recorded.
- fmt failing is the tell: cargo fmt --check passes locally in under a second on the same commit. A job that cannot even run fmt did not run anything.
- The workflow targets ubuntu-latest (GitHub-hosted, .github/workflows/ci.yml:52,89), and 0 self-hosted runners are registered -- so this is NOT a missing self-hosted runner.

LIKELY CAUSE, NOT CONFIRMED -- needs the owner, who has the billing view: this repository is PRIVATE, private repos consume GitHub Actions minutes, and exhausted minutes (or a spending cap, or Actions disabled at the account level) produces exactly this signature -- every job failing instantly with zero steps. Check Settings > Billing > Actions minutes, and Settings > Actions > General for the repo. If it is minutes, the options are paying for them, moving the heavy launch-gate to a self-hosted runner, or accepting that the gate runs locally only and saying so everywhere it is cited.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN ONE RED TEST. Several beads rest on this gate as if it ran:
- btc-policy-9y5.8 deliverable (2) requires the FULL matrix green with recorded artifacts.
- btc-policy-gbw requires the full matrix run against the frozen commit.
- btc-policy-6nq, btc-policy-6nv and others cite 'attack 16/16' as an acceptance gate.
Every one of those has been resting on a gate that has not executed once in the recorded history. Work has been merged to main across that whole period on the assumption that a push-triggered launch gate was watching. It was not.

ALSO FIX WHILE HERE (codex, this review):
- CI runs the DEBUG binary (.github/workflows/ci.yml:144) while the attack suite's pin calibration adapts to machine speed and build profile, so a debug CI run and a release local run exercise materially different memory costs and contention. Decide which profile is the gate and say so.
- CI says it runs 'both demos' but the CLI now has THREE (first-light, theft-refused, recovery-drill). recovery-drill is #[ignore]d in crates/vault-cli/tests/e2e.rs:40 and absent from the launch-gate steps (ci.yml:170). 'attack recovery' overlaps it but the named demo is not gated.

VERIFY: a CI run that actually executes and goes green on an unmodified main; the launch-gate job visibly running attack all with per-scenario output in the log; a deliberately introduced failure (revert one line, push to a branch) confirmed to turn the gate RED, because a gate nobody has ever seen fail is not known to be a gate.

DO NOT close this by deleting or weakening the workflow. The correct outcomes are: make it run, or move it, or explicitly downgrade every bead that cites it -- not quietly reduce what is claimed.

title: Unbounded sign_state convoy defers Lockdown at T: move both Argon2 evaluations out of the critical section
description:
CONSOLIDATED 2026-08-02 after three review rounds plus a consistency pass. THIS SECTION IS
AUTHORITATIVE. The A/R/S findings below are PROVENANCE ONLY - they record how the design was arrived
at and why each constraint exists. Where they contradict this section, THIS SECTION WINS. Do not
implement from them.

## The defect

handle_sign_now holds `sign_state` (acquired lib.rs:4655, released lib.rs:4867/4943) across BOTH of
the node's memory-hard operations: pin::verify_pin (lib.rs:4795, two Argon2 evaluations, ~400ms) and
arm_carrier_id (lib.rs:4823 -> carrier_kdf.derive). `/sign` has NO admission control - unlike
/pending (server.rs:468) and /channel (server.rs:535). The HTTP timeout does not cancel; the job
detaches and continues (server.rs:380). Node::enter_lockdown needs that same `sign_state`
(lib.rs:2003), and std::sync::Mutex offers no fairness or deadline priority.

Post-wrench the coordinator is UNTRUSTED by design (ADR-0010/0012) and holds the auth key, so it can
mint arbitrarily many validly-signed requests with fresh nonces. The delay to Lockdown is bounded
only by how many it sends. ADR-0008/0012 and CONTEXT.md's Duress PIN entry call the transition at T
UNCONDITIONAL. It is not. PRE-EXISTING and undocumented; distinct from the store-wedge residual at
DESIGN.md:113. The design is already convoy-aware and stopped one step short - lib.rs:4651 records
that the wrong-pin backoff sleep was deliberately moved OUTSIDE this lock.

## NAMING - read this before the phase table

The EXISTING code has two `sign_state` sections and its comments call them "phase 1" (ingress,
lib.rs:4655) and "phase 2" (post-chain-preflight registration, lib.rs:5014 onward). This bead INSERTS
A THIRD. To stop the numbering colliding, the sections are named by ROLE below and those names are
used everywhere in this bead. Existing source comments still say "phase 2" for the REGISTRATION HOLD.

## The design

Both memory-hard operations are PURE functions of immutable state (verified: verify_pin reads
node.pin_evaluator and the request bytes; arm_carrier_id at lib.rs:2404 reads
request.auth_digest(&node.wallet_id) and the immutable carrier_kdf). Neither reads mutable state
under sign_state, so both can move out. This EXTENDS the two-phase pattern handle_sign_now already
has for the chain preflight (drop at lib.rs:4943, out-of-lock preflight behind
node.enter_spend_preflight, re-acquire; lib.rs:4933 documents the re-acquire wait; hardened by bead
btc-policy-f91). It does not invent one.

    INGRESS HOLD (lock)   verify_coord_signature (lib.rs:6326) then nonces.check_and_record (6333)
                          the §0b pin-independent deliverability gates:
                            ensure_request_propagatable (lib.rs:4709) and the delivery horizon
                            (lib.rs:4717-4768, incl. its outbox write). §0 (lib.rs:4691-4699)
                            requires these BEFORE the pin.
                          claim the enter_spend_preflight slot - MUST be inside this hold
                            (lib.rs:2223-2227), else the f91 refresh-overtake race reopens
                          prune_intents, then install MemoOutcome::InFlight keyed by NONCE
                            (carriers_by_nonce, channel.rs:3516) carrying a GENERATION TOKEN
                            of at least (nonce, signature_tag, expiry)
                          explicit drop(state) before every refusal return in this hold
    WINDOW A (no lock)    verify_pin + arm_carrier_id            ~600ms
    COMMIT HOLD (lock)    1. re-check is_locked_down() FIRST, before any intent or overlay write
                          2. record the arm intent AND upgrade InFlight -> Derived as ONE
                             store-locked transaction. THE GENERATION GATE APPLIES TO THE MEMO HALF
                             ONLY: the intent is recorded in EVERY case (it is separately keyed by
                             carrier), and staging without an intent is the "hollow" configuration
                             the source comments forbid. Relinquish the guard's MEMO ownership here
                             per deliverable 2's predicate; the preflight slot is kept through
                             REGISTRATION.
                          3. then the other three predicates - effective-clock expiry (lib.rs:4953),
                             raw-clock future cap (lib.rs:4983), delivery horizon (lib.rs:5003) -
                             each STAGING the carrier on refusal (lib.rs:4964-4971, 5004-5011),
                             EXCEPT the Lockdown exit from step 1, which deliberately does not stage
                          4. charge the attempt budget
    WINDOW B (no lock)    chain preflight                        EXISTING
    REGISTRATION HOLD     register pending, sign, decode PSBTs   EXISTING (source calls it phase 2)

THE FOUR RE-ENTRY PREDICATES RUN AT BOTH RE-ACQUISITIONS. The COMMIT HOLD ADDS its own copies; it
does NOT relocate the existing post-preflight checks at lib.rs:4949-5011, which stay exactly where
they are. Source comment ~lib.rs:4675 states why they guard the chain preflight: "the same expiry
bounds are re-checked after the out-of-lock chain preflight so slow RPC cannot stale the
candidate-registration timestamp". Removing them would let an expiry that lapses during WINDOW B be
registered against, reopening the staged-refusal class the 9y5.3 review closed (lib.rs:4962-4972).

MemoOutcome (channel.rs:1300) gains a second variant. Today it is a SINGLE-VARIANT enum, and
CarrierMemoLookup::Vacant (channel.rs:1331) defines absence as "nonce unseen AFTER the authoritative
handler returned" - a temporal assumption baked into a data type. Without a second variant the
window creates a state nothing can name, and a peer receipt landing in it is read as a refusal,
answered ACCEPTED, and never retried (channel.rs:5316) - a SILENT FALSE POSITIVE in which the sender
believes a peer holds a carrier it never recorded. channel.rs:1320-1329 calls that hazard class
"theft, not censorship". THE CONCRETE STAKE: §0 arming counts receipts to reach t-of-n, so receipts
lost this way mean a node never arms - with two compromised withholders in 3-of-5, a slow honest
node can lose both remaining honest receipts, stay unarmed, and form an UNFROZEN quorum. The duress
freeze silently fails to engage.

An in-flight receipt MUST be answered RATE_LIMITED. retry_loop (channel.rs:5299) RETURNS on Accepted
and Rejected and RETRIES only on RateLimited and UnknownCandidate; answering Accepted IS the bug.
RATE_LIMITED converts a silent false positive into an honest delivery failure, which ADR-0012's
censorship residual bounds. InFlight must map to RATE_LIMITED BEFORE both try_reserve and
claim_carrier_derivation, and must NOT record the sender - routing it through the derivation claim
burns the sender's one derivation and Skips a later honest receipt forever.

## Required deliverables

1. The section structure above, including the both-re-acquisitions rule.

2. THE GENERATION TOKEN, plus the COMPLETE CLEANUP PREDICATE, plus a defined response for every
   outcome.
   THE PREDICATE, restored verbatim from provenance S1 because compression lost it once already:
   **Drop removes ONLY a generation-matched InFlight entry - NEVER a Derived one - and EVERY
   successful Derived installation, INCLUDING the ABSENT branch below, relinquishes memo-cleanup
   ownership.** "Disarm at the upgrade point" alone is NOT sufficient: it is an action that can be
   missed on a branch, whereas the predicate is a guard checked on every exit. Deleting a Derived
   memo on exit recreates the silent-false-positive/failed-arm defect S1 found. Two handler generations can share a nonce key: in check_and_record the expiry test
   PRECEDES the replay test (replay.rs:385-427), so past expiry a differently-signed body with a
   fresh expiry is Accepted and enters its own WINDOW A while the old handler still runs.
   Additionally prune_intents (channel.rs:2314-2321) retains PURELY on `expiry > now` with NO concept
   of an owner, and runs from carrier_memo_lookup (channel.rs:3515), record_arm_intent
   (channel.rs:3434) and this bead's new install site - so under the deliverable-4 flood a LIVE
   InFlight entry whose expiry passes IS PRUNED MID-WINDOW by any other request or receipt. Specify
   all three COMMIT-HOLD cases explicitly, they are not the same:
     - MATCHED InFlight  -> upgrade to Derived, proceed.
     - MISMATCHED (a newer generation owns the key) -> DECIDED: the stale handler must NEITHER
       reinsert NOR delete the memo, and must NOT charge the budget again. It FALLS THROUGH to the
       COMMIT-HOLD expiry re-check, which refuses it (its own expiry has necessarily passed - that is
       the only way a newer generation could claim the key, since check_and_record tests expiry
       before replay, replay.rs:385-427) and STAGES the carrier on that refusal like every other
       expiry exit (lib.rs:4964-4971). Rationale: the stale handler's body differs, so its carrier
       differs, so its own intent is separately keyed and harmless; refusing without staging would
       drop a duress signal the coordinator already authenticated.
     - ABSENT (pruned mid-window) -> DECIDED: RECORD THE INTENT ANYWAY, re-install the memo directly
       as Derived under this request's generation, and continue. This is the A2-compliant reading and
       it is FORCED, not a preference: the alternative - treating absence as staleness and refusing -
       SILENTLY SWALLOWS A DURESS SIGNAL, which is the failure class this entire bead exists to
       close. An implementer must not "simplify" this into the staleness branch.
   The consequence a receipt sees after such a prune is ACCEPTED against a Vacant memo - the silent
   false positive, returning at the expiry boundary. ACCEPTED as a bounded residual: senders GaveUp
   at commitment_expiry (channel.rs:5312) so the lost receipt could not have armed anything anyway
   (confirm_carrier refuses expired carriers on the same comparison, channel.rs:3775). Note it in the code comment; it does NOT need a THREAT-MODEL.md entry.

3. Guard Drop MUST be poison-tolerant - unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()), NEVER .expect. The
   existing guard's Drop is deliberately lock-free and lib.rs:2352-2358 names the hazard: "panic
   while unwinding past a poisoned one". A double panic during unwind ABORTS the process, killing
   every Lockdown net and leaving the node dead-but-UNLATCHED instead of in terminal Lockdown.
   Taking the STORE lock in Drop is acceptable on ordering grounds (sign_state -> store matches
   Node::confirm_carrier, lib.rs:2288-2290); the poison handling is not optional.

4. DEFERRED OUT OF THIS BEAD - see btc-policy-1y2. Recorded here only so the
   decision is visible; DO NOT BUILD IT AS PART OF 9zs. Kept in the numbering so the other
   deliverables' references stay stable.
   A /sign ADMISSION SEMAPHORE - a RESOURCE BULKHEAD, NOT part of the correctness fix.
   Its old safety justification was WITHDRAWN 2026-08-02 by an over-specification audit; see AUDIT-1
   in the provenance for why (short version: work_lock is the same unfair mutex, so the bound dies to
   this bead's own successive-vs-simultaneous argument, and ADR-0012's per-carrier release gate
   already means a merely DELAYED node is closed, not unfrozen). What it actually buys: /sign is the
   node's only admission-free surface (/pending caps at 1, server.rs:138/468; /channel at 64,
   server.rs:535), and flood requests park DETACHED blocking threads (server.rs:34, 380-387) in a
   pool shared with the fire preflight (lib.rs:2760), combine (lib.rs:2858) and watchtower
   (watchtower.rs:560). That exposure is PRE-EXISTING - this reorder changes which lock is held, not
   pool occupancy - which is exactly why it is deferred rather than shipped here.
   SPEC: `const SIGN_MAX_CONCURRENCY: usize = 2` beside PENDING_MAX_CONCURRENCY (server.rs:138);
   try_acquire_owned, shed never queue; acquired after the body is parsed and wiped, before
   tokio::spawn; permit MOVED INTO the blocking closure so it survives the timeout detach (the
   /pending and /channel pattern, server.rs:479-491 / 570-581); Refresh consumes one; saturation is
   HTTP 429 with a fixed body; hardcoded, not config, not manifest-sealed, not adaptive. Count 2 =
   1 in-flight + 1 idempotent resubmit, which HANDLER_TIMEOUT's own contract invites (server.rs:34,
   380-387); permits above that buy nothing, since work_lock serializes all request-time Argon2
   (pin.rs:243-245) and the REGISTRATION HOLD serializes the rest (lib.rs:5014/5360/5444/5475).
   SCOPE: per-surface, /sign only. With no node-wide Argon2 property left to defend, the /channel
   question needs no fan-out arithmetic.

5. retry_after_secs STAYS THE FIXED 1s every existing site sends - DECIDED, the either/or fork is
   closed. RateLimited does not advance the backoff ladder (channel.rs:5318-5325) and the floor is 1s,
   so every in-flight nonce draws one retry per second per peer. That load is trivial and bounded: a
   retry is a pre-Argon2 replay refusal (lib.rs:4681-4689) costing microseconds under sign_state, and
   in-flight nonces are bounded by concurrent handlers. A GROWING retry_after_secs is actively
   counterproductive - it delays honest receipt delivery against short expiries, producing more
   GaveUps (channel.rs:5310-5330), which is the outcome this bead exists to reduce. Put the bound
   arithmetic in the comment; do not write the essay.

6. A TWO-VALUE CLOCK, with the mapping stated, not left to the implementer. record_arm_intent uses
   ONE `now` for first_seen, the overlay calculation, pruning and insertion
   (channel.rs:3425/3434/3452). Required mapping: INGRESS-HOLD effective time supplies the immutable
   `first_seen`; COMMIT-HOLD effective/current time supplies pruning, `pin_budget.charge`
   (which the reorder moves into this hold), and the overlay's current-time
   input; the overlay therefore receives BOTH. Rationale: COMMIT-HOLD time for all of them lets a
   work_lock delay move T later (contra channel.rs:1263); INGRESS-HOLD time for all violates the
   nonce-log effective-clock coupling (replay.rs:358).

7. New arms at the two call sites this bead originally missed. claim_carrier_derivation
   (channel.rs:3559-3566) MUST RETURN FALSE for InFlight, and the upgrade MUST initialise
   resolved_senders EMPTY. confirm_carrier's expiry eviction (channel.rs:3777-3779) retains on
   Derived{..}, so InFlight survives it - correct, and the deliverable-2 ABSENT case already covers
   expiry pruning, so no separate narration is required.

8. StoreShape (channel.rs:12203-12212) MUST mask InFlight's signature_tag exactly as it masks
   Derived's, and for the same reason: the coordinator signature covers the PIN. The irrefutable
   `let MemoOutcome::Derived {...}` at channel.rs:12210 will not compile with a second variant, and
   an unmasked fix would make the SILENCE projection ITSELF a pin oracle.

9. TEST COVERAGE, and the SILENCE case is specified, not left generic. REQUIRED: a CONCURRENT
   NORMAL-vs-DURESS comparison that injects the SAME receipt during WINDOW A under each pin and
   asserts the response, the retry sequence AND count, and that no sender claim is recorded, are
   identical. A single-pin "mid-window RATE_LIMITED works" test does NOT satisfy this and would have
   satisfied the previous wording - that omission is why this is spelled out. Also required:
   structural proof that BOTH Argon2 operations occur outside `sign_state` (a counting/order trace
   proves PLACEMENT; it does not prove elapsed shrinkage, so do not claim shrinkage from it). The obligation is the coverage, NOT a prescribed architecture: the
   existing harness cannot express it (ingress_pass drives one /sign to completion, channel.rs:12434,
   and ingress_trace is thread_local, ingress_trace.rs:227), and IngressOp (ingress_trace.rs:155-218)
   has no PIN-evaluation variant, so verify_pin's position relative to the lock ops has no seam. A
   new seam IS necessary; which seam is the implementer's call.

10. Update or delete the comments the implementation makes false - the debug_assert's "1:1"
    justification at channel.rs:3441 (keep its bound; do NOT replace it with intents.len() +
    memos.len(), which double-counts every Derived request) and the invariant prose at
    channel.rs:2306-2313 / 3430-3444, which assert a state that no longer holds once an intent can be
    born expired. Correcting the false comments is required; a standalone invariant-design exercise
    is not.

11. LANGUAGE. One security-critical correction, two one-liners, one optional.
    (a) REQUIRED: THE LOCKDOWN DELAY HAS NO FINITE BOUND. A semaphore bounds SIMULTANEOUS jobs, not
    SUCCESSIVE ones; on an unfair mutex a continuing flood keeps admitting jobs that overtake a
    waiting enter_lockdown. Neither "one uncontended lock acquisition" nor "phase-2 critical-section
    length times queue depth" is true - both were earlier attempts at this same sentence, which is
    why it is called out. This bead removes ~600ms of memory-hard work from the contended section;
    what bounds the CONSEQUENCES is ADR-0012's release gate plus expiry-bounded arming, not this
    change. Correct CONTEXT.md's Duress PIN entry and ADR-0012 to say exactly that, and record the
    unbounded residual in THREAT-MODEL.md.
    (b) In the lib.rs:4639 comment block the implementation rewrites: the critical section does not drop to "microseconds" - the REGISTRATION HOLD still decodes
    PSBTs, validates rungs, signs and registers (lib.rs:5014/5360/5444/5475).
    (c) Same comment block: the backoff semantics change - a burst can precompute Argon2 and then receive zero backoff
    (pin.rs:692/710).
    (d) OPTIONAL: a CONTEXT.md term for "claimed the nonce, not yet ruled on it". Polish; the enum
    variant and the THREAT-MODEL residual carry the load.

## Rejected alternatives - do not re-propose

(a) An admission semaphore as the PRIMARY fix: bounds concurrency, does not remove the root cause.
Deliverable 4 defers it to a follow-up bead; it is not part of this one. (b) A bare latch_lockdown at T:
force_lockdown_fail_closed's safety argument (lib.rs:2063) rests on a POISONED lock blocking
concurrent registration, and there is no poison at T on a healthy node, so an in-flight /sign could
sign and register after the latch. (c) Moving the nonce check after the KDF to close the window:
reintroduces the captured-request replay convoy lib.rs:4648-4650 deliberately closed. (d) Do not
touch verify_pin's internals - both digests, fixed order, constant-time select.

## Invariants and gates

SILENCE (WINDOW A is pin-uniform BY CONSTRUCTION - both evaluations and the derivation run
unconditionally for every verdict including forced-Wrong, pin.rs:376-397, lib.rs:4790-4800 - but
response and retry-count uniformity are UNVERIFIED and need deliverable 9); signer/partial COUPLING
+ RELEASE-GATE; determinism across the honest set; fail-closed.

LOCKDOWN AT T IS DELIBERATELY NOT LISTED ABOVE AS A DELIVERED INVARIANT, and that omission is the
point. Per deliverable 11(a) this bead does NOT make it unconditional - it removes ~600ms of
memory-hard work from the contended section, and NOTHING MORE. It does not bound concurrent
occupancy either: that was the deferred semaphore's contribution and now belongs to
btc-policy-1y2. An UNBOUNDED acquisition delay on an unfair mutex remains. Listing it unqualified here would be the same
broader-than-mechanism claim in abbreviated form, which is how it survived three previous rewrites.
What must not REGRESS is the existing behaviour: the deadline driver still fires, and the transition
is still attempted every tick.

GATES: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; full workspace
tests INCLUDING all seven SILENCE comparison cases (they compare normal-vs-duress RELATIVELY, not
against a golden sequence, so a pin-uniform reorder keeps them green - if any case needs WEAKENING,
STOP and escalate, that means the reorder became pin-dependent); all three demos; attack all
(btc-policy-rt0's escape-class-sequences is EXPECTED red on a loaded box - report, do not tune); and
the STRUCTURAL PROOF required by deliverable 9 that both Argon2 operations occur outside
`sign_state`, using whichever seam deliverable 9's implementer chooses - never wall-clock, and never
described as proof of elapsed shrinkage, which a placement trace cannot show.


=================================================================
AUDIT-1, 2026-08-02 - the over-specification pass (codex: CUT deliverable 4; Fable: DOWNGRADE).
Six rounds in, every prior round had only ADDED. This one was run inverted, default answer CUT.
=================================================================

WHY DELIVERABLE 4'S SAFETY JUSTIFICATION DIED. It claimed WINDOW A is otherwise unbounded, so a
flood defers arming. But this bead's own deliverable 11(c) says a semaphore bounds SIMULTANEOUS
jobs, not SUCCESSIVE ones - and work_lock (pin.rs:95/126) is the SAME unfair std::sync::Mutex, so a
sustained flood barges the duress request's work_lock acquisition at ANY permit count. The argument
had been applied to sign_state/Lockdown but not to work_lock/WINDOW A. Applied consistently it
collapses. Separately the threat is ALREADY COVERED: ADR-0012 line 81's release gate is symmetric
and per-carrier - "every registered pair, normal or duress, additionally waits for its own carrier's
t-holder decision" - so a node whose arming is merely DELAYED is CLOSED, not unfrozen; delay alone
forms no quorum, and a request stuck in WINDOW A has not signed. The unfrozen-quorum/theft class
belongs to SILENT receipt loss, which deliverables 1-3 close; the converted outcome is the
censorship residual ADR-0012 accepts and ADR-0014's Hot budget bounds. Provenance item A5 framed
this correctly as a P2 resource bulkhead; the consolidation ESCALATED it into a Lockdown defence it
structurally is not. Recorded because that escalation-during-consolidation is a failure mode worth
recognising, not just a wrong sentence.

VERIFIED FOR THE RECORD (relevant if the scope question is ever reopened): a relayed fresh-nonce

A0. [P0, BOTH] THE PHASE SPLIT AS WRITTEN REOPENS THE RACE BEAD f91 CLOSED. enter_spend_preflight's
own doc requires the slot be claimed WHILE sign_state IS STILL HELD IN PHASE 1 (lib.rs:2223-2227),
and the refresh-subordination invariant is stated outright: "there is no instant at which an
in-flight spend is invisible to this rule" (lib.rs:5697-5708, predicate lib.rs:5713). The proposed
out-of-lock window A sits AFTER phase 1 releases and BEFORE the slot claim at lib.rs:4940, so during
it the spend is in neither `pending` nor the preflight counter. A refresh can complete its shorter
pipeline, pass lib.rs:5713, and register as immediately fireable over an input the spend's mandatory
escape needs; candidate registration checks only same-commitment conflicts and capacity
(channel.rs:2350-2366), so nothing downstream re-detects it. The window is attacker-stretchable: the
very flood this bead models queues the victim on work_lock for K x ~600ms. FIX: claim the RAII slot
in PHASE 1 and hold it continuously through BOTH unlocked windows and final registration. The
guard's lock-free Drop (lib.rs:2364-2367) already tolerates release on every exit.

A1. [P0, CODEX ONLY - verified independently, Fable missed it] THE WINDOW CREATES A STATE THE CODE
CANNOT REPRESENT: "nonce consumed, carrier memo absent". Coordinator freshness consumes the nonce in
phase 1 (lib.rs:4682); the memo is not installed until record_arm_intent (lib.rs:4822,
channel.rs:3449). CarrierMemoLookup::Vacant DEFINES ITSELF as "Nonce unseen AFTER the authoritative
ingress handler returned: that handler did not record an intent" (channel.rs:1331-1334) - there is
no in-flight variant. So a peer receipt arriving during window A is read as "the handler refused
this", discarded (lib.rs:4383-4385), and its sender is answered ACCEPTED and never retries
(channel.rs:5315). Node::confirm_carrier's sign_state acquisition (lib.rs:2288) is precisely what
forbids that ordering today. CONSEQUENCE: §0 confirmation-gated arming counts receipts to reach
t-of-n. Receipts lost in this window mean the node may never arm - with two compromised withholders
in 3-of-5, a slow honest node can lose both remaining honest receipts, stay unarmed, and form an
UNFROZEN quorum. That is a duress-arming failure: the coercion protection silently does not engage.
THIS MUST BE SOLVED BEFORE THE REORDER SHIPS. Candidate direction (NOT yet validated): install an
in-flight marker keyed by NONCE in phase 1, so the receipt path can distinguish "handler refused"
from "handler still working" and retain/retry instead of dropping. Do NOT solve it by moving the
nonce check after the KDF - that reintroduces the captured-request replay convoy lib.rs:4648-4650
deliberately closed.

A2. [P1, BOTH] "RE-CHECK is_locked_down() AND EXPIRY" IS INCOMPLETE, AND THE ORDERING IS WRONG.
The existing preflight re-entry checks FOUR predicates, not two: Lockdown (lib.rs:4949),
effective-clock expiry (lib.rs:4953), the raw-clock future cap (lib.rs:4983), and the delivery
horizon (lib.rs:5003). Worse, that re-entry runs with the arm intent ALREADY RECORDED, which is why
all its refusal paths stage the carrier (lib.rs:4964-4971, 5004-5011: staging without that ordering
leaves "the intent ... hollow"). The new phase 2 must CREATE the intent, so copying the discipline
literally yields a request whose expiry crossed during window A refused with NO intent recorded and
NO holder slot claimed - the "silently swallow the duress signal" class the 9y5.3 review closed.
FIX: phase 2 records the intent BEFORE the re-checks, and every new refusal path stages the carrier.
Each new node-local refusal must also define its forwarding/self-holder behaviour.

A3. [P1, BOTH] THE CLOCK NEEDS TWO VALUES, NOT ONE. record_arm_intent currently uses a SINGLE `now`
for the promised first_seen, the current-time overlay calculation, intent pruning, and insertion
(channel.rs:3425/3434/3452). Using phase-2 time for all of them lets an arbitrary work_lock delay
move T LATER, contrary to channel.rs:1263. Using phase-1 time for all of them violates the nonce-log

current/effective time values. State which one each consumer gets.

A4. [P1, BOTH] PHASE 1 ALSO CONTAINS THE §0b GATES, which the target shape above omits: the

A1 RESOLVED 2026-08-02 (grilling session). This SUPERSEDES the "candidate direction (NOT yet
validated)" in A1 above. Design settled against source; two open questions named at the end are
genuinely open and must not be glossed.

R1. THE ROOT CAUSE IS A MISSING DOMAIN STATE, NOT A MISSING CHECK. MemoOutcome (channel.rs:1300) is
a SINGLE-VARIANT enum - it can express only `Derived`. CarrierMemoLookup::Vacant (channel.rs:1331)
then bakes a TEMPORAL assumption into a data type: "Nonce unseen AFTER the authoritative ingress
handler returned". Absence is DEFINED to mean "already decided, recorded nothing". There is no way
to say "claimed the nonce, still deciding" - which is exactly the state the reorder creates. The
ubiquitous language has the same hole: CONTEXT.md defines Commitment, Pending spend, Alert and
Refusal, but has no term for a nonce the handler has claimed and not yet ruled on.

R2. THE FIX: MAKE IN-FLIGHT REPRESENTABLE.
    enum MemoOutcome {
        InFlight { signature_tag },   // NEW - installed in phase 1, nonce is known there
        Derived  { carrier, signature_tag, resolved_senders },
    }
carriers_by_nonce is keyed by NONCE (channel.rs:3516), and the nonce IS known in phase 1, so an
entry can exist before the carrier is derived. Phase 2 upgrades InFlight -> Derived.

R3. THE RECEIPT ANSWER IS FORCED BY THE RETRY MACHINERY - it must be RateLimited, never Accepted.
retry_loop (channel.rs:5299-5340) RETURNS on Accepted and on Rejected, and RETRIES only on
RateLimited { retry_after_secs } and UnknownCandidate. Answering Accepted is precisely today's bug
(it terminates the sender's retry loop). RATE_LIMITED already has precedent on this exact surface:
the DeriveForConfirmation busy-slot path answers RATE_LIMITED so the sender retries with a fresh
channel envelope rather than consuming the one receipt the retry exists to deliver.

R4. WHY RateLimited IS RIGHT FOR A BETTER REASON THAN "IT RETRIES". The fan-out error path
(lib.rs:4158) carries BOTH MSG_TYPE_REQUEST and MSG_TYPE_PARTIAL, and its comment - "a peer that
never accepts costs redundancy, never safety: the combine simply proceeds with whoever answered" -
reasons about the COMBINE, i.e. partials. For a carrier, non-delivery means that peer never arms;
that case is ALREADY in the threat model as ADR-0012's censorship residual, bounded by the Hot
budget. What is NOT in the threat model is the failure this window creates: the peer RECEIVES the
carrier, answers ACCEPTED, and records nothing - a SILENT FALSE POSITIVE, categorically worse than
censorship because the sender believes a node holds a carrier it never recorded. RateLimited
converts that false positive into an honest delivery failure the existing model already bounds. If
retries exhaust, the outcome degrades to documented censorship rather than phantom holders. Note
channel.rs:1320-1329 already names this hazard class and calls it "theft, not censorship".

R5. ONE RAII GUARD, NOT TWO. Finding A0 already requires claiming the enter_spend_preflight slot in
PHASE 1 and holding it across both unlocked windows. The InFlight memo entry MUST ride that SAME
guard: one object claimed in phase 1, owning both the preflight slot and the memo entry, released on
every exit. There are many refusal exits between phase 1 and phase 2 (the four re-entry predicates,
charge.refuse, policy refusals); hand-rolled cleanup would have to catch each one. The existing
guard's lock-free Drop (lib.rs:2364-2367) already tolerates release on every exit. A leaked entry is
bounded rather than permanent: prune_intents prunes on the nonce horizon (channel.rs:3515), so the
worst case is a memo that expires with its nonce.

R6. PHASE 2 ORDER (combining A2 and this): record the intent and upgrade InFlight -> Derived BEFORE
the four re-checks, and stage the carrier on every new refusal path. Recording after the re-checks
reproduces A2's hollow-intent bug.

R7. TIMING IS FINE, AND NOT A REGRESSION UNDER FLOOD. The first backoff rung is 1s
(default_backoff, channel.rs:5272) with a 1s floor in retry_loop, against a ~600ms window - one
round-trip normally suffices, and the retry deadline is the commitment expiry. Under the flood this
bead models, window A stretches to K x ~600ms and receipts retry longer. That is NOT worse than
today: today the same flood makes an incoming receipt BLOCK on sign_state inside confirm_carrier
(lib.rs:2288) while holding a channel permit. RateLimited releases the permit and retries - the same
trade DeriveForConfirmation's busy-slot path already makes deliberately.

R8. SILENCE. Window A is pin-uniform BY CONSTRUCTION - both Argon2 evaluations and the carrier
derivation run unconditionally for every verdict including forced-Wrong - so the in-flight answer
cannot vary by pin. But this is a NEW RESPONSE CLASS on a duress-adjacent surface, so it needs a
pin-uniformity TEST, not an argument. Extend the c9r comparison cases to cover a receipt arriving
mid-window under both pins.

R9. LANGUAGE. Adding this state means the glossary gains a term. Once the variant lands, add it to
CONTEXT.md - the domain needs a word for "this node has claimed the nonce and not yet ruled on it",
because the absence of that word is what let the bug exist. Do NOT put implementation detail in
CONTEXT.md; name the STATE, not the enum.

OPEN QUESTIONS - genuinely unresolved, do not gloss. (Q1) Does MemoOutcome::InFlight need capacity
accounting distinct from MAX_COORD_NONCES? Entries now appear EARLIER in the request lifecycle, so
the live-entry population changes shape even if its bound does not; the debug_assert at
channel.rs:3446 ties intent count to the nonce log and may need revisiting. (Q2) What does a SECOND
direct /sign for the same nonce see mid-window? It SHOULD hit the phase-1 nonce replay path
(NonceDecision::Replayed, lib.rs:6354) and never reach window A - but this was NOT traced. Verify
before relying on it.
