A1 REVISED AGAIN 2026-08-02 after a two-model panel on the R1-R9 design (codex: DESIGN-BROKEN;
Fable: DESIGN-NEEDS-CHANGES). BOTH found the same two P0s. R5 as written is WRONG and is superseded
by S1-S2 below. R6, R7 and R8 all need amendment. The remaining R-items stand.
=================================================================

S1. [P0, BOTH] THE SHARED GUARD DELETES THE REAL MEMO ON THE SUCCESS PATH. R5 said one guard owns
the preflight slot AND the memo entry, "released on every exit", worst case "a memo that expires with
its nonce". That reasoning holds only while the entry is InFlight. record_arm_intent performs the
upgrade by OVERWRITING carriers_by_nonce with MemoOutcome::Derived (channel.rs:3466-3476), and the
successful return IS an exit - so the guard deletes the Derived memo the whole receipt path depends
on. Traced failure: a duress /sign is accepted, phase 2 records the intent and upgrades the memo, the
handler returns, the guard drops and deletes it; every peer receipt then hits carrier_memo_lookup ->
Vacant (channel.rs:3516-3518) -> None (lib.rs:4383-4385) -> ACCEPTED -> the sender's retry_loop
returns (channel.rs:5316). No node reaches t holders. Nothing arms. THAT IS THE EXACT FAILURE A1
EXISTS TO CLOSE, REINTRODUCED ON THE NORMAL PATH rather than an edge case.
FIX: the guard needs TWO ownership states. Retain the preflight counter through final registration
(A0 requires that), but RELINQUISH memo-cleanup ownership at the moment of the atomic upgrade. Drop
must remove the entry ONLY IF it is still InFlight AND still THIS request's generation.

S2. [P0, BOTH] A DROP THAT TAKES THE STORE LOCK WITH .expect TURNS A DESIGNED FAIL-CLOSED POISON
INTO A PROCESS ABORT. The existing guard's doc ALREADY FORBIDS THIS - lib.rs:2352-2358 says "Drop
takes NO lock. That is deliberate and load-bearing: ... a guard that re-took that lock would deadlock
... or - worse - panic while unwinding past a poisoned one." I proposed extending a guard whose own
comment rules the extension out. Traced failure: a thread panics inside record_arm_intent while
holding the store lock; the store poisons on unwind; unwinding reaches the guard's Drop, which calls
.lock().expect(...), gets PoisonError, and panics DURING unwind -> Rust ABORTS. Abort kills the
in-job blocking_with_lockdown_net net, the outer handler arm (server.rs:373) and the 1 Hz driver
nets, so latch_lockdown (lib.rs:2016) never writes the xattr and THE NODE DIES UNLATCHED instead of
reaching terminal Lockdown - the fail-closed destination lib.rs:2047-2068 exists to guarantee. In
model, not theoretical: force_lockdown_fail_closed and critical_lock_poisoned exist precisely because
a poisoned critical section is expected.
FIX: Drop MUST be poison-tolerant - unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()), NEVER .expect. Taking the
STORE lock in Drop is acceptable on ordering grounds (guard drops before `state`, so store is taken
inside the sign_state critical section, which matches Node::confirm_carrier's sign_state->store order
at lib.rs:2288-2290 - no inversion), but add an explicit drop(state) before phase-1 refusal returns
so those exits do not wait on the store while holding sign_state.

S3. [P0/P1, CODEX] TWO HANDLER GENERATIONS CAN SHARE ONE NONCE KEY. The phase-1 replay assumption
(R-series Q2) is verified only WHILE THE FIRST NONCE IS LIVE. In check_and_record the expiry test
PRECEDES the replay test (replay.rs:385-427), so once expiry passes, the exact old request sees
CommitmentExpired - but a DIFFERENTLY SIGNED body with a FRESH expiry is Accepted and enters its own
window A while the old handler is still running. Window A can outlive a 60s expiry (see S6).
Unconditional nonce-keyed insertion would then let the STALE handler overwrite the NEW generation's
entry (channel.rs:3466-3475). FIX: upgrade and Drop must both compare an unforgeable GENERATION
TOKEN - at minimum (nonce, signature_tag, expiry). A stale handler must never reinsert or delete.
This is the same mechanism S1's fix needs, so build it once.

S4. [P2, CODEX] Q3 ANSWER - no conceptual DeriveForConfirmation/Skip problem EXISTS, but only under
a precise condition: InFlight must map DIRECTLY to RATE_LIMITED before BOTH try_reserve AND
claim_carrier_derivation, and must NOT record the sender anywhere. claim_carrier_derivation must
return false for InFlight; the upgrade initialises resolved_senders empty (channel.rs:3545-3566).
IF InFlight IS ROUTED THROUGH THE DERIVATION CLAIM, the sender burns its one derivation against an
InFlight entry and a later conflicting-signature honest receipt is Skipped FOREVER - a P0 lost
receipt, the same class this whole design exists to prevent. After Derived, the exact-signature match
occurs before the spent-sender check (channel.rs:3520-3540), so an exact retry is not skipped.

S5. [P2, FABLE] RATE_LIMITED DOES NOT ADVANCE THE BACKOFF LADDER, so the new response class pins
honest peers at 1 Hz for the entire window. In retry_loop only UnknownCandidate/Err advance the
ladder index; RateLimited uses the server-supplied retry_after_secs VERBATIM (channel.rs:5318-5325)
and every existing site sends 1 (lib.rs:4405, server.rs:539), with a 1s floor at channel.rs:5339. So
every peer receipt for every in-flight nonce re-attempts once per second for all of window A, and
each attempt re-enters handle_sign_after_lock (lib.rs:4326) which ACQUIRES sign_state for its replay
refusal. Under the flood this bead models that is a SELF-INFLICTED SUSTAINED STREAM OF sign_state
ACQUISITIONS ON THE VERY LOCK THE BEAD IS PROTECTING. R7 compared permit behaviour and concluded "not
worse than today"; that is sound for permits and SILENTLY OMITS THE RETRY RATE. FIX: specify a
growing retry_after_secs, or state the 1 Hz cost explicitly and justify it.

S6. [P2, FABLE] WINDOW A IS UNBOUNDED, SO A5'S ADMISSION SEMAPHORE IS LOAD-BEARING, NOT OPTIONAL.
work_lock is a plain unfair std::sync::Mutex (pin.rs:95/126), the blocking-pool queue is unbounded,
and /sign has no admission control - so with MAX_COORD_NONCES = 4,096 (replay.rs:409) window A can
stretch to roughly 4,096 x 600ms ~ 40 MINUTES. A hostile coordinator sets expiry to its own minimum,
now + delivery_horizon_secs = 60s (lib.rs:6197-6200, default at lib.rs:779-781). Every honest peer's
retry_loop then hits GaveUp at commitment_expiry (channel.rs:5312) long before the memo upgrades, so
the victim collects no receipts and never arms. R4's "degrades to documented censorship" is right as
far as it goes, but UNDER THE FLOOD THIS BEAD MODELS THE DEGRADATION IS THE COMMON CASE, NOT THE
TAIL. Fable judges this not a regression (today the receipt blocks on sign_state behind the same
convoy and confirm_carrier refuses it past expiry anyway, channel.rs:3775) - but A5 is what actually
bounds it. PROMOTE A5 from "additional deliverable" to a REQUIRED part of this bead.

S7. [P2, FABLE] R6'S ORDER LETS record_arm_intent RUN AFTER TERMINAL LOCKDOWN LATCHED. Today the
phase-1 Lockdown check (lib.rs:4665) and the arm hook (lib.rs:4827) sit inside ONE continuous
sign_state hold, so a store mutation after Lockdown is structurally impossible. Window A breaks that,
and R6 mandates recording the intent BEFORE the four re-checks - of which Lockdown is the first
(lib.rs:4950). So write_safety_overlay (channel.rs:3425) can run on a node that entered terminal
Lockdown during window A, making lib.rs:4491's "answers FRAUD_SUSPECTED and does nothing else" false.
FIX: re-check Lockdown FIRST, before recording the intent; keep the intent-before-re-checks ordering
only for the other three predicates. Also CARVE OUT the Lockdown exit from R6's blanket "every new
refusal path stages the carrier" - today it deliberately does NOT stage, and staging there would
contradict ADR-0008 terminal semantics.

S8. [P2, FABLE] R8'S TEST IS NOT IMPLEMENTABLE IN THE EXISTING HARNESS, AND THE SILENCE PROJECTION
ITSELF CAN BECOME A PIN ORACLE. ingress_pass (channel.rs:12434-12474) drives ONE /sign to completion
and samples store_shape afterwards, and ingress_trace is thread_local! (ingress_trace.rs:227). A
receipt arriving MID-WINDOW is concurrent with a /sign that has not returned, so none of the seven
c9r cases can express it and the trace cannot span two threads. R8 said "extend the c9r comparison
cases"; it requires a NEW CONCURRENT HARNESS. Second and more concrete: StoreShape deliberately MASKS
Derived's signature_tag (channel.rs:12203-12204, 12211-12212) BECAUSE THE COORD SIGNATURE COVERS THE
PIN. The irrefutable `let MemoOutcome::Derived {...}` at channel.rs:12210 will not compile with a
second variant, and whoever fixes it MUST MASK InFlight's tag too - leaving it unmasked would make
the SILENCE projection itself a pin oracle.

S9. [P3, FABLE] A PHASE-1 INSTALL SITE MUST PRUNE, and phase 2 can create an intent BORN EXPIRED.
Today carriers_by_nonce's only writer is record_arm_intent, which calls prune_intents immediately
before inserting (channel.rs:3434); a phase-1 install path that omits it lets the map accumulate
across the whole max_commitment_age_secs window when /channel traffic is absent. Separately, moving
intent creation to phase 2 after an unbounded window A - ordered before the expiry re-check - can
insert an intent and memo whose expiry <= now, which the pre-insert prune does not clean. Bounded
(confirm_carrier evicts on the same comparison at channel.rs:3775) but the invariant comments at
channel.rs:2306-2313 and 3430-3444 assert a state that no longer holds; update them.

S10. [P3, BOTH] TWO CALL SITES THIS BEAD NEVER NAMED. claim_carrier_derivation's match
(channel.rs:3559-3566) and confirm_carrier's expiry eviction (channel.rs:3777-3779) both need new
arms. The eviction one carries a real DECISION, not just a compile fix: its retain predicate matches
Derived{..}, so InFlight entries SURVIVE eviction. That is the correct behaviour - do not evict a
claim whose handler is still running - but it must be a STATED decision, not a side effect of pattern
syntax.

S11. [P2, CODEX] The debug_assert at channel.rs:3446 needs no relaxation and MUST NOT be replaced by
intents.len() + memos.len(), which double-counts every Derived request. It still protects a real,
narrower invariant. Update its "1:1" commentary and add a SEPARATE memo/InFlight invariant; relaxing
it would conceal stale-handler resurrection (S3).

S12. [P3, FABLE] The residual language remains too strong. "One uncontended lock acquisition remains"
understates it: under a 4,096-deep flood enter_lockdown (lib.rs:2003) contends with 4,096 phase-2
critical sections that decode PSBTs, sign, and register candidates. Honest statement: "bounded by
phase-2 critical-section length times queue depth, on an unfair mutex."

ANSWERS TO THE ORIGINAL OPEN QUESTIONS. Q1: no separate CAPACITY accounting is needed - the bound is
transitive through the nonce log (4,096, replay.rs:404-411) and abandonment cannot inflate it because
/sign jobs are detached and run to completion (server.rs:343/380). But OWNERSHIP accounting IS needed
(S3), and prune_intents CAN delete a live InFlight entry (channel.rs:2314-2321 retains purely on
expiry, with no concept of an owner). Q2: the bead's assumption is CORRECT while the nonce is live -
a second direct /sign refuses NONCE_REPLAYED at lib.rs:4689 and never reaches window A or touches the
memo - but see S3 for what happens across an expiry boundary. Q5: no pin-class-dependent control-flow
path exists in window A (verify_pin always evaluates Normal then Duress and selects afterwards,
pin.rs:376-397; forced-Wrong is applied only after both evaluations, lib.rs:4790-4800; the derivation
runs independently of the verdict) - but response and RETRY-COUNT uniformity remain UNVERIFIED and
need the new concurrent test from S8.

   that `derive()` locks (pin.rs), and `pin_and_carrier_kdfs_share_one_node_wide_memory_slot`
   already asserted it. Concurrent WINDOW As serialize node-wide; the Argon2 pacing MOVED from
   `sign_state` to `work_lock`, it did not disappear. Note that AUDIT-1 used exactly this fact to
   kill deliverable 4's safety justification and did not sweep the other claims resting on it.

2. DELIVERABLE 5's BOUND WAS WRONG. 'That load is trivial and bounded' treated WINDOW A as a
   constant. It is not: because WINDOW A serializes on that same work_lock, its DURATION scales
   with concurrent handlers, so retries per in-flight nonce grow ~C^2 x peers and compete for
   /channel's 64 permits with honest partials. Corrected arithmetic now lives in THREAT-MODEL R11.

3. '/sign IS THE NODE'S ONLY ADMISSION-FREE SURFACE' IS FALSE. `/events` and `/healthz` carry no
   permit either; only `/pending` (capped at 1) and `/channel` (semaphore) do. The load-bearing
   claim -- the one R11's argument actually needs -- is that /sign is the only admission-free
   surface that ACQUIRES `sign_state`. The same overclaim was corrected in btc-policy-1y2 on
   2026-08-02 and survived here; a reviewer raised it in round 3 and it was silently dropped for
   five rounds, because readers who know the right claim reconstruct it from the wrong sentence.

4. DELIVERABLE 2's BOUNDING ARGUMENT FOR THE ABSENT RESIDUAL DOES NOT HOLD IN GENERAL. It argued a
   pruned-then-ACCEPTED receipt is harmless because 'senders GaveUp at commitment_expiry so the
   lost receipt could not have armed anything anyway'. That holds only when the expiry is REAL.
   Under a TRANSIENT forward clock excursion the carrier is still live once the clock corrects, and
   the handler proceeds to sign while the receipt is gone. Mitigated in the implementation
   (`prune_intents` now retains an InFlight claim, and a Derived memo whose owner is still ruling);
   the RULED-memo half is pre-existing and is filed as btc-policy-q6v.

ALSO SHIPPED BEYOND THE SPEC: `CarrierMemoLookup::AwaitingPropagation`, closing the same
silent-false-positive class across WINDOW B. That instance PREDATES this bead (verified identical
on origin/main) and was found by the round-7 panel.

DELIVERABLE 4 WAS NOT BUILT, as specified -- no /sign semaphore exists. Still deferred to
btc-policy-1y2. Deliverable 11(d) was declined as optional, with reasoning.

METHOD NOTE WORTH KEEPING: eight rounds of reviewing this bead's TEXT found none of items 1-4. One
round against a compiler found the first. The defects were invisible to text review because they
exist only as interactions between the spec's requirements and the code they land in.
close_reason:
Merged 2026-08-05 as b4087b3 (PR #1). Three-hold /sign restructure with both Argon2id PIN
evaluations and the carrier derivation outside sign_state; MemoOutcome::InFlight + generation
gate closing the WINDOW A silent-receipt-loss path; CarrierMemoLookup::AwaitingPropagation
closing the pre-existing WINDOW B instance of the same class.

Deliverables 1-3 and 5-11(a)(b)(c) done. 4 deferred to btc-policy-1y2 as specified — no /sign
semaphore exists. 11(d) declined as optional, with reasoning.

VERIFIED TWICE: full local gates (fmt, clippy -D warnings, 685 tests, three demos, attack all
16/16) and CI on a dedicated runner (launch gate 17 steps, 16/16). The seven SILENCE comparison
cases are byte-identical to main and passed unmodified — none needed weakening.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO, recorded because three earlier attempts at this sentence overclaimed: it
does not make Lockdown at T unconditional. The acquisition delay on an unfair mutex still has no
finite bound (THREAT-MODEL R11).

FOUR OF THIS BEAD'S OWN CLAIMS WERE FALSIFIED BY IMPLEMENTING IT — see the note on this bead.
Residual filed as btc-policy-q6v; two unrelated defects found in passing as btc-policy-tf0 and
btc-policy-xz2.

title: V0-8a0: migrate vault-node to tokio+axum, http.rs deleted
description:
## Outcome
vault-node serves /sign + /events via axum on tokio (one port, fully async), with http.rs deleted. Behavior-neutral for what the coordinator consumes. This async base is the prerequisite for the node channel (V0-8a) and every timer-driven milestone after it (V0-8b Hold-expiry combine, V0-4 duress T).

## Why this exists
The hand-rolled synchronous HTTP server (crates/vault-node/src/http.rs) is one sequential serve loop: a stalled client head-of-line-blocks /sign for up to 10s, and it cannot host the peer-facing /channel route or async timers. Migrating while the surface is two routes is far cheaper than after V0-8a/V0-8b/V0-4 pile onto the sync shape (2026-07-16 eng review).

## Verification (ship gate)
nix develop -c cargo fmt --check; clippy -D warnings; cargo test --workspace; demo first-light exits 0. http.rs no longer exists. The new HTTP-level regression tests lock the axum edge contract, and the sign-path atomicity + no-cancel tests prove the concurrency model.

## Deployment context (ADR-0007)
The whole node runs from tmpfs/ramdisk: reboot = bare machine = permanent node death. "State on disk" never means durable; nothing this task writes needs to survive a reboot.

---
FULL TASK SPEC (self-contained executable memory; the rb-lite task file this was transferred from is gitignored):

# V0-8a0: migrate vault-node to tokio + axum — behavior-neutral where it counts, http.rs deleted

## Environment — read first
- No system C compiler. Run EVERY cargo/bitcoind command through the flake dev
  shell: `nix develop -c cargo test`, etc. Plain `cargo` fails.
- This is a **mechanical migration**. It exists so the next task (V0-8a, the
  node channel) lands on an async base as a small, security-only diff.
  Decision record (2026-07-16 eng review): the node goes **fully async**
  (tokio + axum), all surfaces on **one port**, because V0-8a adds a
  peer-facing route and V0-8b/V0-4 add timers (Hold-expiry, duress T).
  Deployment context (ADR-0007, informs no code here but explains the state
  model): the whole node runs from **tmpfs/ramdisk** — reboot = bare machine
  = node death. So "state on disk" never means durable; nothing this task
  writes needs to survive a reboot.

## Problem description
`crates/vault-node/src/http.rs` is a hand-rolled synchronous HTTP/1.1 server —
one sequential serve loop, one request at a time. It was right when `/sign` was
the only route; it is wrong as the base for the channel (head-of-line blocking:
a stalled client holds the loop up to 10s) and for the timer-driven milestones
after it. Replace it with axum on tokio.

**Compatibility contract (be precise about what "behavior-neutral" means):**
- **Byte-compatible** for what the coordinator consumes: `POST /sign` → 200
  with the exact signed/pending/refusal JSON; 400 with `{"error": detail}` on
  an undecodable body (`BadRequest` stays 400, never a refusal). `GET /events`
  / `/events?since=<cursor>` → same JSON; absent/unparseable `since` reads 0.
- **Edge statuses adopt axum's standard answers** (oversized body may be 413,
  wrong method 405, unknown route 404 with axum's body, query strings routed by
  path). Do NOT replicate the hand-rolled server's quirks — instead the
  regression tests below CAPTURE the new edge contract so it is explicit and
  locked from now on.

## Required changes (`crates/vault-node` + workspace manifests)
1. **Add deps**: `tokio` (rt-multi-thread, macros, time, net) and `axum` to
   vault-node. Workspace-pin versions; `Cargo.lock` changes accordingly.
   Nothing else — no tower-http, no tracing stack, no reqwest (V0-8a adds it).
2. **Port routes to axum** per the compatibility contract above. Body limit
   stays 1 MiB (`DefaultBodyLimit`). Add a request-timeout layer for handler
   execution. A client that stalls mid-headers no longer wedges anything (each
   connection is its own task — that is the point of the migration); a
   socket-level header-read deadline is v1 hardening, NOT this task.
3. **Sign-path atomicity (critical).** Today the sequential serve loop gives
   `handle_sign` end-to-end atomicity for free: its check-then-update sequences
   over the replay and pending logs (`replay_log`, `pending_log` at
   lib.rs:134-138) never interleave. Under axum, requests are concurrent.
   Preserve the CURRENT semantics: **wrap the replay log AND the pending log
   together in ONE `Mutex<SignState>`** (a small struct holding both), held
   across the WHOLE `handle_sign` call. **This narrow restructuring IS
   authorized and required** (codex audit 2026-07-16): `Node`'s two `RefCell`s
   make it non-`Sync`, so axum cannot share it as state without this change —
   "do not restructure Node" (below) means do not reorganize its OTHER fields
   or split policy state, NOT "leave the two logs as un-shareable RefCells."
   **Two separate log mutexes remain FORBIDDEN** (interleaved check/update
   between two concurrent identical requests would corrupt replay semantics —
   the two logs must move under one lock). `/events` state, the alert queue,
   and watchtower state stay independently accessible (their own
   `Arc<Mutex<..>>` as today), so `/events` never waits behind `/sign`.
   Document at the lock: **`/sign` is serialized BY DESIGN** — concurrency buys
   ISOLATION of `/sign` from `/events`/`/channel`, NOT sign-vs-sign throughput;
   two `/sign` requests still run one-at-a-time and that is correct. Run the (synchronous,
   CPU-bearing) `handle_sign` body inside `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` so
   descriptor scans/secp work never stall the runtime. **An accepted sign job
   must NOT be cancelled by a handler timeout** — a half-run sign that mutated
   the replay/pending log then got dropped is a ghost side effect; let accepted
   `/sign` work run to completion (the handler timeout guards connection
   liveness, not the committed sign job). Concretely: wrap the `spawn_blocking`
   JoinHandle in `tokio::time::timeout`; on timeout, drop the response future
   (the client gets a timeout status) but let the blocking task finish and
   commit its verdict. Recovery is by idempotent resubmission — the anti-replay
   log returns the recorded verdict for an identical commitment (DESIGN.md
   "anti-replay log" §, job (1) idempotency).
4. **Delete `http.rs`** — do not keep two HTTP stacks. Its `parse_since` unit
   test moves/adapts to wherever cursor parsing now lives.
5. **`main.rs`** becomes `#[tokio::main]`; serve the one axum app on
   `listen_port`.
6. **Watchtower driver**: `Node::spawn_watchtower`'s interval thread becomes a
   tokio interval task whose tick body runs via `spawn_blocking` (the tick
   calls blocking bitcoind JSON-RPC in `chain.rs`; a slow RPC must never stall
   the async runtime). `chain.rs` itself does NOT need an async rewrite.
7. **`Node` stays as it is** otherwise — apart from the authorized
   `Mutex<SignState>` change in step 3, do not reorganize its other fields,
   split policy state, or make policy code async.

## Tests (`vault-node`)
- All existing unit tests pass unchanged (policy, handle_sign, watchtower,
  replay) — except `http.rs`'s `parse_since` test, which moves with the code.
- **HTTP-level regression tests (NEW — the point of this task):** over a real
  loopback socket against the axum app:
  - `POST /sign` valid body → 200, exact response JSON shape.
  - `POST /sign` garbage → 400 `{"error": ...}`.
  - Oversized body (> 1 MiB) → rejected with the axum-standard status —
    assert the status you get and lock it as the contract; never 500 or hang.
  - `GET /events?since=42` and bare `/events` → cursor semantics unchanged.
  - Unknown route → 404; wrong method → assert-and-lock the axum answer.
- **Concurrency regression:** two identical `/sign` requests submitted
  concurrently → exactly one fresh acceptance path runs; replay/pending logs
  end consistent (no interleaving corruption). (`/sign` serializes against
  `/sign` by design — do NOT assert two signs overlap.)
- **Isolation (test each cause SEPARATELY, not as an "or" — codex audit):**
  (i) a slow/blocking `/sign` in flight → `GET /events` still responds
  promptly; (ii) a watchtower tick against a slow chain backend → `/events`
  still responds promptly; (iii) a **stalled client holding incomplete request
  headers open** → a separate `/events` request succeeds promptly (proves the
  per-connection-task model removed head-of-line blocking). This is what the
  async migration buys; it is NOT sign-vs-sign parallelism. (`/channel` gets
  the same isolation guarantee in V0-8a, where it exists.)
- **No-cancel sign job:** a `/sign` that exceeds the handler timeout returns a
  timeout status to the client, BUT the accepted job completes and commits its
  verdict (replay/pending logs consistent), and an identical resubmission
  returns the recorded verdict — no ghost half-run, no lost sign. (Assert all
  three: client sees timeout, log mutated once, resubmit is idempotent.)
- `nix develop -c cargo run -p vault-cli -- demo first-light` exits 0.

## Scope guard
- Touch `crates/vault-node/`, the workspace `Cargo.toml`, and `Cargo.lock`
  only. Do NOT add any channel/peer code (V0-8a), do NOT touch the
  coordinator, policy-core, vault-proto, or the demo. Do NOT change any
  request/response JSON schema.
- Target ≤ 700 lines net including the new tests. If materially more, stop
  and simplify.
- Do not run `rb-lite`, signal your own process tree, or touch `.rb-lite/`,
  `.ralph-burning/`, `.git/ralph-burning-live/`.

## Acceptance criteria
- `nix develop -c cargo fmt --check`, `nix develop -c cargo clippy --workspace
  --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `nix develop -c cargo test --workspace` pass.
- `http.rs` no longer exists; the node serves `/sign` + `/events` via axum
  meeting the compatibility contract, proven by the HTTP-level regression
  tests, including the sign-path atomicity test.
- `demo first-light` exits 0.


---
## Polish notes (bead-polish-loop 2026-07-16)
- **This bead unblocks btc-policy-byf (the node channel) and MUST merge first.** It is a behavior-neutral migration — reviewers should confirm no observable /sign or /events behavior changed except the deliberately-locked axum edge statuses (413/405/404 bodies).
- **Authoritative design source (committed):** the "fully async, one port" decision is docs/DESIGN.md + the 2026-07-16 eng review; tmpfs reboot-death is docs/adr/0007-node-death-on-reboot.md. No ADR schema changes in this task.

title: Latched-repair state pays a full scantxoutset every 10s pass (hn8 follow-up)
description: Fable hn8 review [P3], independent finding. Compound-failure state: a reorg below the wallet's completion anchor sets the repair latch AND the re-import keeps failing (read-only wallet dir, wallet support removed mid-flight). Each 10s SCAN_INTERVAL pass then takes the cold branch, because 'repair_pending && !repair_in_progress' refuses the delta base (crates/vault-node/src/chain.rs ~1506-1513), so EVERY pass pays a full scantxoutset (~10.4s on signet, serialized process-wide across every node sharing the bitcoind) purely to re-derive a birthday for a repair that keeps failing. Pre-hn8 this corner delta-advanced after a single scan, so it is a regression in that specific state. AVAILABILITY ONLY — verdicts stay correct, the cache stays complete — but it degrades exactly the property this bead was for, under a failure the operator may not notice (see the sibling /healthz surfacing bead). FIX SHAPE: let a still-anchored scan-derived cache serve as the delta base while latched, re-scanning only once per repair ATTEMPT rather than once per pass — the latch protects the WALLET, not the cache, and an active-anchored cold cache is safe to delta-advance. Gates: fmt/clippy-D/workspace tests incl. the scripted-RPC chain suite, attack 16/16, all 3 demos.

title: V0-4b (core): two-track duress state machine
description:
## V0-4b (CORE): two-track duress state machine. Folded audit r2 (armed combine window is T-based not commitment-expiry-capped — resolves the empty-window sweep failure). Depends on V0-8b + V0-4a + V0-10.

FULL TASK SPEC (self-contained; source task file gitignored):

# V0-4b (core): two-track duress state machine

## Environment — read first
- No system C compiler. Run cargo/bitcoind via `nix develop -c ...`.
- **Prerequisites merged:** V0-8b (node combine+broadcast with **release-at-fire**
  partial gate, **paired spend+escape candidates** registered + signed at ingress,
  the **coordinator-authenticated `request` channel carrier** that propagates a
  request to all peers, the ChainBackend package-acceptance + authorized-set),
  V0-4a (dual-pin both-Argon2 constant-time compare, per-node attempt budget with
  the arm-even-when-locked-out hook, Lockdown + FRAUD_SUSPECTED), **V0-10**
  (recovery-path branch + recovery spend — so "funds frozen → recovery" is a
  demonstrable exit).
- **AUTHORITATIVE, READ IN FULL: `docs/adr/0012-...` "Duress state machine (per
  node) — normative"** (two-track model, transition table, 8 invariants, V0-4
  implementation-semantics checklist) + the escape-admissibility paragraphs
  ("Nodes validate the escape…", "Build over the mempool UTXO set…",
  "Class-aware escape coverage…"). Also ADR-0013 §3 (class), §6 (coverage,
  feerate, epsilon, duress_delay_secs, refresh bounds), `CONTEXT.md`.
- The **adversarial regtest/CLI harness is a SEPARATE dependent bead**
  (V0-4b-harness); this bead is the production state machine + its unit/model
  tests only.

## Outcome
A valid, coordinator-authenticated **duress-pin** request **unconditionally**
freezes hot-class finalization and schedules **Lockdown at T** (the SAFETY track,
keyed on the pin ALONE — chain-view-independent), while a **best-effort Firing
sweep** of the user-signed escape is attempted at T (the SWEEP track, gated by
the full admissibility predicate at FIRE-TIME only). Sweep failure = funds frozen
→ recovery (V0-10), never theft. Silent to an outside attacker.

## Required changes (`crates/vault-node`)

### 1. Which transition rows this bead owns
V0-8b already implements the NORMAL rows (`Idle + normal SpendRequest`,
`Idle + RefreshRequest`, `Scheduled + fire-time`) via sign-at-ingress +
release-at-fire. This bead adds the DURESS rows of the ADR-0012 table and MUST
NOT weaken the normal rows or invariant 7 (release-at-fire). Implement verbatim:
`Idle + duress` → Armed; `Scheduled + valid duress (coord OR peer)` → suppress
the scheduled spend then Arm; `Armed + peer duress` → arm idempotently;
`Armed/Scheduled + hot spend while Armed` → refuse finalize, `T ← min(T, its
Hold-expiry − ε)`; `Armed + clock reaches T` → **Lockdown UNCONDITIONALLY** +
spawn Firing job; `Firing` (orthogonal); `Lockdown + request` → FRAUD_SUSPECTED;
`Lockdown + peer sweep-combine` → accepted; `Armed + reboot` → node death.

### 2. Initial T computation (codex D4 — SECURITY, was omitted)
`T = min(first_seen_duress + duress_delay_secs, earliest_pending_hot_fire − ε)`.
- Recompute (shrink only) when a new hot spend is accepted while Armed.
- **Bounded ε** validation (a small margin; reject absurd ε).
- **Past/matured case:** if the computed T is already past (or a pending hot
  spend's public Hold-expiry precedes T), **fire immediately**. Rationale: a
  previously-pending hot spend must NOT settle at its publicly-expected
  Hold-expiry AFTER a later T — that visible non-settlement during the hostage
  window would reveal duress. State the formula, recomputation rule, ε bound,
  and past-means-fire-now semantics explicitly.

### 3. Constant-observable ingress — fully closed (codex D7, silence)
Every request (normal OR duress) does the identical observable work; the pin
(V0-4a compare) flips only an internal fire bit. Explicitly:
- **Both pins propagate the same coordinator-signed request** to peers (V0-8b's
  `request` carrier) — identical peer-fanout **count, order, payload size, and
  retry policy**.
- **Neither candidate's partial is transmitted until its fire** (invariant 7 —
  spend AND escape).
- Identical **HTTP status / body / length / release deadline** for a valid normal
  vs a valid duress request; **peer failures cannot alter the pin-dependent
  response path** (the response does not wait on, or vary with, peer-fanout
  outcomes).
- The same-shaped **two-slot schedule record** (immediate + delayed slot) is
  written to RAMDISK on both pins (escape-class delayed slot is a no-op under
  normal; a residual sweep under duress). One atomic RAMDISK write; never durable
  disk (a durable "duress detected" record is forbidden, ADR-0008).
- **Response cover:** `pending`/`first_seen`/remaining-Hold reported identically
  under both pins; never expose Armed-vs-Scheduled or the real fire-time before T.

### 4. The 8 invariants (ADR-0012) — implement, do NOT weaken
(i) Lockdown at T unconditional (never waits for escape confirmation — EVERY
fire-failure branch still Locks Down at T); (ii) arming/lockdown
chain-view-independent (pin alone); (iii) reboot-death (RAMDISK, nothing
persists); (iv) pin-compare constant-cost (V0-4a); (v) fail-closed lockout (valid
duress arms regardless of lockout, via V0-4a's hook); (vi) idempotency before
cache (process the pin/safety signal BEFORE any cached commitment verdict, so a
duress resubmission with a fresh nonce of a previously-normal-pending commitment
still arms); (vii) partial-release authorization (arming atomically + monotonically
suppresses every existing/future hot-partial release — installed timers + cached
commitments — for BOTH candidates); (viii) escape-class two-slot record.

### 5. Full escape-admissibility predicate (codex D6 — FIRE-TIME only, never arm gates)
At the Firing job (T), the sweep fires only if armed-set has **t distinct valid
escape signers per input** AND the escape is admissible. The FULL predicate
(ADR-0012 — not just three labels):
- **coverage** ≥ threshold (e.g. 95%), **class-aware** (ADR-0012 "Class-aware
  escape coverage"): hot-class spend frozen → escape supersedes it, coverage over
  confirmed + vault-authorized-unconfirmed; escape-class spend completes → escape
  inputs **disjoint** from the completed spend, coverage over their **union**;
- **feerate** ≥ panic floor;
- **final `nLockTime`** + **non-relative-locking `nSequence`** (`0xffffffff` —
  also makes E non-RBF-signaling so the fixed-panic-fee rebroadcast loop is sound);
- **every input confirmed OR a vault-authorized-unconfirmed parent** (own
  spend-change/refresh — never an external unconfirmed deposit; toxic-deposit
  safe);
- **full package `testmempoolaccept`** (E + its unconfirmed vault-authorized
  ancestors), not merely relay-standard.
Each admissibility FAILURE → the sweep does not fire; **Lockdown at T still
happens unconditionally** → funds frozen → recovery. NEVER an arm gate.

### 6. Refresh rules under duress (codex D5)
- **Any pending spend blocks all refreshes** (already V0-8b subordination) — do
  not let a disjoint refresh invalidate escape inputs during `[arm, T]`.
- The **escape-class exception** per ADR-0012 (escape-class completes; residual
  sweep over the union).
- **No pin-dependent cancellation:** there is NO operation whose presence/timing
  depends on the pin that could become a duress oracle. Any cancel/supersede is
  identical under both pins.

### 7. Candidate-registry duress obligations (deferred from V0-8a D13)
- **Armed-candidate expiry exemption + fire-complete cleanup:** an armed/
  scheduled-to-fire candidate is EXEMPT from the commitment-expiry sweep AND the
  `/channel`-lookup expiry rejection until its fire completes (escape-class T =
  `first_seen + duress_delay_secs` can exceed `max_commitment_age_secs`); finite
  lifecycle (cleared on fire-complete) so it cannot pin the capacity cap.
- **Armed combine window is T-based, NOT commitment-expiry-capped (codex fix
  2026-07-17 — resolves the empty-window contradiction):** V0-8b caps a NORMAL
  candidate's combine window at `min(commitment_expiry, fire_time +
  combine_slack_secs)`. But a duress escape's `T` can land AFTER
  `commitment_expiry`, which would make that window EMPTY — no partial could be
  released or collected and every such sweep would deterministically fail. For an
  **armed/escape candidate the combine window is `[T, T + combine_slack_secs]`**
  (the commitment-expiry cap does NOT apply — the candidate is already exempt
  from expiry pruning, so its combine window must be too). Partials for the armed
  escape are released at T and collected within this T-based window. State this
  as the reconciliation of the armed-expiry-exemption with V0-8b's normal-window
  cap.
- **Capacity gate AFTER pin/safety:** the candidate-store capacity check runs
  AFTER arm/freeze so a duress request is never dropped for fullness.
- **Firing job bound (codex nit):** define when the never-confirming
  rebroadcast job ends / how it stays resource-bounded while the node is locked
  down (e.g. bounded retries / until commitment-relevant horizon).

## Tests (unit/model — the V0-4 checklist; broad regtest lives in V0-4b-harness)
- **Atomic monotonic Armed overlay** (barrier-controlled REPEATED races, not one
  scheduler-dependent race): pending hot spend + duress arm racing its
  Hold-expiry → the pre-pending partial never slips out.
- **Both-Argon2 + constant-time-select** (structural, from V0-4a): normal/duress/
  wrong indistinguishable in Argon2 count + budget touch.
- **Fail-closed lockout**: lock out C/D/E on wrong pins, then the real duress
  request still arms.
- **Idempotency ordering**: normal-pending commitment resubmitted with the duress
  pin + fresh nonce → arms.
- **Partial-release**: no partial (spend OR escape) leaves before its fire; a
  compromised peer soliciting at ingress gets none.
- **Response cover**: direct response byte/status/length comparison + `/events`
  comparison under both pins → identical until T; peer-message trace + fanout
  count/order/size identical; timer/lock/write instrumentation identical.
- **Initial T**: pre-pending, matured-pending (fire-now), and a nearer post-arm
  hot spend (shrink T).
- **Unconditional Lockdown**: assert Lockdown at T for sweep-success, `< t`,
  coverage-fail, feerate-fail, package-fail, broadcast-fail, and
  never-confirming broadcast — every branch.
- **Lockdown behavior**: accepts in-flight sweep-combine partials while rejecting
  ALL new signing (FRAUD_SUSPECTED).
- **Candidate exemption**: armed candidate exempt at BOTH prune paths (sweep +
  `/channel` lookup); cleaned up after fire; capacity released.
- **Escape-class**: normal delayed-slot no-op vs duress residual sweep (disjoint
  inputs, union coverage).
- **Reboot-death**: DEPLOYMENT death (delete the simulated tmpfs deployment) —
  arm t+1, kill one before T → sweep still fires; drop below t → lockdown-only
  (no sweep, no theft); the killed node cannot restart/rejoin.
- **Arm-split closed**: no unarmed sub-quorum can complete a coerced hot spend
  after any node received the valid duress request (via request propagation).

## Scope guard
- Touch `crates/vault-node/` only. CONSUME V0-8b (channel, carrier, candidates,
  broadcast), V0-4a (pin, budget, Lockdown), V0-10 (recovery). Do NOT rework the
  channel wire, the combine/broadcast plumbing, or the pin substrate. Do NOT
  build the broad adversarial regtest/CLI harness (that is V0-4b-harness). Do NOT
  add device-bound duress tokens, dynamic policy, or duress_response toggles
  (rejected). RAMDISK only — no durable duress signal.
- Build the two-track machine EXACTLY per ADR-0012; do not invent behavior the
  ADR doesn't specify or weaken any invariant to satisfy a reviewer. Size
  advisory; never compress invariants, transition rows, or checklist tests.
- Do not run `rb-lite`, signal your own process tree, or touch `.rb-lite/`,
  `.ralph-burning/`, `.git/ralph-burning-live/`, `.beads/`.

## Acceptance criteria
- fmt/clippy -D warnings/test --workspace pass; `demo first-light` exits 0.
- Every duress transition row + all 8 invariants + the full fire-time
  admissibility predicate + initial-T semantics + constant-observable-ingress
  closure implemented; the V0-4 implementation-semantics checklist unit/model
  tests pass. The two-track machine is live; the broad adversarial demonstration
  is V0-4b-harness.
close_reason: V0-4b duress arming merged to main (abbfe75). Theft-safe for coerced-with-duress-pin spends via the release-gate + signer/partial coupling (dual-model reviewed: codex+Fable). Pending-spend-censorship residual bounded by the Hot budget (V0-11 btc-policy-0fa, ADR-0014). 297 vault-node + 65 sign tests, first-light + recovery-drill exit 0.

title: Surface wallet-fallback state on /healthz (hn8 follow-up)
description:
Fable hn8 review [P3], re-check item 5 — STILL OPEN after 6 rb-lite rounds, downgraded from P2. A bitcoind without usable wallet RPC (-disablewallet, unwritable wallet dir, wallet support absent) silently pins the node to the scantxoutset fallback FOREVER. The fallback is complete, correct, and verdict-identical — so this is not a safety issue — but it silently forfeits the entire readiness/latency win btc-policy-hn8 exists for (measured: ~10.4s per scan on signet's 72.2M-output set, serialized process-wide across all five nodes), and the only signal today is two eprintln lines in the node's own log. FIX: a pin-independent boolean on /healthz (e.g. vault_wallet_serving) fed from existing state; full_scan_count() already exists as the natural hook. SILENCE-SAFE: the refresher never reads pin/duress/arm state, so the field cannot vary by pin class — but the /healthz field set is a SILENCE surface, so the byte-identity tests (healthz_is_byte_identical_on_an_armed_pre_t_node) must be extended to cover it, and the field must be identical on armed and idle twins. Consider also a startup capability probe in verify_required_indexes (chain.rs ~666) so a misconfigured backend is loud at boot rather than silently slow forever.

PRIORITY NOTE (bead-polish 2026-07-30): the header above still reads '[P3] ... downgraded from P2' from when this was filed. The bead IS P2 and that is correct -- it now blocks btc-policy-s12, the stage whose entire purpose is operational measurement, and a node silently pinned to the scantxoutset fallback forever would corrupt exactly the attrition and latency numbers stage 4 exists to collect. Read the P3 in the first line as history, not as the current priority.

title: Hardware-signing path for the user key (PSBT hand-off)
description:
FROM THE 2026-07-29 STATE REVIEW (Fable #2). docs/DESIGN.md premise 1 is 'a user hardware key AND a t-of-n quorum', and threat rows A2/A3 turn on the user key being stealable-but-not-sufficient. In code the user key is SOFTWARE in every driver (Actor::random / in-process secp keys), and there is no cyberkrill, HWI, or PSBT hand-off anywhere in the tree.

WHY IT MATTERS (priority P2 as of 2026-07-29 — deferred past the capped mainnet rungs per ADR-0015, gating the stage-9 freeze btc-policy-yt7 instead; the dust cap carries this risk until then): on a real deployment the software user key would live on the coordinator host — the one machine ADR-0012 already names as the SEVERE residual (a pre-wrench coordinator compromise reads the normal PIN and substitutes it, silently nullifying duress). A software user key on that same host MERGES adversary A3 with that residual: the attacker skips the wrench entirely for the hot-bounded portion. The design's core premise is currently false in code.

DELIVER: a PSBT hand-off seam — the coordinator composes the spend and its mandatory escape, exports PSBTs, a hardware device DISPLAYS and signs them, and the signed PSBTs come back. Reuse the user's own tooling where it fits (cyberkrill / HWI) rather than adding a dependency; see the standing rule in docs/SBOM-AND-DEPENDENCY-POLICY.md.

CARE — the display is the security boundary: the device must show the user what they are actually authorizing (destination, amount, and that a mandatory escape is co-signed), or the hand-off adds ceremony without adding safety. A device that blind-signs a PSBT the coordinator composed defends nothing against a compromised coordinator, which is the entire point.

NON-GOALS: choosing a specific vendor; multisig-on-device UX; changing the descriptor.

VERIFY: an honest spend completes with the user key never present in the coordinator process; a test or documented drill showing what the device displays for a spend AND for its escape.

Dependents:
  <- btc-policy-yt7 (blocks) - Rollout stage 9 freeze: full Path suite on the real configuration, then external review #2


VALIDITY NOTE, RESCOPED 2026-07-30 (owner decision: hardware signing is optional and postponed). This note used to say bq6 'must be EXERCISED ON A SIGNET RUNG (stage 6 or 7) before the stage-9 freeze' -- a MUST that conflicted with ADR-0015 lines 86-95, which deliberately do not require hardware signing for the capped rungs 3-8. It is now a RECOMMENDATION, not a gate: exercising bq6 on a signet rung is preferable if it happens to be ready, and this bead blocks only btc-policy-yt7 (the stage-9 freeze). If hardware signing first runs at stage 9, the PSBT hand-off, the device-display trust boundary and the escape co-sign path all debut at the freeze rung, and stage 8's mainnet soak will have exercised a spend path that stage 9 then replaces.

title: V0-8a: node-to-node channel (signed envelopes + verified partial exchange)
description:
## Outcome
vault-node gains an authenticated node-to-node channel: per-message signed envelopes (no session) over POST /channel on the existing axum app, plus a verified partial-signature exchange primitive backed by a candidate registry populated by the real /sign path. These are the primitives V0-8b drives to combine + broadcast; this task builds ONLY the channel layer.

## Why this exists
Under Model B the coordinator is a pure relay: nodes assemble the t-of-n signature among themselves and broadcast. That requires an authenticated channel that carries signatures and assembly only — never policy — and a way for a node to verify a peer's partial against its OWN recomputed sighash (never blind-merge a peer PSBT). ADR-0012 "The node-to-node channel" + ADR-0013 §4 (manifest) are authoritative.

## Critical security properties (must all hold)
- Channel identity endorsed by the node's Bitcoin signing key, verified against the immutable manifest — the coordinator cannot mint/impersonate a node.
- Per-message possession proof (envelope signature over a fresh nonce+timestamp) — no session handshake.
- recipient_node_id binds each envelope to its receiver — closes cross-recipient replay for THIS and every future msg_type.
- Signature covers the RAW payload_b64 field (verify BEFORE decode) — identity before payload parsing.
- Partials verified against the expected descriptor pubkey over the node's OWN registered sighash — never blind-merge.
- Signing-oracle prohibition: structurally no channel message can cause the node to sign.

## Non-goals / scope guard
Touch crates/vault-node/, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock ONLY. The ONLY /sign-path change is the register_candidate post-verdict funnel. Do NOT build combine/broadcast (V0-8b), duress state machine (V0-4), Tor/mTLS (v1), full manifest provisioning (V0-9), or any session/connection state. Target ~1200-1600 lines incl tests.

## Verification (ship gate)
fmt/clippy -D warnings/test --workspace green; demo first-light exits 0; the two-in-process-nodes E2E exchanges one verified partial THROUGH the real /sign→/channel path (no test-only candidate injection).

## Deployment context (ADR-0007)
tmpfs/ramdisk: reboot = bare machine = permanent node death; a dead node never rejoins the immutable manifest (restore capacity = rotate to a successor vault). No channel state persists.

---
FULL TASK SPEC (self-contained executable memory; the rb-lite task file this was transferred from is gitignored):

# V0-8a: node-to-node channel — identity, signed envelopes, partial-signature exchange

## Environment — read first
- No system C compiler. Run EVERY cargo/bitcoind command through the flake dev
  shell: `nix develop -c cargo test`, etc. Plain `cargo` fails.
- **Prerequisite: V0-8a0 (axum migration) is merged.** The node is async
  (tokio + axum, one port, `http.rs` deleted, sign-path Mutex +
  spawn_blocking). Build the channel as routes and tasks on that base. All new
  code is async.
- Read `docs/adr/0012-model-b-spend-and-duress-architecture.md` (**"The
  node-to-node channel"** section — the authoritative security properties) and
  `docs/adr/0013-concrete-protocol-schemas.md` (§4 manifest — the
  channel-identity root). Also `CONTEXT.md` ("Node channel", "Manifest").
- This is the **channel layer only**. It does NOT rework the spend path or the
  coordinator (that is V0-8b). It provides the primitives V0-8b will drive:
  authenticated peer messaging + a verified partial-signature exchange.

## Problem description
Under Model B, nodes assemble the t-of-n signature among themselves and
broadcast (the coordinator is a pure relay). This task builds the
**authenticated peer messaging** those nodes use, and the **partial-signature
exchange** primitive — but NOT the combine/broadcast wiring or the spend-path
rework (V0-8b). The channel carries signatures and assembly only, **never
policy**.

Design decisions locked by the 2026-07-16 eng review (do not re-litigate):
- **No session handshake.** Every peer message is a self-authenticating
  **signed envelope** (possession is proven per message — the fresh
  nonce+timestamp IS the challenge). This satisfies ADR-0012's
  challenge-response/possession requirement with no connection state machine.
- **Same port.** Channel messages are a route (`POST /channel`) on the node's
  one axum app. Axum's concurrency removes the head-of-line-blocking that
  motivated a separate port; layered DoS guards handle peer spam.
  **Principle (2026-07-16): no endpoint on a node derives ANY authority from
  network reachability — all authority is cryptographic, rooted in the
  manifest.** The coordinator can reach `/channel` and peers can reach
  `/sign`; both gain nothing (envelopes need an endorsed channel key; sign
  requests need user/coordinator signatures). Firewalls are hygiene, never a
  trust boundary.
- **Node-local types.** The envelope types live in `vault-node` — the
  coordinator never parses channel messages (V0-8b is also node-side).
- **Reboot survival is a NON-goal.** The whole node runs from **tmpfs/ramdisk**
  (ADR-0007): reboot = bare machine = **permanent node death** (a dead node
  never rejoins the immutable manifest; restoring capacity means rotating to a
  successor vault, not resurrecting the node). No channel state (nonce cache,
  partial store, candidates) needs to persist.
  Derivation determinism (below) exists so the setup-time endorsement matches
  the runtime key — not to survive reboots.
- **Outbound HTTP client = `reqwest`** (user decision 2026-07-16): V0-8b/V0-4
  and v1 (SOCKS/Tor) reuse it.

## Required changes (`crates/vault-node` + workspace manifests)

### 1. Channel identity (ADR-0012)
Each node has a **RAM-only channel keypair**, derived **deterministically**
from the node's key material:
`channel_seckey = tagged_hash("btc-policy/channel-key/v0", node_seckey)`
interpreted as a big-endian scalar. **Retry algorithm (codex audit — make it
deterministic):** if the 32-byte digest is zero or ≥ the secp256k1 curve order,
re-hash `tagged_hash("btc-policy/channel-key/v0", node_seckey || counter)` with
a u8 `counter` starting at 0 and incrementing until the result is a valid
scalar (probability of even one retry is ~2^-128; the loop is for total
determinism, not practical reach). Write the tag string once as a const. Never persisted; derived
at startup. Deterministic so the setup-time endorsement and the runtime key
always agree; must differ from the signing key. (V0-9 swaps the seed input to
wskdf without changing the shape.)

The channel pubkey is **endorsed by the node's Bitcoin signing key** over a
domain-separated structure `(wallet_id, manifest_hash, node_id,
channel_pubkey, protocol_version, transport_endpoints)`. A node accepts a
peer's channel identity **only** if the endorsement verifies against a signing
pubkey bound to that `node_id` in the (immutable) manifest for this vault.
The coordinator cannot mint or impersonate a node.

### 2. Manifest + config (minimal but real — full provisioning is V0-9)
**The `[channel]` config block is OPTIONAL (codex audit 2026-07-16 — resolves
the demo contradiction).** Absent ⇒ **absent-channel mode**: the `/channel`
route is NOT mounted, NO manifest/bijection/endorsement invariants run, and the
node behaves exactly as today. This is what lets `demo first-light` (which does
not use the channel) keep passing **without editing the demo** — the demo omits
`[channel]`. Present ⇒ every invariant below applies and `/channel` is mounted.
- The `[channel]` block carries: `node_id` (this node's id) and `nodes` — the
  FULL membership list of all `n` entries **including this node itself**, each
  `{ node_id, endpoints, signing_pubkey, channel_pubkey, channel_endorsement }`.
  (`nodes`, not `peers`, and self is included — the manifest hash needs all `n`;
  self-inclusion removes the "does peers contain me?" ambiguity.) **`endpoints`
  is PLURAL** — a `Vec` of endpoint strings (a node may advertise clearnet +
  onion), matching the endorsement/manifest `transport_endpoints` byte-for-byte
  (codex audit 2026-07-16: there is no singular `endpoint` anywhere; the config,
  the hashed manifest, and the endorsement domain all use the same plural list).
  **`channel_pubkey` is REQUIRED** on every entry. At startup assert the
  `node_id`s form an **exact `0..n-1` bijection** with the descriptor's
  canonical node keys (§1 ordering); a gap, dup, or out-of-range id is fatal.
- **Endpoint consistency (codex I4):** assert this node's own entry's
  `endpoints` includes the address the daemon actually binds `/channel` on, and
  that every node's `endpoints` are canonical and parseable — a manifest
  endorsing one self endpoint set while the daemon binds another silently drops
  the node from the combine set. Fatal config error on mismatch.
- **Resource-limit config (all in `[channel]`, units + CONCRETE defaults —
  ADR-0013 §5):** `max_active_candidates` (count, default **1024**),
  `max_candidate_store_bytes` (bytes, default **67_108_864 = 64 MiB**; byte
  accounting = stored PSBT + sighashes + partials per candidate),
  `per_peer_quota_per_min` (envelopes/min/peer, default **600**),
  `max_concurrent_channel_requests` (pre-auth global bound, default **64**),
  `max_msg_bytes` (default **1_048_576 = 1 MiB**), `max_response_bytes`
  (outbound read bound, default **65_536**), `per_send_deadline_secs` (default
  **5**). Every field has a default so a minimal `[channel]` block is valid.
- **Two-pass construction (no hash cycle):** the canonical manifest is the
  endorsement-FREE structure
  `(wallet_id, nodes[node_id, signing_pubkey, channel_pubkey,
  transport_endpoints] ordered by node_id, protocol_version)` —
  **`channel_pubkey` IS in the hashed structure** (deterministic, so known at
  setup before endorsements; the manifest exists to pin channel identity).
  `manifest_hash` = tagged SHA-256 over its canonical serialization;
  endorsements are computed OVER that hash and distributed alongside, never
  inside it (ADR-0013 §4). **This v0 `manifest_hash` is PROVISIONAL:** V0-9
  defines the final canonical serialization of the full §4 struct (adding
  vault_descriptor, coordinator_auth_pubkey, t/n, allowlist,
  escape_descriptor) and all endorsements re-derive then — no
  hash continuity is promised before the provisioning ceremony.
- **Startup invariants (assert, fail to start otherwise):** this node's own
  signing pubkey is one of the descriptor's node keys; every manifest signing
  pubkey is one of the descriptor's node keys; `node_id` ↔ descriptor-key
  mapping is total and unambiguous (this mapping is also what "expected
  descriptor pubkey for signer X" below means). **Additionally (codex audit
  2026-07-16):** the node's LOCALLY-derived channel pubkey must equal its own
  `nodes[self]` `channel_pubkey` entry (a valid-but-mismatched self entry
  otherwise makes the node permanently unreachable — its peers verify against a
  key it never signs with); and when a config carries an `expected_manifest_hash`,
  the computed provisional `manifest_hash` must equal it (ADR-0013 trust-root
  posture — the node is sealed to a specific manifest).

### 3. Signed envelopes = peer authentication (the wire contract — exact)

**Domain-separation tags (all tagged SHA-256; fixed consts, codex audit
2026-07-16 — every digest in the system MUST name its tag so independent
derivations agree):**
- channel-key derivation: `"btc-policy/channel-key/v0"`
- manifest hash: `"btc-policy/manifest/v0"` (over the §2 BaseManifest canonical
  bytes)
- channel-key endorsement: `"btc-policy/channel-endorsement/v0"` (over the
  §1 domain-separated structure)
- envelope signature preimage: `"btc-policy/channel-envelope/v0"`
- `user_sig_hash`: `"btc-policy/user-sig-hash/v0"`
**Byte conventions (fixed):** all pubkeys 33-byte compressed (raw in preimages,
hex only in JSON); all hashes 32-byte raw in preimages, lowercase hex in JSON;
`nonce` 16 random bytes (hex in JSON, raw in preimage). **Length-prefix rule
(codex audit 2026-07-16):** ONLY variable-length fields (`payload_b64` bytes,
`endpoints` strings, script bytes, DER sigs) get a u32-LE length prefix;
**fixed-width numeric fields (timestamp u64, node_id u16, input index u32,
protocol_version u32, version i32, lock_time u32, sequence u32) are written at
their fixed width LE with NO length prefix** (they are self-delimiting). Pick a
width per numeric field and keep it fixed.
**Encoding ownership (v0 — DESIGN "wire format greenfield until v1"):** the
implementer OWNS the exact canonical byte layout of every preimage (per-digest
field order, the fixed numeric widths above, endpoint serialization) and MUST
**document it in a single module-level table in code** so signer and verifier
provably read the same bytes. v0 is single-workspace, so cross-implementation
byte-stability is NOT required until v1; the requirement here is INTERNAL
consistency + regression-locking, not conformance to an external standard.
**Golden vectors (test requirement — strengthened, codex B3 fix 2026-07-16):**
freeze the chosen layout by hard-coding, per digest (channel-key derivation,
manifest hash, endorsement digest, envelope digest, user_sig_hash), BOTH the
**expected canonical preimage bytes** AND the resulting digest — not just the
digest. A vector that only pins the digest, generated from the same
canonicalizer under test, can bless a common-mode omission (e.g. signer AND
verifier both skip `nonce` → an attacker mutates the nonce and replays inside
the timestamp window while round-trip tests still pass). Pinning the preimage
bytes catches that. **Additionally: per-field mutation of the ENVELOPE** — flip
each signed field (`msg_type`, `protocol_version`, `wallet_id`, `manifest_hash`,
`sender_node_id`, `recipient_node_id`, `payload_b64`, **`nonce`, `timestamp`**)
one at a time and assert each mutation invalidates `channel_sig`. Round-trip
tests separately prove signer == verifier.

Every channel message is one JSON envelope:
`{ msg_type, protocol_version, wallet_id, manifest_hash, sender_node_id,
   recipient_node_id, payload_b64, nonce, timestamp, channel_sig }`
- **Crypto:** secp256k1 ECDSA; 33-byte compressed pubkeys; DER signatures
  (consistent with the node's existing signing stack).
- **Signature preimage:** tagged SHA-256 (`"btc-policy/channel-envelope/v0"`)
  over a **canonical length-prefixed byte serialization** of
  `(msg_type, protocol_version, wallet_id, manifest_hash, sender_node_id,
  recipient_node_id, payload_b64_bytes, nonce, timestamp)` — fixed field
  order, applying the **Byte conventions rule below as normative** (codex fix
  2026-07-16, resolving the earlier contradiction): variable-length fields
  (`msg_type`, `payload_b64_bytes`, `nonce`) get a u32-LE length prefix;
  fixed-width numerics (`protocol_version` u32, `sender_node_id`/
  `recipient_node_id` u16, `timestamp` u64) are written at their declared width
  LE with NO prefix; `wallet_id`/`manifest_hash` are fixed 32 raw bytes, no
  prefix. There is NO "u64 for all numeric fields" rule — that wording is
  retracted. One shared canonicalizer produces this; the module table + golden
  vectors record the exact per-field widths. **Sign the
  raw ASCII bytes of the `payload_b64` field, NOT the decoded payload**
  (codex-review fix 2026-07-16: decoding before signature verification is
  forbidden — "identity before payload parsing" — so the signature must cover
  the un-decoded base64 field; the node verifies the envelope, THEN
  base64-decodes `payload_b64`). NOT over serialized JSON.
- **`protocol_version`** is in the envelope AND the preimage; a node rejects
  any envelope whose `protocol_version` ≠ the manifest-pinned version (the
  version lives on the envelope, not the payload; ADR-0013 §4's `BaseManifest`
  pins it). **v0 constant: `protocol_version = 0`** — the minimal in-memory
  manifest sets it to `0` and the node compares against that; define it as a
  named const (`PROTOCOL_VERSION_V0 = 0`), not a magic literal. (V0-9's real
  provisioning carries the same field forward.)
- **`recipient_node_id`** binds the envelope to its intended receiver: a node
  rejects any envelope whose `recipient_node_id` ≠ its own `node_id`. Closes
  cross-recipient replay for THIS and every future `msg_type` (a directed
  message a peer replays to a different node fails the bind), so replay-safety
  never rests on idempotency alone.
- **`payload_b64` is opaque:** base64 of canonical payload bytes, decoded only
  AFTER the envelope authenticates.
- `timestamp`: u64 unix seconds; `nonce`: 16 random bytes, hex.
- **Freshness window (decided 2026-07-16):** accept
  `timestamp ∈ [now − 300s, now + 60s]` — 5 min past tolerance (v1 Tor
  latency + retries + skew), 60s future (skew only). Two `const`s with the
  rationale in a comment, NOT config (hygiene knob, not a ceremony knob — the
  window is hygiene, not safety: every planned msg_type is recipient-bound +
  idempotent). **Nonce-cache prune keys on the envelope's `timestamp`, not
  receipt time** (Fable-review fix 2026-07-16): retain a nonce until
  `timestamp < now − 300` — pruning a future-stamped envelope by receipt time
  would reopen a ~60s replay window. Nodes never exchange or negotiate time —
  no inter-node time protocol, ever (attacker-influenceable input to a hygiene
  mechanism); hosts run NTP (v1 deployment guidance). Use a **monotonic
  high-water mark** for `now` in both the freshness test and the nonce prune
  (never let `now` go backwards) — a backwards NTP step would otherwise let
  pruned nonces re-enter the window with an empty cache. **Count freshness
  rejections per peer and surface them through the existing alert queue /
  `GET /events` path** (codex I2 — a concrete operator-visible surface, not a
  bare counter): emit a structured event carrying the peer `node_id`, the
  running reject count, and a clock-skew hint, so an operator sees WHICH node's
  clock is off before it is silently ejected from the combine set.
  **PRESERVE the existing watchtower event JSON** (codex audit 2026-07-16): the
  current alert shape (`watchtower.rs`) and its dedupe key assume every event
  has a txid/outpoint. Do NOT fabricate transaction fields for a freshness
  event — generalize the internal event to an enum (or give the freshness event
  an explicit dedupe key) so existing recovery-path/un-cosigned alerts keep
  their exact JSON and dedupe behavior. Test peer attribution, monotonic count,
  and visibility through `/events`, AND that existing watchtower alert JSON is
  unchanged. Also assert a
  saturated `/channel` verification load does NOT starve `/events` or the
  watchtower tick (the isolation the async migration bought).
- **Receiver verification order:** `protocol_version` = manifest's →
  **`wallet_id` = my vault's AND `manifest_hash` = mine** (explicit
  local-vault equality — codex fix 2026-07-16: the endorsement domain
  separator catches cross-vault indirectly, but a direct equality check is
  cleaner and independently testable) → `recipient_node_id` = my `node_id` →
  sender_node_id in manifest → endorsement valid → `channel_sig` valid over the
  recomputed preimage → `timestamp` within the freshness window → **atomically
  consume `(sender_node_id, nonce)`** (check-unseen-and-insert in ONE step,
  AFTER sig + freshness pass but BEFORE dispatch — codex B1 fix 2026-07-16:
  deferring nonce consumption until after acceptance would let an
  authenticated-but-rejected message be replayed; the seen-nonce set is keyed
  by authenticated `sender_node_id`) → only then base64-decode `payload_b64`
  and dispatch on `msg_type`.
- `msg_type` exists so V0-8b (combine coordination) and V0-4 (duress
  propagation) add message types without a wire break; this task implements
  exactly one: `partial`. **Every registered `msg_type` MUST be recipient-bound
  (via `recipient_node_id`) AND idempotent — each `msg_type` must define an
  explicit idempotency key and pass a duplicate-delivery test before it is
  registered for dispatch** (both-model fix 2026-07-16: "assert idempotent"
  can't enforce semantics, so make it a concrete gate — a type without a
  declared idempotency key + passing dup-delivery test does not ship). For
  `partial` the idempotency key is `(commitment_id, input, signer)` and
  re-delivery re-stores the already-verified partial (a no-op); the nonce
  check is hygiene on top.

### 4. Candidate registry (the seam that makes verification possible)
`/channel` must verify partials against this node's OWN canonical view — which
today dies as a local variable inside `handle_sign`. Add a
`register_candidate(...)` call on `handle_sign`'s **verdict paths** (both the
early-return `Pending` and the signed-response path). **A small, behavior-
preserving control-flow refactor of `handle_sign` is permitted** for this —
"exactly one call site" is not required and cannot cover both a Pending
early-return and a signed return while excluding refusals; a single
post-verdict funnel (`register on Pending|Signed, never on Refusal`) is the
clean shape (codex fix 2026-07-16). This is the ONLY spend-path CHANGE
permitted; do not alter any policy check, response shape, or the sign decision.
- **Keyed by `commitment_id`** (NOT bare unsigned-txid — codex/Fable fix
  2026-07-16: the same txid can have several live commitments with different
  expiry/user-signature instances; keying by txid would collide them). The
  record stores: `commitment_id`, the unsigned-txid (verified transaction
  identity — partials still bind to it), the canonical PSBT, per-input
  sighashes (recomputed by THIS node), the expected descriptor pubkey per
  (input, node_id), the spend's user-signature material, `user_sig_hash`
  (**tagged SHA-256 over the user's DER signature(s) + sighash-type byte(s),
  in input order, as this node verified them at ingress**), and the
  commitment expiry (its own, fixed eviction horizon — no extension).
  Registration reserves a candidate slot **after** the verdict. **In V0-8a, at
  capacity the candidate is simply NOT inserted** (log it; the `/sign` verdict
  and response are unchanged — there is no wire-level `AT_CAPACITY` refusal and
  no duress surface in this task). The full "capacity gate runs AFTER pin/safety
  so a duress arm/freeze is never suppressed" ordering is a **V0-4 obligation**
  (§ scope guard), because only V0-4 introduces the safety track that ordering
  protects.
Storage: `Arc<Mutex<PartialStore>>` on `Node` (the V0-8b Hold-expiry
timer task will read it too).
**Which verdicts register (decided 2026-07-16):** every NON-REFUSED verdict —
instantly-signed spends AND accepted-but-Pending hot spends, both at ingress
(V0-8b's Hold-expiry combine and Model B's sign-at-ingress require Pending
registration; a fast peer's partial arriving during our Hold then verifies
instead of bouncing as unknown-candidate). **Refused requests never
register** — nothing will ever combine for them, and refused junk must not
occupy the store. Escape candidates arrive with the tagged-request migration
(ADR-0013 §2) — out of V0-8a scope.

### 5. Partial-signature exchange (the core primitive)
The `partial` payload carries: `commitment_id`, `wallet_id`, the exact
unsigned-txid, input index, signer node id, sighash type, spend purpose,
`user_sig_hash`, and the partial signature (DER). (`protocol_version` is on the
envelope, not the payload.)
On receipt, after envelope authentication:
- **Equality checks:** payload `wallet_id` matches the envelope's;
  **`signer_node_id == sender_node_id`** (nodes only relay their own partials
  in V0-8a); the payload's txid matches the candidate's stored txid;
  `user_sig_hash` matches the registered candidate's.
- **Candidate check:** the `commitment_id` must be a **registered candidate**;
  a partial for an unknown commitment is answered `UNKNOWN_CANDIDATE`
  (retriable). The sender applies **bounded retry with backoff until the
  commitment expiry** — codex fix 2026-07-16: "re-sends at fire time" alone
  fails the escape-class immediate-fire case and races the concurrent fan-out,
  so an explicit bounded-retry rule (or a candidate-ready ack) is required, not
  an assumption. Do NOT hold unknown partials on the receiver.
- **`spend_purpose` is informational only** — nothing acts on it; transaction
  class is always derived locally (ADR-0012's node-derived class predicate).
- **Verify the partial** against the expected descriptor pubkey for
  (input, signer node id) over this node's **own registered sighash** before
  storing; import only verified signature fields into the canonical PSBT
  (**never blind-merge a peer PSBT**).
- **Structural store bound:** at most one partial per
  (candidate, input, signer); partials accepted only for registered
  candidates. No generic FIFO/LRU eviction — a compromised peer must not be
  able to evict quorum-useful partials.
- **Hard capacity cap (decided 2026-07-16, D12):** a configured maximum on
  active candidates AND total bytes, bounding RAM. **In V0-8a this gates ONLY
  the registry insertion, never the wire.** At capacity: the candidate is not
  inserted (log it), no live candidate is ever evicted (a compromised peer must
  not evict quorum-useful partials), and the `/sign` verdict/response is
  **unchanged** — there is no wire-level `AT_CAPACITY` message and no duress
  surface in this task. The insertion runs after the verdict, so the sign
  decision is never affected by store fullness.
  **V0-4 obligation (not built here):** once the duress safety track exists, the
  capacity check must run AFTER pin/safety so a duress SpendRequest still
  arms/freezes when the store is full (freeze + lockdown need no candidate slot;
  only the best-effort sweep candidate does) — preserving ADR-0012's "arming is
  keyed on the duress pin alone, unconditional, resource-independent." Recorded
  in the scope guard.
- **Eviction (decided 2026-07-16; simplified in re-review — D13):** a candidate
  and its stored partials are evicted together when the candidate's
  **commitment expires** (node's own clock). **Keyed by `commitment_id`; each
  distinct commitment is its own candidate — there is NO horizon extension**
  (a fresh commitment is a new key, a new candidate; the old one expires on its
  own clock). Pruning runs in the **same sweep the replay log already runs AND
  is enforced at `/channel` candidate lookup** (an idle node never runs the
  /sign-path sweep, so an expired candidate must be rejected on lookup too).
  **No armed/scheduled exemption in V0-8a** — V0-8a builds no arming, no timers,
  and no fire, so it can neither set nor clear such an exemption. The
  armed-candidate expiry exemption + its fire-complete cleanup are **V0-4/V0-8b
  work** (see scope guard), added where arming and firing actually live.
  *Tests: an expired candidate is gone after the sweep and a late partial for
  it is rejected as unknown/expired even with no intervening /sign; two live
  commitments over the same txid are two distinct candidates.*

### 5b. `/channel` response schema (codex audit — exact shapes + status mapping)
Every `/channel` POST returns one tagged JSON body `{ "status": <TAG>, ... }`
with a fixed HTTP status. Exactly four outcomes:
- **`ACCEPTED`** — HTTP 200 — `{"status":"ACCEPTED"}` — envelope verified and
  the partial stored (or an idempotent re-store of an already-verified partial).
- **`REJECTED`** — HTTP **400** — `{"status":"REJECTED","reason":"<code>"}` —
  **permanent, do NOT retry.** `reason` is a fixed enum whose exact variant
  names are frozen in the module table + tests (codex nit). An oversized
  `/channel` body returns tagged `REJECTED`/400 (not axum's untagged 413 — the
  channel surface is uniformly tagged; `/sign` keeps its existing 413).
  `send_partial` classifies `REJECTED` as permanent. The full mapping of
  every rejection branch (§3 ingress + §5 partial checks) to this response:
  malformed JSON, oversized body, bad `protocol_version`, wrong
  `recipient_node_id`, wrong `wallet_id`/`manifest_hash`, unknown
  `sender_node_id`, bad endorsement, bad `channel_sig`, stale/future
  `timestamp`, replayed `nonce`, malformed `payload_b64`, unknown `msg_type`,
  `signer_node_id != sender_node_id`, payload/envelope field mismatch, wrong
  descriptor pubkey / txid / input / sighash / `user_sig_hash`, bad partial
  signature — ALL map to `REJECTED` with a distinct `reason` code. (Body-size
  and JSON-parse failures may surface as the axum-standard 413/400 before the
  handler; document which, and keep it consistent.)
- **`UNKNOWN_CANDIDATE`** — HTTP **409**, **retriable** —
  `{"status":"UNKNOWN_CANDIDATE"}` — envelope valid but the `commitment_id` is
  not (yet) a registered candidate here.
- **`RATE_LIMITED`** — HTTP **429**, retriable after backoff —
  `{"status":"RATE_LIMITED","retry_after_secs":<n>}` — per-peer quota or the
  pre-auth concurrency bound was hit.
Test the mapping: assert each rejection branch yields its exact status + reason.

### 6. Outbound: `send_partial` + bounded retry (reqwest)
- Add `reqwest` (default-tls off if unused; json feature as needed).
- `send_partial(peer, envelope)` POSTs to the peer's `/channel` with a
  per-send deadline and a bounded response read (`max_response_bytes`); a
  dead/unreachable peer is an error return, never a panic, and never blocks
  other sends (send to peers concurrently). Peer `endpoints` are canonical base
  URLs WITHOUT the `/channel` path; the sender appends `/channel` exactly once
  (codex nit).
- **Named bounded-retry helper (codex I1):** a `retry_partial_until` (or
  similar) that, on `UNKNOWN_CANDIDATE`/`RATE_LIMITED`, retries with backoff
  until the commitment expiry, then gives up. **CRITICAL (codex B1 fix
  2026-07-16): each retry RE-ENVELOPES from the immutable partial payload with a
  FRESH nonce + timestamp + `channel_sig`** — a channel nonce is single-use
  (consumed on the receiver at first sight), so re-sending the *same* envelope
  would self-reject as `REPLAYED_NONCE`. The helper holds the payload, not the
  envelope; it builds a new signed envelope per attempt. Tests: unknown-
  candidate → peer registers later → a freshly re-enveloped retry succeeds;
  **re-sending the identical envelope is rejected as replay, but a fresh
  re-envelope of the same payload is accepted** (prove both); expiry terminates
  retry; backoff honored; concurrent fan-out independent. One-shot
  `send_partial` alone is NOT sufficient.
- **Partial-release authorization (ADR-0012):** `send_partial` is
  `pub(crate)`, with the invariant documented at its definition: no partial
  may leave the node before its candidate's authorized fire event; V0-8a has
  NO production caller — V0-8b must add the fire-authorization gate before
  wiring one. Tests are the only callers in this task.

### 7. Signing-oracle prohibition (structural, absolute)
A peer message must **never** cause the node to create a signature. The
`/channel` handler only *verifies and stores*; it has structurally no path to
invoke the signer. Add a test asserting no channel message of any `msg_type`
triggers signing.

### 8. DoS guards (layered)
- **Pre-auth (cheap, before any crypto):** the existing 1 MiB body limit; a
  global bound on concurrent `/channel` requests — so forged traffic cannot
  burn a victim peer's quota or the node's CPU unboundedly.
- **Post-auth (after envelope verification):** per-peer quota
  (envelopes/minute) keyed by authenticated sender_node_id; duplicate-envelope
  suppression (the nonce set); the structural PartialStore bound from §5.
- Isolated from the watchtower task.

### 9. Module docs
Give the channel module a module-level ASCII diagram of the envelope ingress
pipeline (protocol_version → recipient bind → manifest → endorsement → sig →
freshness → nonce → decode payload_b64 → equality → candidate(commitment_id) →
verify-partial → store, with every rejection exit).

## Tests (`vault-node`)
- **Derivation**: channel key is a pure function — same config ⇒ same channel
  pubkey; channel pubkey ≠ signing pubkey.
- **Manifest/startup invariants**: a config whose signing key is not in the
  descriptor fails startup; manifest hash is stable across field-order
  permutations of the input (canonicalization works); endorsement over the
  wrong manifest_hash rejected.
- **Identity/endorsement**: endorsed by an in-manifest signing key → accepted;
  endorsed by a non-member key → rejected; **an envelope carrying another
  vault's `wallet_id`/`manifest_hash` → rejected by the direct local-equality
  check, independently of endorsement validity** (a well-formed envelope for a
  different vault is refused before sender lookup); **an envelope signed by the
  coordinator auth key instead of an endorsed channel key → rejected** (the
  "coordinator cannot mint a node" property, executable).
- **Envelope ingress rejection branches** (each its own test): tampered
  `payload_b64` bytes (channel_sig fails) → rejected; **`recipient_node_id` ≠
  my node_id → rejected** (cross-recipient replay); **`protocol_version` ≠
  manifest's → rejected**; stale timestamp → rejected; **future-stamped
  envelope's nonce retained until its timestamp leaves the window** (no ~60s
  replay reopen); replayed nonce → rejected AND the nonce set is pruned by
  timestamp (bounded); oversized body → rejected; per-peer quota exceeded →
  rejected; global concurrent bound enforced; malformed JSON → 400;
  payload/envelope field mismatch → rejected; `signer_node_id != sender_node_id`
  → rejected.
- **Wire preimage**: signature verifies over the raw `payload_b64` ASCII bytes
  WITHOUT decoding first (a valid envelope authenticates before any
  base64-decode); a bit-flip in `payload_b64` fails verification.
- **Partial exchange**: a valid partial over a registered candidate + correct
  descriptor pubkey verifies and is stored; wrong signer key, wrong txid,
  wrong input index, wrong sighash, wrong `user_sig_hash` → rejected;
  unknown-`commitment_id` → `UNKNOWN_CANDIDATE` (retriable); duplicate
  suppressed; a second different partial for the same (candidate, input,
  signer) does not evict the first verified one.
- **Registry lifecycle**: two live commitments over the same txid (fresh
  nonce/expiry) are distinct candidates (keyed by `commitment_id`), and
  registering the second does not evict the first; each expires on its own
  commitment clock (no horizon extension); an expired candidate is rejected at
  `/channel` lookup with no intervening `/sign` sweep; at the hard capacity cap
  the new candidate is **not inserted** and no live candidate is evicted,
  **and the `/sign` verdict/response is unchanged by the cap** (capacity gates
  the registry slot, not the sign decision — no wire `AT_CAPACITY` in V0-8a).
- **Signing-oracle**: no channel message of any `msg_type` causes the node to
