per-coin confirmation heights. Do not build 00i's deliverables here; do not pretend the E2E can run
without an address.

## 4. REVIEW CORRECTIONS 2026-08-05 (codex+Fable panel on the ADR-0016 commit)

(a) SEALING REQUIRES THE CANONICAL PREIMAGE, not just manifest.json. Nodes recompute the manifest
hash from `base_manifest_bytes`, not from the file, so a field written to the JSON but absent from
that preimage is a value no node is bound to. This bead
must amend the preimage AND the node config startup parses, in the same change. Without that,
`escape_bump_max_fee_pct` is decoration. See ADR-0016 decision 3a.

ADR-0013 §4'S PREIMAGE LIST WAS TWO FIELDS SHORT (`escape_feerate_floor`, `escape_coverage_pct`,
which the code hashes at channel.rs:499-501). THAT IS NOW FIXED IN THE ADR — do not re-fix it. What
remains yours is adding the NEW field as an unsigned `u8`, fixed-width one byte, written as
`e.u8(escape_bump_max_fee_pct)` immediately after `e.u8(escape_coverage_pct)` and before
`e.u32(nodes.len() as u32)`, plus the node config startup parses.

(b) THE CEREMONY VALIDATION RULE IS EXACT, not "comfortably below":
BOTH of `escape_bump_max_fee_pct <= 100 - escape_coverage_pct` and
`escape_bump_max_fee_pct <= policy_core::MAX_FEE_PERCENT` (10) -- the second is not optional: at a
low coverage the first alone admits 19, and every rung above 10% is refused at ingress by
`verify_escape`, sealing a vault whose own ladder is unusable. PLUS the 5x margin ADR-0016 DECIDES
(`escape_bump_max_fee_pct * 5 <= 100 - escape_coverage_pct`), which is a chosen margin and not a
node fact -- nodes accept 2-5% at the 95% default (both caps are <=, and policy-core doctrine is
"Exactly at the cap passes"). Integer arithmetic, at seal time.

(c) THE JOINT CEREMONY QUESTION IS OWNED BY btc-policy-wdu, WHICH DEPENDS ON THIS BEAD. The edge runs in that direction so this bead does not block its seven existing dependents on the timelock work, while wdu is definitively second and cannot close with separate prompts. Today the startup rejection is `policy_core::parse_vault_template` (template.rs:182), run by EVERY NODE AT STARTUP -- not recovery.rs:88, which is a redundant drill-side assertion three lines after a parse that already errored and is unreachable for a non-default timelock. That parser is why there is no non-default value to couple to until wdu lands, and it is what wdu must change. SCOPE: this bead ships the ladder field, its Ceremony input and the validation; wdu wires the combined SELECTION and displays both resulting values as choices. What this bead must NOT do is offer the timelock as a selectable value against a parser that rejects every non-default -- that is the half joint prompt to avoid. It MUST still DISPLAY the timelock beside the ceiling as a fixed 180 days: disclosure is not coupling, and without it every vault sealed between this bead and wdu is sealed after an uncoupled choice, irreversibly, in violation of ADR-0016 §4.

(d) COUNT TRANSACTIONS PRESENTED, NOT SIGNATURES, in every acceptance criterion. A multi-input PSBT
takes one signature per input, so "exactly two signatures" has no stable observable meaning; "two
transactions presented for approval per SpendRequest" does. Do NOT qualify that with
"non-self-paired": a self-paired SpendRequest is refused outright (see the P1 correction above), so
the qualifier is vacuous and quietly preserves the withdrawn model.

## 5. ACCEPTED REVIEW FINDINGS: DOCUMENTATION CONSISTENCY (same delivery; no new mechanism)

Before this bead closes, reconcile every named normative copy with the already-authoritative code
and ADR-0013 contracts:

- ADR-0016's signing-seam decision must REQUIRE approval of every otherwise-valid escape-class pair
  with the generic escape-destination display above. Remove the reject-the-pair option; add no role
  binding.
- The transaction-class predicate must say that verified vault change is permitted in every class
  and excluded from classification: escape-class iff every *destination* output pays the escape
  descriptor, refresh-class iff every output pays the vault descriptor, hot-class iff every
  *destination* output pays a hot-allowlist descriptor, mixed/unrecognized destinations rejected.
  Fix ADR-0012's immediately-following "Nodes validate the escape" bullet, V0-PLAN's second V0-6
  predicate, and ADR-0016's bounded-residual paragraph; do not leave the corrected rule beside an
  "every output" copy.
- ADR-0012's coordinator-auth preimage formula must include `escape_bumps`: its length is written
  unconditionally and every rung's full bytes are length-prefixed by `CoordRequest::canonical_bytes`.
  This finding is limited to the ladder omission; do not turn it into unrelated preimage redesign.
- CONTEXT's Escape glossary entry must say that an omitted or undecodable mandatory Escape produces
  HTTP 400 `BadRequest`, not a `200 {refusal}` policy result.
- CONTEXT's Coordinator boundary must say it cannot broadcast arbitrary bytes itself, while recording
  the accepted influence it retains over node broadcast: rung stripping/re-signing can suppress or
  downgrade the T-time sweep, and escape-class role swapping can choose which signed leg releases
  immediately and can suppress the residual sweep. It still cannot alter or redirect a user-signed
  transaction.
- V0-PLAN's enumerated immutable-manifest `Fields:` list must include the existing preimage fields
  `escape_feerate_floor` and `escape_coverage_pct`; ADR-0013 §4 and `base_manifest_bytes` remain the
  authority.

Close with a literal sweep across CONTEXT.md, docs/, crates/, and btc-policy-mby/sqn/wdu for each of
those claims. A corrected paragraph beside a stale twin does not satisfy this bead.

title: Refresh maturity monitoring: countdown, nags, and a safety-margin gate for funded vaults
description:
FILED 2026-07-30 from the codex+Fable spec review. Fable named this the single most likely cause of real loss of funds given the current specs, and NO BEAD OWNED IT -- verified by grepping all 46 beads for maturity/countdown/nag.

THE GAP. docs/DESIGN.md specifies refresh nags 'from day 120, shrill from day 150' and a ~90-day signing cadence. docs/ROLLOUT-PLAN.md requires Survivor vaults to 'publish their maturity countdown and Refresh before a mandatory safety margin'. btc-policy-mby delivers the refresh COMMAND, but its NON-GOALS line explicitly excludes 'monitoring/alerting integration' -- so nothing computes the countdown, nothing nags, and nothing blocks a stage from running past maturity. The specs require a control that no bead builds.

WHY IT IS THE TOP LOSS PATH, not merely a UX nicety. The 2-of-3 recovery keyset is distributed to THIRD PARTIES on purpose -- it doubles as the inheritance mechanism (CONTEXT.md). After the timelock matures it is a COMPLETE authorization path: no PIN, no user key, no Hold, no allowlist, no federation, no coordinator. Every other theft path in this design requires defeating something cryptographic or multi-party; this one requires only a calendar and two people (or one thief who has collected two key backups). The failure is INVISIBLE until the spend confirms, and the watchtower's recovery-path alert is POST-SPEND -- by the time it fires the coins are moving and the normal path is already dead.

It is worse today than the design assumes: a sealed vault cannot be refreshed at all (threat-model R9, btc-policy-mby), so ANY funded sealed vault is on a fixed fuse from its first deposit. And the relative timelock runs PER UTXO from each coin's confirmation, so there is no single vault-level maturity date -- a straggler deposit made after Lockdown starts its own clock.

DELIVER:
(1) A per-UTXO maturity computation -- earliest maturity across the vault's unspent set, not a vault-level constant, derived from each coin's confirmation height and the descriptor's timelock.
(2) A countdown surface an operator can read WITHOUT the coordinator being trusted or even alive, since a dead coordinator is exactly when a vault drifts. Prefer something derivable from the descriptor and a chain view alone.
(3) Nags at thresholds expressed as FRACTIONS OF THE VAULT'S OWN TIMELOCK -- 2/3 and 5/6 of it -- NOT as fixed day counts. On the 180-day default those land on day 120 and day 150, matching DESIGN.md, which is where the fixed numbers came from. THE FIXED NUMBERS ARE WRONG IN THIS GRAPH: btc-policy-wdu (same gate, P1) makes the timelock configurable per vault, so on a 90-day vault a day-120 nag fires AFTER maturity and a day-150 nag never fires at all -- the exact invisible-calendar failure this bead exists to prevent, on precisely the vaults wdu makes weakest. The 'mandatory safety margin' ROLLOUT-PLAN.md refers to but never numbers must likewise be a fraction, not a day count.
(4) A stage gate: a Survivor vault that crosses the safety margin during an observation run either gets refreshed or the run aborts. Today the stage-8 soak's whole purpose ('run it for a while') pushes in the opposite direction.
(5) State plainly what this does NOT do: it protects the operator who looks. It is not a control against a recovery-key holder who acts, and it must not be written up as one.

DEPENDS ON btc-policy-mby (the refresh command must exist before a nag can tell anyone to run it).

VERIFY: a regtest vault with mixed-age UTXOs reports the correct earliest maturity; nags fire at both thresholds ON THE DEFAULT TIMELOCK **AND** ON A SHORT NON-DEFAULT ONE (the second case is the real test -- an implementation with hardcoded day counts passes the first and fails the second, so a VERIFY that only exercised the default would rubber-stamp the bug); the safety-margin gate refuses to let a stage run continue past the margin; the countdown is correct for a coin deposited AFTER Lockdown (the straggler case, which is the one that has no remedy).

OWNERSHIP BOUNDARY (bead-polish 2026-07-30): THE NOTIFICATION CHANNEL BELONGS TO btc-policy-2oz, NOT HERE. This bead owns COMPUTING maturity and deciding WHEN a nag is due; 2oz owns getting a message to a human and handling a dead delivery path. Filed separately, both described 'notify the operator', which would have produced two channels with two failure modes and two things to configure. A maturity nag is delivered through 2oz's channel.

title: Resolve the node lifecycle contradiction (ADR decision; the drill is btc-policy-h22)
description:
FROM THE 2026-07-29 STATE REVIEW (codex #2). The operational documents are MUTUALLY INCOMPATIBLE, which means routine maintenance has no valid security-preserving procedure:
 - ADR-0005: the host is SEALED — SSH uninstalled, no administrative access path, 'no reset, no reconfiguration, no upgrade-in-place'.
 - ADR-0007: a rebooted node is a DEAD node (tmpfs; the reboot wipes key, Lockdown latch, generation marker).
 - docs/SETUP-CEREMONY.md: each node starts once and its preimage is destroyed.
 - docs/OPERATIONS-RUNBOOK.md: every start needs the preimage, and it is a backup item.
(The rolling-restart claim in UPGRADE-AND-ROTATION-POLICY was already deleted in 14c2312 as unperformable under ADR-0005; this bead resolves the REMAINING tension rather than papering it.)

DECIDE, in an ADR, ONE model:
 (a) immutable one-shot nodes — every binary or config change is a vault migration, the preimage is genuinely destroyed after first start, and there is no supported restart; or
 (b) recoverable hardware-backed nodes — the signing key lives in hardware rather than being re-derived from an operator preimage, restart is a supported operation, and Lockdown becomes a DURABLE MONOTONIC latch rather than something a reboot clears.
Option (b) is the one codex recommends longer-term; option (a) is what the code implements today. Whichever is chosen, the ADR must supersede or amend the losers explicitly — this failure mode is documents disagreeing, so a new document that merely adds a fourth voice makes it worse.

SPLIT 2026-07-30 (bead-polish): THE DRILL MOVED TO ITS OWN BEAD (see below). This bead is now the DECISION ONLY, which is what btc-policy-qbt (stage 5) and btc-policy-juq are actually gated on. The decision needs stage-4 attrition data (btc-policy-s12) and nothing else; bundling the drill with it made stage 5 wait on migration tooling it does not need.

VERIFY (decision): an ADR exists choosing (a) or (b); it EXPLICITLY supersedes or amends every losing document rather than adding a fourth voice -- this failure mode is documents disagreeing, so a new document that merely joins the argument makes it worse; and every operational doc is updated to match. The destructive drill that proves the chosen model is survivable is a separate bead and gates the same downstream work.

title: finalize_cmd round-trip test coverage (assemble -> node-endorse -> finalize)
description: 9y5.5 review surfaced that finalize_cmd (the real CLI production seal path) has NO e2e/unit coverage: the regtest harness (fed.rs) uses setup::node_config_toml + assemble() directly, never finalize_cmd. This is WHY codex found finalize bugs across passes 3-6 (wallet_id/manifest_hash recompute, coordinator-secret verify, listen_port-from-endpoints, complete typed manifest.json, backup regen). Add a round-trip test: run assemble (writes ceremony-state.json + coordinator-auth.secret + descriptor.txt etc.), generate each node's endorsement via ceremony::endorse on the device channel key (from the fixture preimages), run finalize_cmd, then assert: manifest.json is a complete typed BaseManifest (protocol_version u32 0, t/n/recovery_timelock/policy_version present); node-<id>.toml is 0600 with listen_port matching its endpoint; the finalize consistency checks fire (edited descriptor/wallet_id/manifest_hash/coordinator-secret/port each rejected before sealing). Parent: btc-policy-9y5.5 (closed, merged 8e3bb86).
close_reason: finalize_cmd round-trip coverage merged to main (075107e). Five tests drive the real commands (assemble_cmd -> per-device ceremony::endorse -> finalize_cmd): complete typed manifest.json incl. every hash-preimage field, 0600 node configs binding the ENDORSED endpoint port, all consistency checks firing before sealing (edited descriptor/manifest_hash/policy cap/endpoint/wrong coordinator secret), backup regeneration proven by corrupting siblings, missing+forged endorsements refused. Each property mutation-verified. Reviewed clean by codex + Fable (3 Fable findings fixed: unpinned backup regeneration, 4 unasserted manifest preimage fields, unpinned listen_port-from-endpoints).

title: 9y5.7 follow-up: batch the escape-ladder mempool residency scan
description: codex 9y5.7 pass-2 [P2]. mempool_escape_rung (crates/vault-node/src/lib.rs ~3091) loops over every ladder rung calling backend.mempool_transaction(txid), and BitcoindBackend::mempool_transaction (chain.rs:1184) issues a FULL getrawmempool (mempool_txids, chain.rs:688, uncached) on every call. So when NO rung is resident (first fire tick, or after eviction) a MAX_ESCAPE_BUMPS+1 (=4) rung ladder parses the entire mempool up to 4x per 1-Hz fire_tick — wasteful exactly under congestion when the combine window is tightest. SAFE + BOUNDED (correctness unaffected; the multiplication is transient — once a rung is broadcast the loop returns on the first resident match). FIX: add a batched membership method to the ChainBackend trait (mempool_txids() -> HashSet<Txid> or resident_rung(&[Txid])), implement for BitcoindBackend (private helper exists) AND MockBackend, then rewrite mempool_escape_rung to read the snapshot ONCE and getrawtransaction only the matching rung. Deferred from 9y5.7 finish: fix touches fire path + backend trait; concern is bounded perf, not correctness. Gates: fmt/clippy-D/workspace tests, attack 16/16, all 3 demos.
close_reason: Batched ladder mempool residency read merged to main (b4a3f93). New ChainBackend::mempool_resident(&[Txid]) collapses up-to-4 full getrawmempool pulls per fire tick to one snapshot; default impl preserves old per-txid behaviour, BitcoindBackend overrides. Cheapest-rung-first order preserved (the resident rung is what the RBF replacement's ancestry proof is built against). Reviewed by codex + Fable; all Fable findings fixed (restored the ladder-membership guard the batched call had downgraded, covered the live-Core path, deduped mock/default via one helper, documented the fetch-race). Mutation-verified. Pre-existing sibling pathology in validate_ancestors filed as btc-policy-zzv.

title: Sealed node image: ADR-0005 build (no SSH, no admin path, tmpfs, reboot-death)
description:
FILED 2026-07-29 from the plan review (Fable Q6.3). Rollout stages 4,5,7,8,9 all require SEALED HOSTS, and the plan and bead s12 both cited btc-policy-4y3 as 'the sealed-host build' — but 4y3 is COORDINATOR host hardening: a different machine, a different threat (THREAT-MODEL R8b). The ADR-0005 sealed NODE image had NO BEAD AT ALL; the s12 -> 4y3 edge worked only by title confusion.

DELIVER the reproducible sealed node image ADR-0005 actually specifies: SSH uninstalled, no administrative access path of any kind, no reset, no reconfiguration, no upgrade-in-place; config and key material on tmpfs so a reboot wipes the signing key, the Lockdown latch, and the process-generation xattr (ADR-0007); the node's only surfaces being its API (/sign, /channel, /events, /healthz, /pending) and its chain backend. The image build must be reproducible and documented — an operator has to be able to rebuild and diff it, since after sealing there is no way to inspect the running host.

CARE: the seal is what makes duress Lockdown irreversible BY ANYONE, including the legitimate owner — that is why coercion has no reset to demand. Any capability left on the host that could restart or reconfigure a node is the reset a wrench attacker asks for. Enumerate explicitly what survives on the host and why a coercer cannot use it.

CONSEQUENCE TO STATE PLAINLY IN THE ARTIFACT: with this image, patching a node costs a full vault rotation and a dead node has no remedy. Stages 4 and 7 exist to measure whether that is livable (bead s12).

VERIFY: two independent builds of the image produce identical artifacts; a sealed node serves the Path suite; and a written enumeration of residual host capability, reviewable by an external auditor.

title: Reproducible build pipeline: byte-identical rebuilds, signed artifacts, dependency gates in CI
description:
SPLIT OUT OF btc-policy-gbw 2026-07-30 (codex+Fable bead review). gbw had no blockers, so it could be closed against a commit lacking the stage-1 code; the freeze now waits for that code while THIS bead -- the pipeline that makes a freeze possible -- can start immediately.

DELIVER: (a) a REPRODUCIBLE BUILD -- pinned toolchain, deterministic flags, documented procedure -- such that an independent rebuild of a given commit yields byte-identical binaries. Verified by someone rebuilding on a DIFFERENT MACHINE; a hash produced by the same box proves nothing. Name who or what that second machine is (CI runner, a second developer box) rather than leaving it to the implementer. (b) SIGNED RELEASE ARTIFACTS -- state which key signs, who holds it, and how a verifier obtains the public half; a signature nobody can check is decoration. (c) cargo audit / cargo deny WIRED INTO CI, the gap docs/SBOM-AND-DEPENDENCY-POLICY.md already admits and threat-model R4 records; this is independently landable today and should not wait for (a).

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT ADDRESS (see btc-policy-4y3 and ADR-0012): reproducible builds are SUPPLY-CHAIN PROVENANCE. They close the poisoned-build and tampered-dependency vectors of residual R8b. They do NOT address malware resident on a correctly-built, correctly-verified running coordinator -- that needs no modified binary -- and they do not touch a wrench beginning mid-spend. The one narrow extra benefit is detection: re-hashing an installed binary catches malware that persisted by patching it, and only if the check runs from OUTSIDE the compromised host.

VERIFY: two different machines produce identical hashes for the same commit; CI fails on a known-vulnerable dependency (demonstrate with a deliberately pinned bad version, then revert); a third party can verify a release signature from published instructions alone.

title: Operator CLI slice: 'pending' — poll every node and diff against what the user authorized
description:
SPLIT OUT OF btc-policy-mby 2026-07-30 (codex+Fable bead review). Slice 3 of 4. DEPENDS ON the mby core substrate. Small, read-only, and independently landable.

WHY: docs/OPERATIONS-RUNBOOK.md tells a user to poll /pending -- 'presumably by hand', as threat-model R9 records. This is the incident surface btc-policy-k0t built on the node side, with nothing on the operator side to consume it. THREAT-MODEL A7 answers the coordinator-auth-key thief by citing 'every node's pin-uniform GET /pending projection', which is only an answer if some tool actually polls it.

DELIVER: 'pending' -- poll GET /pending on ALL n nodes (not a quorum, and never via the coordinator's own view), present the accepted-candidate set per node, and DIFF IT against the spends this operator authorized.

THE HARD PART, which must be decided in this bead rather than left to the implementer: WHERE THE AUTHORIZED-COMMITMENT RECORD LIVES. Diffing requires durable local state recording what the user authorized -- but ADR-0010 makes the coordinator an untrusted relay, so a journal that lives only there can be edited by the component the diff is meant to catch. Specify the journal's location, format and trust properties, and state plainly what an attacker who controls the coordinator host can do to it. If the honest answer is 'nothing protects it there', say so and put it elsewhere.

ALSO: a divergence between nodes is itself the signal (one node holding a candidate the others do not is the arm-split shape ADR-0012 cares about), so present per-node disagreement rather than merging into one list.

VERIFY: a candidate accepted by all n shows as agreed; a candidate injected at one node only shows as divergent; a spend the user never authorized shows as unrecognized; the command works against a node set where one node is unreachable, without hanging or silently dropping it from the comparison.

title: Passive receipt clock destroys a ruled carrier memo and intent: raw-clock prune loses holder confirmations irrecoverably
description:
FOUND 2026-08-03 during btc-policy-9zs implementation (rb-lite round-9 panel, codex gpt-5.6-sol,
rated P0 confidence 10/10). PRE-EXISTING: verified byte-identical on origin/main before 9zs. Filed
at P1 rather than P0 because the trigger is an ENVIRONMENTAL clock fault rather than anything a
post-wrench coordinator controls -- but the consequence class is theft, not censorship, so disagree
with that downgrade if you have reason to.

## The defect

`ChannelState::carrier_memo_lookup` calls `store.prune_intents(now)` where `now` is the RAW wall
clock: production `handle_channel_body_now` passes `channel::unix_now` as `confirmation_clock`.
`prune_intents` retains both `intents` and `carriers_by_nonce` on `expiry > now`. A transient
forward clock excursion -- NTP step, VM restore, RTC fault -- past a live carrier's expiry therefore
DELETES this node's own arm intent and its `Derived` memo, on an untrusted read, driven by a
PASSIVE peer receipt rather than by anything this node decided.

This violates a rule the repo states explicitly in `NonceLog::effective_now`'s doc (replay.rs):
'Carrier intents must use this same value: pruning or confirming them against raw wall time after
the nonce log has advanced would let a clock rollback revive logically-expired confirmation state.'

## Why it does not recover

`NonceLog` deliberately does NOT advance `high_water` for a REJECTED forward-clock request
(replay.rs), precisely so one excursion cannot latch a bogus future mark and refuse honestly-timed
requests afterwards. That correct decision means nothing restores the deleted state once the clock
corrects. A later peer receipt resolves to `Vacant` -> `carrier = None` -> `ChannelReply::Accepted`;
`retry_loop` RETURNS on `Accepted`, so the sender never retries; `confirm_carrier` then finds no
intent and returns NONE forever.

## The stake

Section 0 arming counts receipts to reach t-of-n. A silently lost receipt can leave one honest node
UNARMED. Codex's chain: during the explicitly supported normal-to-duress resubmission, that unarmed
node plus t-1 compromised nodes can release and finalize the pending hot spend, because the freeze
is LOCAL. That is the unfrozen-quorum / theft class -- the same class `MemoOutcome::InFlight` was
added to close, arriving through a different door.

## What btc-policy-9zs did and did not do

9zs added `owner_still_ruling` so `prune_intents` retains BOTH an `InFlight` claim AND a `Derived`
memo whose owner is still ruling. That closes the half 9zs itself created. The remaining hole is a
RULED `Derived` memo whose intent has aged out -- the case the code comment calls 'the ordinary
expiry case'. So 9zs NARROWED this defect and documented the boundary in code; it did not close it.
Do not read the surviving asymmetry as an oversight.

## The decision this bead must make -- do not skip it

Making passive expiry non-destructive requires deciding what BOUNDS the two maps if untrusted reads
can never evict. `prune_intents_after_nonce_accept` is the authorized evictor today and is what
keeps them bounded. Options, each with a different bound argument:
  (a) route every passive prune through `effective_now` instead of raw wall time;
  (b) make passive prune fully non-destructive and rely solely on the accept-path evictor;
  (c) give memos a separate rollback-guarded horizon.
Pick one and STATE the bound argument. Do NOT fix this by widening `owner_ruling` to all `Derived`
memos without one -- that is precisely what makes the maps unbounded.

## Verify

A test that steps the receipt clock forward past a LIVE RULED carrier's expiry, lands a peer
receipt, steps the clock back, and asserts the intent and memo both survive and the receipt is
still counted. The existing `a_forward_receipt_clock_cannot_make_an_in_flight_claim_vacant_before_rollback`
(added by 9zs) is the template; extend it to the ruled case. Both maps must be shown to stay
bounded under the chosen option.

title: Rollout stage 5: sealed hosts on mainnet (gated on the nju lifecycle decision)
description:
Rollout ladder stage 5 (docs/ROLLOUT-PLAN.md): five machines, one provider, SEALED hosts, MAINNET. Full two-vault Path suite.

GATED ON btc-policy-nju BEING DECIDED — with stage-4 attrition data in hand. That ordering is the whole point of the 2026-07-29 decision: seal on signet first (stage 4, bead s12), measure how long five sealed nodes actually survive untouched and what a migration-to-patch really costs, and only then choose between immutable one-shot nodes and recoverable hardware-backed nodes with a durable monotonic Lockdown latch. Putting mainnet funds behind the wrong model is exactly what this rung waits for.

HONEST FRAMING (plan review, Fable Q5): this is a DEFAULT, not a pure deferral. Stage 4 cannot run without a sealed node image, and the seal IS the immutable one-shot model — so everything from stage 4 onward is built on model (a) unless attrition proves it intolerable. Also, part of the answer is knowable now: commodity cloud providers reboot and live-migrate VMs on their own schedule, and under ADR-0007 every such event is a dead node, so stage-4 attrition will likely be dominated by provider maintenance. Measure the magnitude, not the direction.

IF nju RESOLVES TO (b), hardware-backed with supported restart, a durable Lockdown latch is necessary but NOT sufficient — see the durable-state bead; and review #2's scope must reopen to cover the reworked core invariant, because review #1 froze a core in which reboot-death was load-bearing.

VERIFY: full Path suite on both vaults; the nju ADR closed and its superseded alternatives named; no mainnet funds committed before that ADR exists.

title: V0-4b-harness: adversarial regtest demonstration
description:
## V0-4b-harness: adversarial regtest harness demonstrating the duress mechanism on a live n=2t-1 federation. Split from V0-4b-core per the 2026-07-17 audit so a security invariant is not split across implementations. UPDATED 2026-07-20 to the mechanism the dual-model review settled: the signer/partial COUPLING + RELEASE-GATE is the theft proof (not the t-holder receipt count, which is timing), and the one residual (duress-signal censorship of a pre-pending normal hot spend from a sub-quorum) is BOUNDED by the V0-11 Hot budget (ADR-0014). Scenarios: toxic-parent, in-flight-refresh, two-spend-probe(silence), escape+refresh, arm-split-closed(coupling), censorship-residual-bounded(hot budget), partition, reboot-death, coverage/feerate fire-failure, recovery.

FULL TASK SPEC (self-contained; source task file .rb-lite/tasks/v0-4b-harness-adversarial.md is gitignored):

# V0-4b-harness: adversarial regtest harness for the duress mechanism

## Environment — read first
- No system C compiler. Run cargo/bitcoind via `nix develop -c ...`.
- **Prerequisite merged:** V0-4b-core (the two-track duress state machine) + the
  V0-11 hot-spend bound — plus everything they consume (V0-8b, V0-4a, V0-10).
  This bead is the **launch-gate adversarial demonstration**, split from the core
  per the 2026-07-17 audit so a security invariant is not split across
  implementations: the core owns the production state machine + its unit/model
  tests; this owns the broad, environment-heavy regtest/CLI scenarios.
- Authoritative for the MECHANISM (read before writing a single assertion):
  - `docs/adr/0012-...` — the two-track state machine, the transition table, and
    the invariant list. **Two passages are load-bearing and were re-settled by the
    2026-07-20 dual-model (codex + Fable) review; the harness must assert the
    property they state, not the earlier one:**
    - the **"CORRECTION (2026-07-20)"** paragraph at the end of the §"Duress state
      machine" intro, and
    - the **"Partial-release authorization (both candidates)"** invariant (the
      release-gate).
  - `docs/adr/0014-hot-spend-bound.md` — the Hot budget (per-tx cap + velocity
    ledger) that BOUNDS the one residual this design leaves open.
  - `docs/DESIGN.md` (Success Criteria; attack scenarios), `CONTEXT.md`
    ("Duress PIN", "Hot budget").

## The mechanism this harness demonstrates (assert THIS, not the count)
The safety property is **not** "t nodes armed." With `n = 2t−1` and up to `t−1`
compromised, a holder set of size `t` has only `≥ 1` honest member, so a receipt
count can never *prove* `t` honest nodes froze — a receipt proves relay, not
freeze. The confirmation count is a **timing/liveness** mechanism (when the
freeze/sweep commit), not the theft proof.

What makes a coerced spend un-completable is the **signer/partial coupling +
release-gate** (ADR-0012 "Partial-release authorization" + the signing-oracle
prohibition):
1. **Coupling.** A node emits a partial for a candidate ONLY after independently
   receiving and processing that candidate's own user-authorized carrier (no
   peer message is ever a signing oracle). Processing a **duress**-pin carrier
   arms → freezes that candidate under the same store lock that would release it.
   So the set of honest nodes that hold a *releasable* partial for a
   duress-carried spend is a subset of the set that *froze* it — you cannot have
   an honest node that signed the carrier but did not freeze it. The arm cannot
   be split away from the signature.
2. **Release-gate.** Neither the spend's nor the escape's partial leaves the node
   before that candidate's authorized fire event; arming atomically + monotonically
   suppresses every existing and future hot-partial release. A hot candidate is
   never observable open-but-unfrozen (the freeze is set under the release lock).
3. **Result.** No honest node ever releases a coerced partial → only `≤ t−1`
   compromised nodes can → never a signing quorum. The sweep may still fail
   (funds sit frozen → recovery); that is denial, never theft.

**The one residual, and its bound.** A DIFFERENT case is not closed by the
coupling: a hot spend submitted EARLIER with the *normal* pin (legitimately
pending in Hold, every node holding an unfrozen partial), where a later duress
signal is **censored by a compromised coordinator** from a sub-quorum of honest
nodes — those nodes never freeze it and release at Hold-expiry. This censorship
residual is the accepted "hot wallet is the risk budget" residual, and it is
**bounded** by the V0-11 Hot budget (per-tx cap + rolling-window velocity), so
the most it can admit per window is one Hot budget, never the vault (ADR-0014).

## Outcome
An adversarial regtest harness (a `vault-cli attack`/`demo` subcommand and/or an
integration-test module) that DEMONSTRATES, end-to-end on a live regtest
federation (`n = 2t−1`, e.g. 3-of-5), that the duress mechanism holds its safety +
silence properties under adversarial conditions: freeze + lockdown → recovery, no
theft path, silent to an outside attacker, and the censorship residual empirically
bounded to the Hot budget. This is the empirical counterpart to V0-4b-core's unit
tests — the "wrench-attack answer is live" evidence.

## Why this exists
ADR-0012 says several duress properties are best "verified empirically … with an
adversarial regtest harness" — they involve process kills, network partitions,
mempool packages, and timing probes that unit tests can't fully exercise. And the
2026-07-20 review turned on a mechanism (coupling + release-gate vs. a receipt
count) that a live demonstration must pin down: the harness proves the *coupling*
holds against a coordinator that actively tries to split the arm from the
signature, and that the residual it does not close is bounded by the Hot budget.

## Required — the harness scenarios (each asserts the SAFETY outcome + no theft)
1. **toxic-parent**: an escape built over an external unconfirmed deposit →
   excluded (build-over-mempool); the escape either fires over vault-authorized
   inputs only or the sweep fails → Lockdown → recovery. No poisoned escape.
2. **in-flight-refresh**: a refresh in flight when duress arms → the escape
   chains off the refresh output (vault-authorized) OR the sweep fails → denial,
   never theft; the coerced hot spend is dead (frozen partial + unconditional
   Lockdown at T).
3. **two-spend-probe (silence)**: an attacker probing with two spends cannot read
   the duress bit — identical observable outcomes (latency, `/events`, peer
   traffic, response size) under both pins. Include the Hot-budget refusal path:
   a `HOT_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` refusal is pin-independent, so it does not leak the bit.
4. **escape-class + refresh sequences**: the two-slot record + `Idle→Armed`
   suppression behave per the transition table; escape-class completes + residual
   sweep over disjoint/union inputs; the normal pin's delayed slot is a no-op.
5. **arm-split-closed (the coupling — codex P0, 2026-07-19)**: a coerced hot spend
   submitted WITH the duress pin; a compromised coordinator tries to split the arm
   from the signature by making the carrier reach exactly ONE honest node and not
   the rest, via each concrete vector ADR-0012 names: (a) corrupt the user-signed
   escape so a peer's local policy refuses before propagation, (b) oversize the
   carrier past a peer's `max_msg_bytes`, (c) set an expiry that lapses mid-fan-out.
   **Assert the coupling, not a count:** the honest nodes that did not receive the
   carrier never signed its partial (no signing oracle), and the one(s) that did
   receive it froze it (release-gate). So at Hold-expiry the releasable partials
   number `≤ t−1` (compromised only) → the combine cannot reach a quorum → the
   coerced spend never broadcasts. Lockdown at T on the armed node(s) → recovery.
   There is no honest node that signed the carrier but left its partial unfrozen.
6. **censorship-residual-bounded (the Hot budget — ADR-0014 / V0-11)**: the case
   the coupling does NOT close — a hot spend pending under the *normal* pin, with a
   later duress signal censored from a sub-quorum. Demonstrate the BOUND, three
   parts: (a) an over-`hot_max_per_tx` coerced hot spend is refused at ingress at
   EVERY node with `HOT_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` **before signing**, so it never becomes a
   censor-completable pending candidate — and the duress arm still fires +
   propagates on that refusal path (composition); (b) within-cap hot spends whose
   window sum exceeds `hot_max_per_window` hit `HOT_VELOCITY_EXCEEDED` at ingress on
   the 2nd+ (an attacker cannot queue several large hot spends in one Hold and clear
   them all); (c) the release path gives budget back — a hot spend cancelled/expired
   **while still unexposed** frees its reservation, while a broadcast/released one
   meters to age-out (monotonic window). Net: the censored-completion is bounded to
   ≤ one window's Hot budget, never the vault.
7. **partition / selective delivery**: deliver the duress carrier to a subset of
   nodes. Safety does **not** depend on every node arming; it depends on the
   coupling — assert no honest node releases a coerced partial regardless of how
   many armed. Drop the reachable-armed set below `t` → lockdown-only (no sweep, no
   theft) → recovery. (Contrast with the OLD framing "propagation arms every
   reachable node": that all-or-nothing arming is the timing story, not the safety.)
8. **process-kill / reboot-death**: kill an armed node (destroy its tmpfs
   deployment) before T → surviving armed set (≥ t) still fires the sweep; drop
   below t → lockdown-only; the killed node holds no keys/schedule/partials and
   cannot restart/rejoin (RAMDISK reboot-death). Also cover the lockdown latch
   surviving a PROCESS restart but dying on machine reboot (V0-4a durability).
9. **coverage/feerate/package fire-time failures** on live regtest → the sweep
   does not fire, Lockdown at T still happens (unconditional), funds recoverable
   via V0-10.
10. **recovery demonstration**: after a lockdown-only outcome, exercise the V0-10
    timelocked recovery spend (time-warp past the relative lock) → funds move via
    recovery. This makes "freeze + lockdown → recovery" a demonstrated exit.

## Tests / acceptance
- Each scenario runs on a co-located regtest federation (`n = 2t−1`) and asserts:
  no theft path (funds only ever reach vault/hot/escape/recovery, never an attacker
  address the user didn't author), the SAFETY track held (freeze + unconditional
  Lockdown at T), and — for the probe/timing scenarios — silence (indistinguishable
  observables under both pins, including the Hot-budget refusal path).
- The arm-split scenario asserts the **coupling** specifically: enumerate the
  honest nodes that emitted a partial for the coerced carrier and show every one of
  them also froze it (releasable-partial count ≤ t−1). A test that only counts
  "how many armed" is asserting the wrong property — it must show no signed-but-
  unfrozen honest partial exists.
- The Hot-budget scenario asserts the numeric bound: over-cap refused pre-signing
  at every node; window sum capped; released/expired reservations returned.
- A scorecard-style exit (like `demo first-light`) communicates pass/fail per
  scenario; the whole harness exits 0 when all safety assertions hold.
- fmt/clippy -D warnings/test --workspace pass; `demo first-light` still exits 0.

## Scope guard
- Touch `crates/vault-cli/` (attack/demo subcommand) + integration test modules;
  MINIMAL `crates/vault-node/` changes only if a test seam is genuinely needed
  (prefer driving the real daemon). Do NOT change the duress state machine
  (V0-4b-core), the channel, the release-gate, policy, or the Hot budget ledger —
  DRIVE them adversarially. If a scenario cannot be demonstrated without changing
  production safety code, STOP and flag it rather than weakening the mechanism to
  make a test pass.
- Non-goals: multi-VPS attack range (Approach B, later), the full v1 nine-scenario
  playbook — build the ADR-0012 denial-residual set + the coupling (arm-split) +
  the Hot-budget bound + reboot-death + recovery demonstration. No new production
  safety mechanism; no durable ledger (RAMDISK only). Size budget: a bounded
  harness over the existing daemon, not a re-implementation of the federation.
- Do not run `rb-lite`, signal your own process tree, or touch `.rb-lite/`,
  `.ralph-burning/`, `.git/ralph-burning-live/`, `.beads/`.

## Acceptance criteria
- fmt/clippy -D warnings/test --workspace pass; `demo first-light` exits 0.
- The harness demonstrates, on live regtest (`n = 2t−1`), freeze+lockdown→recovery
  with no theft path and silence to an outside attacker across: the ADR-0012 denial
  residuals; the **coupling** (a coordinator that actively splits the carrier from
  the signature still cannot assemble a coerced quorum); the **Hot-budget bound**
  (the censorship residual capped to one window's budget, refused pre-signing);
  reboot-death; and recovery. The wrench-attack answer is empirically demonstrated,
  and it demonstrates the mechanism the 2026-07-20 review settled — the release-gate
  + coupling — not the receipt count.
close_reason: V0-4b adversarial duress harness merged (0592aa9): 13/13 live regtest, dual-model reviewed clean (codex+Fable both MERGE), and it uncovered+fixed a production silence-oracle bug (confirm_carrier commit/arm split). Last duress bead.

title: Vault migration and rotation tooling: the routine response to a patch, a dead node, or a key change
description:
FILED 2026-07-30 from the codex+Fable bead review (BOTH reviewers). Two beads CONSUME a migration flow that no bead BUILDS.

THE GAP: btc-policy-s12 must time 'one migration-to-patch performed for real' and hits a wall at its own VERIFY. btc-policy-nju drills 'migrate a vault end-to-end'. ADR-0005 makes migration the ROUTINE patch procedure -- sealed nodes have no upgrade-in-place, so patching a node means rotating the vault. docs/UPGRADE-AND-ROTATION-POLICY.md states outright that no tooling exists. DESIGN.md sketches the rotate flow (escape-class sweep to the escape wallet, then fund a successor vault at leisure) and stops there.

DELIVER: (a) create and verify a SUCCESSOR VAULT -- a fresh setup ceremony whose output is checked against the predecessor's parameters, so a migration cannot silently weaken the vault (a shorter timelock, a smaller federation, a reused key); (b) MOVE THE FUNDS by the correct permitted path -- an escape-class sweep through the normal path, never a recovery-branch spend, and never a path that requires the duress subsystem; (c) RETIRE the predecessor: mark deposit addresses dead, record which secrets are now burned, and make reuse of the old descriptor detectable; (d) KEY MATERIAL RULES -- ADR-0015 item 2b requires FRESH material at stage 6 because everything provisioned under the waiver sat inside one provider's console reach, so the tooling must be able to assert 'no key in the successor appeared in the predecessor'; (e) an AUDITABLE RECORD of what moved, when, and from which vault to which.

CONSTRAINT: migration is the response to a COMPROMISE SIGNAL as well as to a patch, so it must work when the predecessor federation is degraded -- some nodes dead, one node suspected. State the minimum live-node count the flow needs and what happens below it.

VERIFY: a full migration on regtest from a 5-node vault to a fresh one, with a deliberately dead node in the predecessor; the successor-verification step REFUSES a successor with a shorter timelock or a reused key; the audit record is sufficient to reconstruct what happened without the operator's memory.

title: attack escape-class-sequences fails on main — the 'attack 16/16' gate cannot currently pass
description:
FILED 2026-07-31 while draining btc-policy-6nq. The adversarial harness reports 15/16, and MANY beads list 'attack 16/16' as an acceptance gate (6nq, 6nv, and the full-matrix requirement in gbw and 9y5.8). That gate cannot currently be met on main, so every bead carrying it is either unclosable or will be closed against a weakened bar.

ESTABLISHED BY TEST, not inferred:
- FAILS on feat/6nq-confirmed-escape-invalidation.
- FAILS identically on origin/main (eb916ff) -- so it is NOT caused by the 6nq change.
- FAILS identically at a1814c6, which predates the btc-policy-9y5.7 escape RBF fee-bump ladder -- so the ladder is not the cause either. It is older than that.
- Reproduces deterministically: three consecutive runs, three different txids, the same failure and the same ~190s runtime. Not intermittent within a run.
- The other 15 scenarios PASS, including every duress, reorg, lockdown and recovery assertion.

THE FAILURE: 'transaction <txid> never reached the mempool or a block' -- the generic settlement-wait helper at crates/vault-cli/src/attack.rs:2058 giving up on a transaction.

HYPOTHESIS, NOT YET CONFIRMED -- test before believing it: this scenario is unusually timing-sensitive and machine-speed-dependent. escape_class_sequences (attack.rs:4900) calls calibrate_pin_cost() and then runs 16 Argon2-heavy samples, and its own comments say 'at the calibration ceiling the 16 Argon2-heavy samples below can take tens of seconds; T must not land mid-loop'. It uses hold_secs 120 / duress_delay_secs 90. The box these runs happened on is SHARED, MULTI-TENANT and was under sustained heavy load (a 6-hour rb-lite run plus review agents). A calibration that adapts to a loaded machine, combined with a fixed settlement window, is a plausible mechanism -- but 'plausible' is where this stops. It could equally be a real defect in escape-class settlement.

INVESTIGATE IN THIS ORDER: (1) re-run on an IDLE box and see whether it passes -- that single result decides between 'harness fragility' and 'real bug', and everything else depends on it; (2) if it passes idle, the bug is the scenario's timing assumptions, and the fix is to make the settlement window derive from the measured calibration rather than from a constant; (3) if it fails idle, this is an escape-class settlement defect on the CROWN-JEWEL fire path and the priority goes up, not down; (4) bisect properly to find where it broke -- it is older than a1814c6 and nobody appears to have noticed, which is its own finding about how often the full suite actually gets run.

DO NOT 'fix' this by loosening the assertion or marking the scenario ignored. A gate that many beads cite, quietly weakened, is worse than a gate that visibly fails.

VERIFY: the scenario passes 3 consecutive runs on an otherwise idle machine; if the fix is to the harness, it must be derived from measurement rather than a bigger constant; the root cause is recorded in the bead so the next person does not repeat this bisect.

DIAGNOSED 2026-07-31 (codex + Fable, both independently, same read-verified mechanism). HYPOTHESIS (A) CONFIRMED -- THIS IS NOT A SETTLEMENT DEFECT.

DECISIVE EVIDENCE: this scenario PASSED in 286s during rb-lite round 7 on this same box, on the code now merged -- 16/16 scenarios held (/tmp/rb-6nq-run/gate-attack-all-round7.log:111, calibration chose one Argon2 = 199ms at 28131 KiB). A deterministic settlement-logic defect cannot pass. It is load-sensitive.

THE MECHANISM, read-verified at line numbers by both reviewers: an escape-class spend fires IMMEDIATELY -- FireWindow { fire_at: now, deadline: min(expiry, now + combine_slack_secs) } (lib.rs:5337-5343, 5433-5438) -- and this scenario uses the minimum combine_slack_secs of 20s (attack.rs:386). Inside those 20 seconds the ENTIRE pipeline must complete: carrier fan-out to holder quorum, each honest node performing 3 memory-hard Argon2 evaluations AT THE CALIBRATED COST (up to 128 MiB), partial exchange, combine, package check, and broadcast -- with release, finalize and broadcast each re-checking the window at send time (channel.rs:4170-4173, 4325-4327, 4394-4401). Missing it is PERMANENT: the candidate can never broadcast afterwards, so the 45s wait_for_tx cannot recover it. A HOT spend does not have this exposure -- quorum forms during its 120s Hold and only the light release/combine/broadcast must fit the 20s window. escape_class_sequences is the ONLY scenario combining immediate-fire + single-node ingress (attack.rs:4987) + calibrated pin cost.

EVERY LEGITIMATE-REFUSAL MECHANISM WAS ELIMINATED by reading each gate: fire-time coverage and the panic-feerate floor apply only to the ARMED sweep (is_armed_escape requires armed.active && sweep_active, both false under the normal pin); the package is a singleton over confirmed inputs; no coin conflict exists among A/B/C/D before the duress T; per-peer quota is 600/min and not overridden; fee is ~85 sat/vB against a 1 sat/vB floor; coverage is 99.17% normal / 99.995% duress against a 95% precondition. 'Broadcast but unobserved' is also excluded -- wait_for_tx polls mempool AND chain every 250ms.

WHICH TRANSACTION: reasoned, NOT observed (both reviewers agree, both flag it as inference): the immediate NORMAL-pin escape-class spend of coin A, at attack.rs:5022. codex correctly notes the wiretap control at attack.rs:895 aliases to a similar ~190s and cannot be excluded from the artifact alone, because the error message is generic.

MY EARLIER BISECT WAS INVALID AND IS WITHDRAWN. I reported this as 'failing identically at eb916ff and a1814c6, so it predates the 9y5.7 RBF ladder'. That reasoning does not hold: every one of those runs happened on a box under sustained heavy load (a 6-hour rb-lite run plus concurrent review agents). I was measuring the load, not the commit. There is no evidence this is old, and the round-7 pass is evidence it is not.

THE FIX (neither reviewer would accept a raised constant, and neither should this bead):
(1) DERIVE combine_slack_secs from the calibration rather than pinning the 20s minimum. It is already a per-scenario Setup field (attack.rs:350, 389). Scale duress_delay_secs with it, since control_separation_secs and the no-op-control margins consume it. The scenario ALREADY owns this pattern -- its sampling-window guard (attack.rs:5147-5163) derives a budget from measurement and fails loudly -- it just never applied it to the immediate legs. Note its headroom comment guards the WRONG risk: it worries about T landing mid-loop while the unguarded budget is [ingress, ingress+combine_slack].
(2) ADD THE MISSING GUARD: refuse at the top, the way 5154 already does, when the measured per-carrier pipeline cost does not comfortably fit combine_slack_secs -- turning a silent wait_for_tx death into an attributed calibration error.
(3) NAME EACH WAIT. The generic 'transaction X never reached the mempool or a block' is a real diagnostic defect: it made the failing transaction unattributable and is why the answer above is inference. At minimum: 'wiretap control', 'normal A', 'duress B', 'duress residual'.
(4) codex's alternative, worth considering: split into a fixture-cost four-coin sequence proving A/B settlement and the no-op/residual semantics, plus a calibrated silence probe for body/size/latency uniformity. The 16 expensive samples are not needed to establish the four-coin chain semantics.

SAME-CLASS EXPOSURE: two_spend_probe is the only other calibrate_pin_cost caller (attack.rs:3957) and shares the fixed 120/90s windows -- same fragility class, currently passing. hold_expiry_race's WRENCH_LEAD_SECS = 4 is machine-timing-sensitive in the same spirit.

WHY IT WENT UNNOTICED: see btc-policy-9yf. CI has never run, 44/44 failures at job startup. There was no watcher.

STILL TRUE, AND STILL THE POINT: under either hypothesis the scenario's actual claim -- that an escape-class spend is pin-uniform, verified on-chain because the acknowledgement cannot distinguish the two -- does not get verified on a loaded machine, because the run dies at a precondition. Fixing the window is what makes the silence assertion reachable.

UPDATE 2026-08-01 — CONFIRMED PASSING ON CI, and the fragility class is broader than this bead.
escape-class-sequences PASSED on CI run 30666082498 at 272s, independently confirming the load-sensitivity diagnosis on hardware that is not this box. But on run 30683094069 it FAILED again with a DIFFERENT failure — a timing-oracle assertion at 317.6ms skew, where run 1 measured 2.27ms on identical code. So this scenario has now failed two distinct ways for two distinct reasons: settlement-window starvation under load (this bead) and noise-dominated timing measurement (bead btc-policy-c9r). Fixing the combine window will not make it green; both need fixing.
notes:
HYPOTHESIS (A) NOW CONFIRMED ON A DEDICATED RUNNER -- 2026-08-03. This bead's own step (1) said one
result would decide between 'harness fragility' and 'real bug': does it pass on an IDLE box? GitHub
Actions supplies exactly that, and it passes.

- CI run 30775557224 (head 2da998c), launch-gate log: `PASS escape-class-sequences 273s`, and the
  suite ends `16/16 scenarios held`.
- Six consecutive ci.yml runs are green with a ~47-minute launch gate each, so this is not a
  one-off. (See btc-policy-9yf's note: CI only started executing again around 2026-07-31.)
- Consistent with this bead's existing DECISIVE EVIDENCE paragraph, where the scenario passed in
  286s during an rb-lite round on the shared box.

FURTHER, ON THE LOADED SHARED BOX ITSELF: during the btc-policy-9zs rb-lite run (2026-08-03,
9 rounds over 15h) `attack all` completed 16/16 with escape-class-sequences PASSING on at least
three separate rounds (r5, r7, r8 gate logs in /tmp/rb-9zs-run/), unprompted, with the implementer
explicitly flagging it as 'report rather than tune'. So the scenario is passing more often on this
box than when this bead was filed -- which weakens 'EXPECTED red on a loaded box' as a standing
assumption and means a future red should be INVESTIGATED, not waved through.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE: the root cause is still the timing coupling this bead diagnosed --
immediate-fire escape (FireWindow fire_at = now) against the minimum combine_slack_secs of 20s,
inside which the whole carrier fan-out, three calibrated Argon2 evaluations per honest node, partial
exchange, combine, package check and broadcast must fit. That coupling is unchanged; the scenario
passes when the box is fast enough and fails when it is not. The bead's step (2) fix still stands:
derive the settlement window from the MEASURED calibration rather than a constant.

DO NOT close this as 'works now'. The correct close is either the measurement-derived window, or an
explicit decision that the launch gate runs on CI only and every bead citing 'attack 16/16' means
CI's result, stated wherever that gate is cited.

title: Rollout stage 4: sealed hosts on signet — MEASURE node attrition
description:
Rollout ladder STAGE 4 ONLY (docs/ROLLOUT-PLAN.md). Stage 5 is btc-policy-qbt; this bead was split on 2026-07-29 so the nju decision could depend on stage-4 data instead of preceding it. Five machines, ONE provider, hosts SEALED per ADR-0005 in full (no SSH, no administrative path, no upgrade-in-place, reboot kills the node), SIGNET. Runs the full two-vault Path suite.

Operates under ADR-0015's test-only waiver of ADR-0009: one provider is a correlation class holding quorum, and sealing does NOT fix that — ADR-0005 concedes a VPS is never fully sealed against its provider (console and rescue access remain).

THE POINT OF THIS STAGE IS MEASUREMENT, not just hardening. Sealing makes patching a node cost a whole vault rotation and gives a dead node no remedy. Whether that is livable is an EMPIRICAL question, and stage 4 answers it cheaply — signet funds. Record: how long five sealed nodes actually survive untouched; what killed them; and the true wall-clock and ceremony cost of one migration-to-patch performed for real, not estimated.

Part of the answer is predictable and should not be presented as an open question: commodity cloud providers reboot and live-migrate VMs on their own schedule, and under ADR-0007 every such event is a dead node. Expect attrition to be dominated by provider maintenance. Measure the MAGNITUDE, not the direction.

THIS STAGE'S DATA DECIDES btc-policy-nju (immutable one-shot nodes vs recoverable hardware-backed nodes with a durable monotonic Lockdown latch). The graph reflects that: s12 BLOCKS nju, and nju blocks qbt (stage 5, mainnet). Do not resolve nju before this stage produces numbers.

DEPENDS ON btc-policy-nwd (the ADR-0005 sealed NODE image — note this is NOT btc-policy-4y3, which is coordinator-host hardening, a different machine and a different threat), btc-policy-azn (on a sealed host /healthz is the ONLY observability, so a node silently pinned to full scans is exactly the health signal this stage must see), and stages 2-3 (btc-policy-4wx).

VERIFY: full Path suite on both vaults; an attrition record with real durations and causes; one migration-to-patch actually performed and timed; the data handed to nju in a form that can decide it.

title: Escape fee ladder derivation: compose and user-sign the rungs the sealed escape_bump_max_fee_pct admits
description:
FOLLOW-ON to btc-policy-mby, split out during the 2026-08-05 owner grilling. mby seals the POLICY
(the `escape_bump_max_fee_pct` manifest field, its Ceremony input, and the validation; btc-policy-wdu owns the combined timelock/ladder prompt); this bead
builds the BEHAVIOUR that consumes it. Decisions and rationale: docs/adr/0016.

## What exists already

`escape_fee_ladder` (crates/vault-cli/src/fed.rs) ALREADY composes the ladder for the demo path:
rungs at ESCAPE_BUMP_MULTIPLIERS = [4, 16, 64] x base fee, funded from the LARGEST escape output
(not the last -- a Fable 9y5.7 review finding), dropping any rung that exceeds
ESCAPE_BUMP_MAX_FEE_PCT of swept value, would leave a sub-dust output (ESCAPE_BUMP_MIN_OUTPUT_SAT =
10_000), or fails to clear the node's incremental-relay minimum. The node accepts an empty ladder
(`if bumps.is_empty() { return Ok(()); }`). It does NOT refuse a ladder on an escape-class spend:
the only ladder gates are the length cap (lib.rs:5495), `ensure_escape_ladder` -- whose
`self_paired` flag is COMMITMENT-ID EQUALITY, not class -- and per-bump `verify_escape`. A valid
escape-class request (distinct disjoint residual, per lib.rs:5849) carrying a ladder passes all
three. So "an escape-class spend produces no ladder" is a CLIENT-SIDE CONVENTION this bead may
adopt, not a node-enforced rule; if it is adopted, say so and do not assert the node enforces it.

So this is mostly WIRING, not design. The work is making the operator CLI use it against a SEALED
vault rather than an in-process fixture.

## Deliver

(a) Replace the hardcoded ESCAPE_BUMP_MAX_FEE_PCT with the SEALED manifest value mby adds. At 0 the
    ladder is empty and the Operator approves exactly two transactions PER SpendRequest (a
    RefreshRequest presents one) -- that path must stay first
    class, not an edge case.
(b) Use the operator CLI signing seam contract owned by mby: hand off the spend, mandatory Escape,
    and composed `escape_bumps` together for user authorization. mby defines and implements the
    seam; this bead only populates the rungs through it.
(c) Derive replacement-rung fees from the base Escape composed by mby. mby owns the production
    feerate source and must produce a base admissible against the sealed `escape_feerate_floor`;
    this bead consumes that base fee and applies the fixed multipliers and drop rules. Do not choose
    a second, independent feerate source for the rungs.
(d) Surface what was composed before the user signs: how many rungs, at what fees, what share of the
    swept value the top rung pays. An Operator authorizing rungs they cannot see is the same
    unlabelled-PSBT problem the seam's shape was chosen to avoid.

## Verify

- A vault sealed at 0 produces, FOR A SpendRequest, an empty ladder and exactly TWO TRANSACTIONS
  PRESENTED for approval
  (not two signatures — a multi-input PSBT takes one per input, so signatures are not a stable
  observable; see ADR-0016). Assert the COUNT,
  not just that it works -- the two-transaction default is the decision this whole thread turned on.
- A vault sealed at a non-zero value, ON A FIXTURE CHOSEN TO ADMIT ONE, produces rungs whose top fee
  is within the sealed ceiling, and every rung is ACCEPTED by a live node at ingress (not merely
  composed). Do NOT assert that a non-zero ceiling always yields rungs: for a small swept value, a
  high base fee, or a large relay-size minimum, every 4x/16x/64x candidate can breach the ceiling,
  the dust floor, or the relay increment even at a generous percentage. A valid non-zero
  configuration that still yields an EMPTY ladder is a supported outcome and needs its own case.
- A ladder composed against a sealed ceiling near the node's own guard is REFUSED BY SETUP, not
  discovered at T. (mby owns that validation; this bead proves it holds end to end.)
- DECIDE, then test, whether a VALID escape-class spend may carry a ladder. A valid one has a
  DISTINCT DISJOINT residual Escape (lib.rs:5849), and that residual is a real delayed sweep that
  nodes will happily fee-bump. Be precise about WHAT would lose bumping: the clawback SPEND itself
  fires immediately and is registered with an empty `escape_bumps` regardless, so omitting the
  ladder costs it nothing. What loses bumping is the DISTINCT RESIDUAL Escape, whose fire window is
  the delayed one. So the real question is whether that residual needs rungs under duress -- decide
  that, rather than assuming the blanket rule is either safe or harmful. Only the SELF-PAIRED shape genuinely has nothing to bump, and that shape is refused outright
  anyway. Whatever is decided, assert on what the CLI composes -- the node enforces no such rule.


## Documentation consistency

Correct `docs/OPERATIONS-RUNBOOK.md` §6's coercion procedure in this delivery. Only freeze plus
Lockdown-at-T are unconditional; the node merely ATTEMPTS the best-effort Escape sweep at T, and
coverage, the feerate floor, `testmempoolaccept`, or non-confirmation can leave the funds frozen for
Recovery. Step 2 must check which outcome occurred rather than presume the coins moved. This is a
wording correction to the existing two-track mechanism, not a new fallback or operator ceremony.

## Non-goals

Changing the multipliers, the funding-output choice, or the drop rules -- those were settled by
btc-policy-9y5.7 and its review. Changing the node-side rung SELECTION at T (ADR-0012 owns it).

title: README.md describes a project that no longer exists: single co-signer + CTV upgrade path, contradicting DESIGN/CONTEXT — and it is the public front page
description:
FOUND 2026-08-04 by the multi-reviewer-loop's cross-file consistency pass while reviewing
btc-policy-9zs. PRE-EXISTING and unrelated to that bead — README.md predates the 2026-07-13
redesign and was never edited. Filed rather than fixed inline because rewriting the project's
public self-description is an editorial decision, not a consistency touch-up.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN ORDINARY DOC DRIFT: this repository was made PUBLIC on 2026-07-31.
README.md is the first thing a visitor reads, and it currently describes a different system than
the one in the tree.

THREE CONTRADICTIONS, each verified against the authoritative side:

1. ARCHITECTURE. README.md:3 says "an isolated policy co-signer" — singular. CONTEXT.md:3 says
   "a user hardware key plus a t-of-n federation of policy-enforcing signer nodes". docs/DESIGN.md:13-15
   names the single-co-signer shape ("IDEA.md's original 2-of-2 design — one host compromise away
   from useless") as THE FLAW the federation exists to fix. The README therefore advertises the
   design the project explicitly abandoned.

2. COVENANTS. README.md:3 promises "a future upgrade path to CTV/CCV covenant vaults".
   docs/DESIGN.md:259 says "**CTV/covenants are out of scope.** No covenant backend seam, no
   covenant-readiness requirement: this is a soft vault on today's consensus rules, full stop."
   These cannot both stand.

3. AUTHORITY. README.md:5 says "See IDEA.md for the full design document". CONTEXT.md:3 designates
   docs/DESIGN.md plus ADR-0012/0013 as the authoritative design documents. A new contributor
   following the README lands on the superseded document.

THE DESIGN/CONTEXT/ADR SIDE IS CORRECT in all three. The fix is to README.md.

DECIDE, do not just patch prose: what is IDEA.md for now? Options are (a) keep it as a historical
record and say so at its top, (b) delete it, or (c) fold anything still live into docs/DESIGN.md.
Leaving it unmarked while the README points at it as authoritative is what produced this.

VERIFY: README.md's opening paragraph describes the t-of-n federation, the user key, and the
timelocked recovery path; makes no covenant promise; and points at docs/DESIGN.md. Then grep the
repo for any other reference to "co-signer" (singular), "CTV", "CCV", or IDEA.md-as-authoritative
and confirm each remaining hit is either historical-and-marked or correct.

title: Duress incident procedure needs human security review, not another AI pass
description:
The duress incident procedure in docs/OPERATIONS-RUNBOOK.md ("The user was coerced (duress PIN
used)") was rewritten SEVEN consecutive times during the ADR-0016 review loop (passes 26-33). Every
single round, the next review found a NEW defect in the freshly written text, several
safety-relevant. This bead exists because that pattern is the finding, not the individual defects.

WHAT THE ROUNDS FOUND, in order -- each introduced by the previous round's fix:
- assumed the sweep always lands, so the no-sweep branch abandoned a vault still holding the funds
- stated recovery maturity as one deadline when the BIP68 lock is per-UTXO and reset by refresh
- sent the operator to read `older(n)` from `manifest.json` (frozen constant; not a knob)
- then OVERCORRECTED to "it is NOT in manifest.json", which is also false (setup.rs:1621, 1633)
- deleted the "Once safe" coercion gate and replaced it with urgency wording, so the procedure told
  a possibly-still-captive victim to run a ceremony generating the new vault's keys and PINs
- serialized the new vault behind up to 180 days of straggler maturity, parking swept funds in a
  single-key escape wallet
- told the operator to verify Lockdown by SUBMITTING a spend or refresh -- which on a
  not-locked-down node can release a refresh and RESET the recovery timelock the procedure depends
  on two steps later
- claimed "nothing below is time-critical", false when the carrier never reached t: nothing armed,
  a coerced hot spend can still finalize, and hold_secs has no positive lower bound

All of the above are FIXED (commits 1c9c9b8..f2ab677 plus this one). What is NOT resolved:

1. THIS SECTION NEEDS A HUMAN SECURITY REVIEWER. Seven-plus AI rewrites each destabilized
   safety-critical incident text; several introduced NEW defects while fixing old ones (a deleted
   coercion gate, funds parked in a single-key wallet for months, a verification step that could
   reset the recovery timelock, and a Lockdown check forgeable by the very adversary the section is
   about). This is concrete evidence for btc-policy-9y5.8 deliverable (3) -- an external HUMAN
   review that this repo's own codex+Fable panels cannot satisfy. Do not close this bead with
   another AI pass.

2. DO NOT RESTATE ADR-0016 HERE. Earlier revisions of this bead listed the open ADR-0016 questions
   inline and went stale three separate times as those questions were decided -- twice telling a
   future implementer to do something the ADR had already established was impossible. The ADR is
   the authority: read docs/adr/0016-the-escape-fee-ladder-is-sealed-and-opt-in.md §3a and §4 for
   the current state of the preimage, protocol-version and ceremony-atomicity decisions, and
   btc-policy-mby for what ships. Nothing about them is a closing requirement for THIS bead beyond
   (a) below. (This is the duplicated-normative-content problem filed as btc-policy-0ip, in
   miniature, in a bead I created.)

WHY THIS KEEPS HAPPENING, and it is not only reviewer noise: the runbook describes operations that
DO NOT EXIST. There is no sealed-vault receive, balance, or spend command, and no operational code
reads manifest.json (R9). Steps 3-6 are prose about a system one layer more finished than the one
built -- exactly what btc-policy-mby's WHY already records. Prose describing unimplemented
operations has no implementation to be checked against, which is why each careful rewrite produced
a new plausible-but-wrong instruction. A banner saying so was added at the head of the section, but
the real fix is mby + en1 landing, after which this procedure should be re-derived FROM the shipped
commands rather than polished further.

VERIFY: (a) a human security reviewer has read the section end to end and signed off; (b) the section agrees with whatever ADR-0016 says at review time -- checked then, not asserted here; (c) once mby and en1 land, every step names a
real command and the banner comes off; (d) a dry run -- someone who did not write it follows the
procedure on signet against a deliberately partial sweep and reports where they got stuck.

title: Rollout stages 6-8: provider diversity, sealing, then the capped mainnet soak
description:
Rollout ladder STAGES 6-8 (docs/ROLLOUT-PLAN.md). Stage 9 is btc-policy-yt7, split out on 2026-07-29 so the bq6/gbw gates have an unambiguous home. Stage 6: many hosting PROVIDERS, open, signet — this is where ADR-0009's no-correlation-class-reaches-quorum requirement first becomes true of the deployment rather than only of the design. Stage 7: many providers, sealed, signet (attrition measurement continues under diversity). Stage 8: many providers, sealed, MAINNET — and keep it running for a while, with the Survivor vault as the observation subject. (Stage 9 — the full Path suite on that exact configuration, then the freeze for external review #2 — is btc-policy-yt7.)

WHY 8 AND 9 ARE SEPARATE: stage 8 answers 'does it survive', stage 9 answers 'does it still do everything'. A vault that has run untouched for weeks and then cannot complete a clawback or a recovery has failed in the way that matters most, and running the destructive suite first would end the observation before it began.

REVIEW #2 must target a frozen reproducible build (btc-policy-gbw), not a moving branch, and is NOT satisfied by automated review — correlated AI panels, including this repo's own codex+Fable loops, are explicitly excluded (docs/THREAT-MODEL.md R7).

DEPENDS ON stages 4-5, btc-policy-gbw.

VERIFY: provider/region/OS diversity documented and attested rather than asserted; the long-run observation has recorded duration and incidents; full Path suite green on the stage-9 configuration; review #2 findings remediated and re-tested before stage 10 (public alpha).

Dependencies:
  -> btc-policy-qbt (blocks) - Rollout stage 5: sealed hosts on mainnet (gated on the nju lifecycle decision)

Dependents:
  <- btc-policy-yt7 (blocks) - Rollout stage 9 freeze: full Path suite on the real configuration, then external review #2
ADDED 2026-07-29 (Fable second-pass review): STAGE 6 IS THE FIRST TIME NODES SIT ON PUBLIC NETWORKS. Every rung to date keeps them on private or single-provider infrastructure. THREAT-MODEL R1 records that GET /pending is an UNAUTHENTICATED spend-activity timing surface — any network peer holding no keys can infer that a /sign was processed, including one that was refused. That residual was ranked when nodes were unreachable; stage 6 changes its exposure and nothing has re-ranked it. Add to this stage's VERIFY: decide and record whether /pending (and /healthz, /events) are exposed publicly, firewalled to the coordinator, or authenticated — before the nodes are reachable, not after. The imb CARE note already requires re-analysing the accepted per-link partition attack for real links; this is the same class of inherited-assumption check.

NOTE ON SCOPE: this bead is stages 6-8 only. Stage 9 (the full Path suite on the shipping configuration, then the freeze for external review #2) is btc-policy-yt7, which carries the bq6 and gbw gates.

Dependencies:
  -> btc-policy-bq6 (blocks) - Hardware-signing path for the user key (PSBT hand-off)
  -> btc-policy-qbt (blocks) - Rollout stage 5: sealed hosts on mainnet (gated on the nju lifecycle decision)

Dependents:
  <- btc-policy-yt7 (blocks) - Rollout stage 9 freeze: full Path suite on the real configuration, then external review #2


WITHDRAWN 2026-07-30 (owner decision: hardware signing is optional and postponed). An addendum here previously said 'HARDWARE SIGNING IS EXERCISED HERE, NOT AT THE FREEZE' and added btc-policy-bq6 as a blocker of this bead, on the argument that stage 8's soak would otherwise exercise a spend path stage 9 replaces. That argument is real and is recorded on bq6 itself, but it does not justify blocking stages 6-8: ADR-0015 lines 86-95 deliberately do NOT require hardware signing for the capped rungs, and the dust cap is the stated mitigation. THE bq6 EDGE IS REMOVED. bq6 gates btc-policy-yt7 (the stage-9 freeze) and nothing earlier. If hardware signing does land before stage 7, prefer exercising it on a signet rung with a FRESH hardware-generated user key rather than importing one previously exposed as software -- but that is an opportunity, not a gate.

title: Split a no-tokio vault-core crate: machine-check the dependency direction (NOT a compile-time lock guarantee)
description:
The strongest possible enforcement of the sync/async boundary is a crate that cannot violate it: a vault-core with NO tokio, axum, or reqwest in its Cargo.toml literally cannot await, spawn, or park a runtime worker. This bead does that. It is sequenced AFTER btc-policy-wqd (which writes the rule down and fixes the live sites) because the ADR fixes the boundary in writing first, and after btc-policy-imb where practical, because the federation-runtime work rewrites the ~300-line transport that would otherwise be extracted twice.

THE MEASUREMENT that makes this attractive. Production async is concentrated, not smeared: chain.rs (5,958 lines) has ZERO; pin.rs (1,367) ZERO; nodekey/replay/prop_*/ingress_trace (~1,960) ZERO; channel.rs is 19,636 lines of synchronous state machine with the ENTIRE async surface in four functions at lines 5119-5420 (send_envelope, retry_loop, try_endpoints, retry_message_until) which acquire NO locks at all - they read only peer_bases, peer_ids, max_response_bytes, all immutable manifest-derived config (channel.rs:4695/4973/4983); lib.rs (9,887) confines async to the drivers, fire_tick, and fan-out; watchtower.rs's async is one function (541-575). Roughly 38,000 lines of sync core against 3,000 of async shell.

BLOCKERS THAT MUST BE CLEARED FIRST - the naive split does NOT compile. Both reviewers found these independently in the 2026-08-02 design review, and the original plan's claim that "tests move with their modules so cfg(test) survives" is FALSE.
1. nodekey.rs:369 - public_identity (PRODUCTION, not test) calls crate::channel::ceremony::channel_pubkey, and channel.rs stays. nodekey cannot move until that helper is relocated.
2. prop_decoder.rs and prop_mutation.rs are #[cfg(test)] MODULES (lib.rs:41-45) importing Node, handle_sign, handle_channel_body, channel::fixture::Fixture, and test_support (prop_decoder.rs:40-48, prop_mutation.rs:40-42) - all staying in vault-node. They cannot move; that is ~1,250 lines removed from the claimed moving set.
3. A dependency crate is NEVER compiled with cfg(test), so cfg(test) items in MOVING modules that are used by STAYING tests all break: chain::mock::MockBackend (gated at chain.rs:2239) is used across lib.rs tests from 7314 and inside Node's own cfg(test) chain_backend_override initializer (lib.rs:1885); pin::test_util::CountingEvaluator is used at lib.rs:9266/9326 and channel.rs:12403; CarrierKdf::total_derivations() is called from lib.rs:2341. FIX: a `test-support` cargo feature on vault-core, or relocate the mocks. Decide which and say why.
4. Numerous moving APIs are pub(crate) - SignState (replay.rs:38), PinEvaluator (pin.rs:80). Cross-crate use needs a deliberate public API, not a blanket pub.
5. watchtower.rs must be split INTERNALLY: the scan and AlertQueue move, the driver (541-575) stays in the shell, and the driver's tests cannot simply follow the scanning core.

CONFIRMED SAFE: ingress_trace is untouched by this split - all references are in lib.rs (36) and channel.rs (9), both of which stay, so its #[cfg(test)] gate survives and does NOT need to become a feature flag. That was the main worry and it is unfounded.

HONEST LIMIT, state it rather than overselling. Every runtime-worker lock violation found so far lives in server.rs, lib.rs, and channel.rs - NONE of them in the modules this bead moves. The moving set is already 100% synchronous. So this delivers organizational clarity and a compile-enforced boundary over code where the rule has never been broken; it does NOT retroactively enforce anything. The enforcement value for lib.rs and channel.rs comes from btc-policy-wqd's CoreMutex assertion, not from here. A later bead can move the channel state machine once imb has settled the transport.

DELIVER: vault-core with no tokio/axum/reqwest; chain.rs, pin.rs, replay.rs, the watchtower scan + AlertQueue, Error (lib.rs:82), and nodekey.rs once blocker 1 is cleared. A test-support feature or relocated mocks per blocker 3. A deliberate public API per blocker 4. vault-node depends on vault-core. CoreMutex must live in vault-core (three of the declaring files move) and export its marker API to vault-node's seam - a thread-local needs no tokio.

GATES: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; full workspace tests with NO test deleted or weakened to accommodate the split (a test that had to be dropped is a blocker, not a detail - report it); all three demos; attack all (btc-policy-rt0 EXPECTED red).

=================================================================
AMENDED 2026-08-02 after a two-model review of this bead's text. THE TITLE AND OPENING CLAIM ARE
FALSE - see C1. Retitled accordingly.
=================================================================

C1. [P1, CODEX] "A no-tokio crate makes parking a runtime worker a COMPILE ERROR" IS FALSE, and it
contradicts this bead's own honest-limit paragraph three sentences later. A crate with no tokio
dependency can still block a caller's runtime thread with Mutex::lock, blocking socket I/O, or
sleep - and chain.rs contains BOTH production mutexes and blocking TCP I/O (chain.rs:429,
chain.rs:2201). The crate boundary prevents the CORE from spelling tokio APIs; it cannot enforce
WHERE shell code calls synchronous core APIs. What the split actually buys: the core cannot await,
spawn, or acquire a tokio primitive, and the dependency direction is machine-checked. Enforcement of
"no std lock on a runtime worker" comes from btc-policy-wqd's CoreMutex assertion, NOT from here.
The honest-limit paragraph was right; the headline was the claim-outruns-mechanism defect this repo
keeps shipping - third instance in these beads' own lineage.

C2. [P1, BOTH] BLOCKER 3 IS INCOMPLETE, and one missed member is the SILENCE gate's own dependency.
Additional cfg(test) items in MOVING modules used by STAYING tests: SignState::shape (replay.rs:53,
used by the c9r ingress gate at channel.rs:12462-12467 - the very instrument bead btc-policy-9zs
Claim 4 depends on); replay/pending len methods (replay.rs:168, used at server.rs:2306);
AttemptBudget's cfg(test) accessors charges/fails/locked_until/shape (pin.rs:729-756, used at
lib.rs:9349/9366-9368/9472/9518); and Event::watchtower (watchtower.rs:122, used at lib.rs:7382).
