A test-support feature solves these ONLY if it covers the complete set including conditional fields
and cross-crate visibility. Enumerate exhaustively before starting; do not trust this list either.

C3. [P2, CODEX] NEW BLOCKER 6 - PUBLIC-PATH COMPATIBILITY. vault-cli and the integration tests
consume vault_node::chain, vault_node::watchtower, vault_node::nodekey, and root PIN helpers
(vault-cli/src/recovery.rs:44, vault-cli/src/setup.rs:70, vault-node/tests/bitcoind_backend.rs:29).
The bead must choose deliberate vault-node re-exports or migrate those consumers and their Cargo
dependencies. Neither is free.

C4. [P3, FABLE] "Three of the declaring files move" is off by one: of the four files declaring
production mutexes, only TWO move (chain.rs, pin.rs). The conclusion - CoreMutex lives in vault-core
- is unaffected.

C5. [P3, FABLE] The "~1,960 lines" figure for nodekey/replay/prop_*/ingress_trace is wrong; actual
is 2,701 (495+687+722+536+261). The substantive claim - all of these files have ZERO async - was
verified true, so the conclusion is unaffected.

C6. [P3, CODEX] The fourth channel async function closes at channel.rs:5422, not 5420.

CONFIRMED CORRECT: blockers 1, 2, 4 and 5 verify exactly; ingress_trace's reference counts verify
EXACTLY (lib.rs 36, channel.rs 9, zero elsewhere) so its cfg(test) gate genuinely survives; and the
HONEST LIMIT is correct - every wqd violation site is in server.rs/lib.rs/channel.rs, all staying,
and the moving set is grep-verified zero-async.

title: V0-8b: node combine+broadcast; coordinator→relay; demo rework
description:
## V0-8b: node combine+broadcast with RELEASE-AT-FIRE (partials never leave before fire — ADR-0012 invariant 7), no-partial /sign response (pure relay), paired spend+escape candidates, coordinator-auth request-carrier over the channel, ChainBackend package-acceptance + authorized-set, class/refresh contracts. Folded 6 audit blockers (2026-07-17). Depends on V0-9 trust-root.

FULL TASK SPEC (self-contained; source task file gitignored):

# V0-8b: node-side combine + broadcast (release-at-fire); coordinator → pure relay; demo rework

## Environment — read first
- No system C compiler. Run cargo/bitcoind via `nix develop -c ...`.
- **Prerequisites merged:** V0-8a0 (tokio+axum), V0-2b (exact-tx commitment),
  V0-8a (channel: signed envelopes, candidate registry keyed by `commitment_id`,
  verified partial store, `send_partial` pub(crate)), **V0-9-trust-root**
  (`coordinator_auth_pubkey` in the manifest; node verifies coordinator-signed
  tagged requests).
- Authoritative: `docs/adr/0012-...` ("Model-B Hold lifecycle", "The
  node-to-node channel", invariants — ESPECIALLY invariant 7 partial-release),
  `docs/adr/0013-...` §2 (tagged requests), §3 (class predicate), §6 (refresh
  bounds), `CONTEXT.md`. Read `crates/vault-node/src/{channel.rs,lib.rs,chain.rs,
  watchtower.rs}` and `crates/vault-cli/src/demo.rs` before starting.

## Outcome
Nodes assemble the t-of-n signature and broadcast; the coordinator is a pure
relay. Sign-and-register at ingress, **release partials only at fire**, combine +
broadcast at the fire event. The `/sign` response carries NO federation partial,
so a hostile coordinator cannot finalize. This is the spine V0-4b rides.

## Required changes

### 1. Release-at-FIRE, not ingress (codex B1 — ADR-0012 invariant 7, LOAD-BEARING)
- On an accepted request the node **signs its partial(s) and registers the
  candidate at ingress** (pin-independent), but **does NOT transmit any partial
  at ingress**. A partial is released to peers ONLY at its candidate's
  authorized fire event, behind the partial-release gate.
- **Fire event:** hot-class fires at Hold-expiry (`first_seen + hold_secs`);
  escape-class and refresh fire immediately. At fire: nodes exchange partials
  over the channel within a bounded **combine window**
  `[fire_time, min(commitment_expiry, fire_time + combine_slack_secs)]`; when
  **≥ t distinct valid signatures PER INPUT** are present, combine + broadcast.
- Why: releasing at ingress lets a single compromised node collect peers'
  partials during the Hold and finalize/broadcast early — breaking the Hold AND
  duress silence without compromising t nodes. The gate is also what V0-4b uses
  to suppress release under duress.

### 2. `/sign` response carries no federation partial (codex B2 — structural pure-relay)
- Replace the current `Signed(PSBT)` response with a fixed **acknowledgement/
  pending** response containing NO node signature (a pending/accepted status +
  the same fields under both classes). Deleting vault-cli's finalize code is not
  enough — the response must structurally withhold the partial so a post-wrench
  coordinator collecting t responses cannot finalize.
- Test: an end-to-end assertion that the coordinator receives ZERO node
  signatures from `/sign` and cannot construct a broadcastable tx; the demo
  asserts no `sendrawtransaction` originates from vault-cli.

### 3. Coordinator-authenticated request propagation over the channel (codex D1)
- Add a channel `request` message type carrying the **coordinator-signed tagged
  request** (V0-9). A node that receives a request (from the coordinator's
  fan-out OR propagated by a peer) validates `coord_sig` + freshness (V0-9),
  then processes it **idempotently** (register the candidate, sign its own
  partial at ingress) and **propagates it to all peers** — so one delivered node
  brings the rest into the same state. Both request classes use the **identical
  propagation path, message count, and size** (this is the constant-observable
  "propagate the request to all peers" step; V0-4b relies on it so a duress
  request that reaches one node arms the rest). Loop/dup suppression via the
  existing envelope nonce + candidate idempotency.

### 4. Paired spend + escape candidates (codex B4/D2)
- Every `SpendRequest` carries a mandatory escape. Register **two distinct
  candidates** — the spend and the escape — each exact-byte bound
  (`commitment_id` per V0-2b) with an unambiguous **role** (spend | escape) and
  paired by request. **Sign BOTH at ingress** (partials withheld per §1). Expose
  fire-gated collection/combine/broadcast for EITHER candidate (the spend fires
  at Hold-expiry under normal; V0-4b fires the escape at T under duress). The
  escape is node-**VALIDATED** (every input a vault UTXO, every output pays the
  escape descriptor, user sig verifies over exact bytes) — never built.

### 5. ChainBackend + authorized-set (codex B5)
- Extend `ChainBackend` (chain.rs) with: **package `testmempoolaccept`**;
  prevout + ancestor lookup (confirmed and mempool); and an **authorized/accepted
  transaction set** distinguishing vault-authorized-unconfirmed parents (own
  spend-change/refresh) from **external unconfirmed deposits** (excluded —
  toxic-deposit safe). Build over the mempool UTXO set (ADR-0012): a spend may
  chain off a vault-authorized unconfirmed parent (can't be replaced without
  t-of-n node sigs); package-validate before broadcast. **Fatal startup** when
  channel mode is on but no chain backend is configured.
- **Watchtower recognition fix (B5):** replace `sign_log`-based recognition with
  ADR-0012's "validated AND policy-ACCEPTED" set — a spend a node policy-refused
  must NOT count as recognized (else a theft fanned to honest nodes suppresses
  its own alert). This required ADR-0012 fix is otherwise unowned.

### 6. Transaction-class + RefreshRequest contracts (codex B6 — ADR-0013 §§2-3, §6)
- **Mixed-class rejection:** derive class from outputs (ADR-0013 §3); reject a
  mixed hot+escape spend (`PSBT_INCONSISTENT`) — current policy wrongly accepts
  any combination of individually-allowlisted outputs.
- **RefreshRequest** (pin-less, ADR-0013 §2): accept it as a first-class variant
  (not a malformed SpendRequest — reject a SpendRequest-shaped refresh). Enforce
  the **minimum refresh interval** and the **tight refresh fee cap** (§6), and
  **refresh subordination**: a refresh is queued/rejected if a spend is pending
  (coarse queue is fine).
- **EXPIRY_TOO_SHORT:** add to the shared refusal enum; refuse a hot-class spend
  whose commitment expiry `< now + hold_secs + combine_slack_secs`
  (`combine_slack_secs` default **60**); **equality passes** (expiry `==` the
  bound is accepted).

## Tests
- **Release-at-fire:** a node does NOT transmit any partial at ingress; at fire
  it releases and, with ≥ t distinct sigs per input, combines + broadcasts (tx
  confirms on regtest). A compromised node cannot obtain peers' partials before
  fire (assert none delivered pre-fire).
- **No-partial response + pure relay:** `/sign` returns no node signature; the
  coordinator cannot finalize; demo issues no `sendrawtransaction` from vault-cli.
- **Request propagation:** a request delivered to ONE node propagates to all,
  each registers the paired candidates and signs at ingress; identical path/
  count/size for both classes; dup/loop suppressed.
- **Paired candidates:** spend and escape registered as distinct exact-byte
  candidates, both signed at ingress; either is fire-collectable.
- **ChainBackend:** package `testmempoolaccept` gates broadcast; a spend over a
  vault-authorized unconfirmed parent is accepted; over an external unconfirmed
  deposit is excluded; multi-input finalization; a dead peer; delayed candidate
  registration; a backend that rejects the package → no broadcast, no panic.
- **Watchtower recognition:** a policy-REFUSED spend is NOT recognized → alerts.
- **Class/refresh:** mixed hot+escape → `PSBT_INCONSISTENT`; RefreshRequest
  accepted, min-interval + fee cap enforced, subordinated to a pending spend;
  SpendRequest-shaped refresh rejected; `EXPIRY_TOO_SHORT` (with equality
  passing).
- `demo first-light` (reworked, channel ON, coordinator-signed requests) exits 0
  — honest spend confirms via NODE broadcast; theft refused 5/5.

## Scope guard
- Touch `crates/vault-node/`, `crates/vault-cli/`, `crates/vault-proto/`,
  `crates/policy-core/` (mixed-class), Cargo. Do NOT build the duress state
  machine / arming / sweep (V0-4b), dual-pin/lockdown (V0-4a), the recovery
  branch (V0-10), Tor/mTLS (v1). Do NOT weaken any V0-8a channel security
  property or invariant 7.
- Non-goals: RBF/fee-bump beyond the fixed cap, mempool-eviction handling
  (accepted denial — package relay does NOT fully cover it), multi-vault. Size
  advisory; do not compress the tests.
- Do not run `rb-lite`, signal your own process tree, or touch `.rb-lite/`,
  `.ralph-burning/`, `.git/ralph-burning-live/`, `.beads/`.

## Acceptance criteria
- fmt/clippy -D warnings/test --workspace pass; `demo first-light` exits 0 with
  NODES broadcasting and coordinator-signed requests.
- Partials release only at fire (invariant 7 holds); `/sign` carries no partial;
  paired spend+escape candidates + request propagation + ChainBackend
  package-acceptance + class/refresh contracts are in place. The spine is ready
  for V0-4a (pin) and V0-4b (duress) to attach.
close_reason: V0-8b merged to main (63ea4d5): node combine+broadcast release-at-fire, paired user-signed escape, coord-auth carrier, ChainBackend package-acceptance. 173 vault-node tests + demo first-light green; codex adversarial P1 verified non-realizable + folded to V0-4b-core.

title: Configurable recovery timelock (per-vault, warn-only except typed confirmation on mainnet)
description:
TWO sealed-parameter jobs, both blocking Rollout stage 1 (docs/ROLLOUT-PLAN.md).

(1) CONFIGURABLE RECOVERY TIMELOCK — decided 2026-07-29. Today policy_core::RECOVERY_TIMELOCK_UNITS is a hard constant (30375 units x 512s = exactly 180 days) and parse_vault_template (crates/policy-core/src/template.rs:182) REJECTS any descriptor whose timelock differs. The regtest recovery drill only works because it fakes time (setmocktime + a few blocks, explicitly not mining 30375 blocks). On signet the chain is not ours, so "test all paths/recoveries" would mean 180 DAYS OF WALL CLOCK per Recovery test — and Recovery is the last exit when everything else has failed, so it would never be exercised on a real chain. DELIVER: the timelock is chosen PER VAULT at creation; 180 days stays the DEFAULT; a low value emits a WARNING — not a hard floor and not an opt-in flag (the user's explicit call), matching how the setup assemble step already warns on a below-floor KDF rather than refusing. parse_vault_template's equality check becomes a range/consistency check. The value must be manifest-bound so it is federation-uniform and startup-checked, exactly like escape_feerate_floor and escape_coverage_pct. BE HONEST IN THE WARNING TEXT: a short timelock is a WEAKER vault — a thief holding 2-of-3 recovery keys waits hours instead of months.

(2) NETWORK PARAMETER — NetworkKind::Test is hardcoded on the PRODUCTION key path (crates/vault-cli/src/setup.rs:1188); addresses are per-driver Network::{Regtest,Signet} constants; docs/SETUP-CEREMONY.md concedes there is no network parameter anywhere in the codebase yet. The ladder needs signet at stages 1,2,4,6,7 and mainnet at 3,5,8,9, so this is not a constant to flip at the end. DELIVER: one network parameter threaded through the ceremony and every driver, validated at load, and recorded in the sealed artifacts so a node CANNOT boot against a backend on a different chain.

VERIFY: a ceremony sealed for one network refuses to boot against another; a vault sealed with a short timelock warns and still works; addresses derived under each network match an INDEPENDENT tool (the user's own cyberkrill), not just this codebase — vault-cli imports vault-node's own manifest code, so today the ceremony proves internal consistency only.

Dependents:
  <- btc-policy-9y5.8 (blocks) - Core-proven gate (Rollout stage 1): Path suite on signet + external review #1
AMENDED 2026-07-29 after the plan review. Both reviewers rejected warn-only for MAINNET. codex's failure case is banal and decisive: an operator mistakes BIP68 512-second units for days, or automation supplies 1, or a signet config is copied to mainnet — the warning scrolls past, and roughly one 512-second unit later two stolen recovery keys are a complete authorization path for the entire vault, with no PIN, no user key, no Hold, no allowlist and no federation involved. Because the manifest is immutable the operator CANNOT repair it in place; the only fix is rotating the vault. 

DECISION (the user's, after seeing both arguments): NO hard floor — the choice stays the operator's — but on MAINNET a below-default value requires TYPED CONFIRMATION that is RECORDED IN THE CEREMONY ARTIFACTS. Signet and regtest keep warn-only.

IMPLEMENT: (a) the parser/descriptor accepts the full consensus-valid range (so signet tests are free); (b) the CREATION WORKFLOW applies the network policy — warn-only on signet/regtest, typed confirmation on mainnet for anything below the 180-day default; (c) the confirmation and the chosen value land in the ceremony artifacts (ceremony-state.json and manifest.json) so an auditor can see it was deliberate rather than accidental; (d) the ceremony DISPLAYS the chosen duration and the earliest expected maturity date in human units, not in 512-second units — unit confusion is the actual failure mode.

A warning is not an authorization ceremony; a recorded confirmation is. That is the distinction this amendment buys.

ALSO FIX, AND THIS IS A CLOSING REQUIREMENT (codex, restated 2026-08-06): the runbook no longer anticipates this bead -- it was corrected to describe the FROZEN reality, so landing `wdu` makes incident-time text wrong in the other direction. The following places assert the frozen state and must be revised in the SAME change that makes the timelock configurable: (1) docs/OPERATIONS-RUNBOOK.md, "The user was coerced (duress PIN used)" step 5 -- "each coin matures 180 days (fixed for every vault; there is no setting)"; (2) the same file's "The normal path is bricked" section -- "after the fixed 180-day recovery lock"; (3) docs/UPGRADE-AND-ROTATION-POLICY.md:90 -- "the only exit is the 180-day recovery timelock"; (4) the same file's §5 emergency table row at :100 -- "after the 180-day relative timelock"; (5) docs/ROLLOUT-PLAN.md's "The recovery timelock must become configurable" section, which currently opens "NOT YET TRUE"; and (6) docs/adr/0005-nodes-are-sealed-after-setup.md's parenthetical "(fixed at 180 days today; `btc-policy-wdu` is the work to make it per-vault)". Also revise docs/DESIGN.md:272 in the OTHER direction: its "Recovery timelock (target state, gated on `btc-policy-wdu`)" bullet becomes true when `wdu` lands, so remove the target-state gating note. Do NOT close this bead with any of the six frozen-state entries unrevised or the DESIGN gating note still present. The runbook and upgrade-policy entries are incident-time text read after a wrench attack; a stale 'it is fixed, do not look for a setting' is exactly the sentence that wastes an operator's time under duress.

Dependents:
  <- btc-policy-9y5.8 (blocks) - Core-proven gate (Rollout stage 1): Path suite on signet + external review #1




Dependents:
  <- btc-policy-9y5.8 (blocks) - Core-proven gate (Rollout stage 1): Path suite on signet + external review #1

SCOPE CORRECTION 2026-07-30 (user). Earlier drafts of this bead justified the mainnet control against a COMPROMISED SETUP TOOL, citing THREAT-MODEL R8b. That is a misreading and is withdrawn. R8b is scoped to the coordinator TRUSTED-UNTIL-WRENCH (ADR-0012, "Pin handling — Direction 3", and the CONTEXT.md Coordinator entry): the residual is malware resident on the OPERATING coordinator that observes the normal PIN during ordinary spends before a coercion event. The SETUP CEREMONY is a separate, one-time, witnessed phase that precedes any funds, and it is trusted. A compromised ceremony tool would not forge a timelock display — it would seal a descriptor containing its own key or exfiltrate the recovery keys, so hardening this one field against it is incoherent.

WHAT THE CONTROL IS FOR: MISTAKES — unit confusion (BIP68 512-second units read as days), scroll-past, a signet config copied to mainnet. Implement (a) typed confirmation on mainnet for below-default values, with the VALUE in the typed phrase rather than a fixed word (a wrapper pipes a constant otherwise); (b) the confirmation and chosen value recorded in ceremony-state.json and manifest.json; (c) the ceremony DISPLAYING the duration in human units, and any maturity shown as "earliest maturity for coins confirmed now" — relative maturity is per-UTXO and moves with deposits and Refreshes.

DROPPED as over-engineering that only made sense under the withdrawn adversarial-ceremony reading: binding the confirmation artifact to a fresh nonce and manifest hash to prevent replay, and failing closed for automation absent a signed out-of-band authorization. There is no adversary in the model to replay it.

RETAINED, on honest grounds: before funding a mainnet vault, parse the sealed descriptor with an INDEPENDENT tool (the user's cyberkrill) and read the timelock back. Justification is correctness, not adversarial — the setup tool may be BUGGY, and a unit-conversion bug produces exactly the value this control exists to prevent.

SPLIT 2026-07-30 (bead-polish, codex sizing finding): THE NETWORK PARAMETER -- item (2) above -- MOVED TO btc-policy-5ag. This bead is now the configurable recovery timelock alone. The two shared only the category 'sealed parameter'; one is a consensus-parameter policy change with a typed-confirmation ceremony, the other threads NetworkKind through every driver. Read item (2) above as history; btc-policy-5ag is authoritative for it.
notes:
ADR-0016 COUPLING OBLIGATION (added 2026-08-05 after a codex review of the ADR-0016 commit).
ADR-0016 decision 4 requires the Ceremony to present this timelock and `escape_bump_max_fee_pct` as ONE question and to display both resulting values before sealing, while keeping them as two independent manifest fields. This bead depends on btc-policy-mby, so it is definitively second and is the single owner of the combined prompt and display. btc-policy-mby owns the ladder field, its Ceremony input and its independent validation; this bead must not close having made the timelock configurable while leaving the prompts separate. Today the startup rejection that matters is `policy_core::parse_vault_template` (template.rs:182), run by every node at startup; recovery.rs:88 is a redundant drill-side assertion after a parse that already errored. That parse is why the joint question is not buildable before this bead lands -- and it is what this bead must change, not the vestigial check.

title: Enforce the sync/async boundary: five runtime-worker lock sites, the lockdown driver off the runtime, and the rule written down
description:
REWRITTEN 2026-08-02 after a two-model design review (codex gpt-5.6-sol + Claude Fable) falsified this bead's own original text. It previously claimed "/events is the ONE lock-touching handler that parks a runtime worker" and that "every std::sync::Mutex acquisition [is] pushed onto spawn_blocking". Both sentences were false when written. The same claim-outruns-mechanism class this repo keeps shipping - see the named-mitigation audit.

THE RULE, in two parts, because they are not the same rule.
(1) Never hold a std lock ACROSS an .await. Already compiler-enforced: std::sync::MutexGuard is !Send, so a future holding one is !Send, and tokio::spawn and axum handlers both require Send. VERIFIED BY COMPILING both cases. NOT universal: the Runtime::block_on root future (main.rs:36) carries no Send bound, and that hole IS exercised - spawn_drivers (main.rs:71, before serve) calls refresh_vault_unspent_cache -> refresh_vault_unspent_cache_mode (chain.rs:1446), which locks at 1453/1483/1501/1506/1522 around a ~10.4s scan on the block_on thread. Harmless today (nothing is served yet) but it must be named, not assumed away.
(2) Never ACQUIRE a std lock on a runtime worker. NOT compiler-checkable. This is the unenforced half and the actual subject of this bead.

THE FULL SITE LIST (the original four were an undercount; both reviewers independently expanded it).
- /events -> Node::events -> alerts.lock()  (server.rs:393, lib.rs:1935-1940)
- propagate_outbox -> outbox.lock()  (lib.rs:4189), reached from TWO handlers, each after its spawn_blocking await: /sign at server.rs:354 and /channel at server.rs:590
- the lockdown driver (lib.rs:2576) -> lockdown_due -> store.lock() (channel.rs:3893) at 1 Hz, and enter_lockdown -> sign_state.lock() (lib.rs:2003) when due
- fire_tick_with_clock: SIX-PLUS touches, not one - prune_store (store, lib.rs:2707), lockdown_tick (store + sign_state, 2713), due_for_fire (store, 2714), the pending poll (sign_state, 2732), fire_settlement_pollable in the filter (store, 2738), and the release block (2817-2852) which holds sign_state ACROSS nested store acquisitions via is_armed_escape and release_partials. The SAFETY-CRITICAL ORDERING comment at lib.rs:2836-2848 forbids restructuring the release-under-guard, so guard scopes must move INTACT.
Verified clean, do not "fix": the watchtower driver locks only inside spawn_blocking (watchtower.rs:560); critical_lock_poisoned and store_poisoned use Mutex::is_poisoned(), a flag read, not an acquisition.

DELIVER.
1. Fix every site above. Guard scopes move intact; do not restructure the fire release path.
2. Move the LOCKDOWN driver off the runtime onto a dedicated std::thread::Builder thread. lockdown_tick(node, now) is already pure and already takes the clock as a parameter, so only the loop changes. The fire/sweep driver STAYS async (best-effort by design, ADR-0012 two-track model) and moves its lock touches inside spawn_blocking. RATIONALE, CORRECTED: this removes the coupling to the shared bounded blocking pool and is neutral-to-positive for SILENCE (today the deadline tick shares workers with the arm-dependent fire pass). It DOES NOT deliver unconditional Lockdown at T - the binding constraint is the sign_state convoy, which is bead btc-policy-9zs. Do not restate the old claim.
3. A sleeper/tick SEAM, because the thread move otherwise DELETES A SILENCE TEST. server.rs:1040 (healthz_live_heartbeat_transition_follows_the_deadline_schedule) is start_paused, spawns the driver as a task, drives it with tokio::time::advance, and asserts an ARMED and an IDLE node publish the same heartbeat bucket on the same tick - a duress-oracle regression test. A raw thread breaks its mechanism. The replacement must preserve that armed-vs-idle same-tick assertion.
4. A CoreMutex newtype over std::sync::Mutex carrying a DEBUG-ONLY assertion. 13 production declaration sites (chain.rs 443/445/447; channel.rs 2723/2724/2726/2730; lib.rs 1081/1108/1112/1144; pin.rs 95/126 - about 11 distinct allocations, since the two pin fields alias one lock and alerts is shared by Node and ChannelState). Acquisition sites need no edits IF lock/try_lock/is_poisoned return the std types, which keeps Node::critical_lock_poisoned (lib.rs:2077) working. NO Deref - that is an assertion bypass. Constructors and fn signatures taking &Mutex / Arc<Mutex> still need edits (watchtower.rs:448-449/545-546, pin.rs:243/321, channel.rs:2840).
5. The DETECTION MECHANISM, which is where this will go wrong. Handle::try_current() returns Ok on BOTH runtime workers and spawn_blocking threads - no public tokio API distinguishes them - so a thread-local marker is required. THREE false-positive classes that must be handled or the assertion fires constantly in debug: (a) FOUR production spawn_blocking sites bypass blocking_with_lockdown_net entirely - lib.rs:2493, lib.rs:2760, lib.rs:2858, watchtower.rs:560 - so EVERY spawn_blocking must go through a marking wrapper, not just the seam; (b) the block_on startup warmup path above; (c) plain #[tokio::test] current-thread tests that lock node state directly in async bodies.
6. Extend the single-worker test pattern. NOTE the original wording here was impossible: /events cannot answer while the alerts lock is held, because it needs that lock. The assertable property is: hold alerts, /events stays PENDING, and /healthz ANSWERS CONCURRENTLY - which is what proves the single worker was not parked. Existing precedent: a_blocking_sign_does_not_delay_events (server.rs:2312, worker_threads=1) holds sign_state, which /events never takes, so it passes without exercising the risk. Verify the new test BITES by introducing the violation, watching it fail, and reverting.
7. Write the ADR. The two rules, the block_on exception, the two-track thread mapping, and the boundary the crate split will later follow - so btc-policy-imb is designed against a line that already exists. ALSO update DESIGN.md:113 and the main.rs:8-19 MIN_WORKER_THREADS rationale: both currently justify the worker floor BY the deadline driver pinning a worker, and the move makes them stale.

NON-GOALS. No tokio::sync::Mutex - it would delete the !Send tripwire. No async chain RPC - it is loopback, buys no latency or throughput, and would cost async_trait or a teardown of the 5 production Arc<dyn ChainBackend + Send + Sync> sites (lib.rs 1943/2689/2700/2893, watchtower.rs:543). The crate split is bead btc-policy-uy9, NOT this one. The convoy fix is btc-policy-9zs, NOT this one.

SEPARATELY NOTED, not in scope: latch_lockdown does an xattr write plus fsync (lib.rs:2028-2031) on a runtime worker via the post-await poison rechecks (server.rs:179-181, lib.rs:2916-2917) - blocking I/O, not a lock, poison-path only. Accept explicitly in the ADR or fold in deliberately. RPC_TIMEOUT (chain.rs:2123) is a per-syscall socket timeout, not an end-to-end deadline, and WALLET_BUILD_RPC_TIMEOUT is 600s (chain.rs:2126).

INVARIANTS: SILENCE (pin-uniform observables - /events must gain no branch, byte, or lock depending on arm state, and item 3 must not lose the armed-vs-idle assertion); signer/partial COUPLING + RELEASE-GATE; Lockdown at T; determinism across the honest set; fail-closed.

GATES: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; full workspace tests; the bite verification in item 6, reported explicitly; all three demos; attack all (btc-policy-rt0 EXPECTED red - report, do not tune).

=================================================================
AMENDED 2026-08-02 after a two-model review of this bead's text (codex + Fable vs source @63290b9).
=================================================================

B1. [P1, CODEX] THE DEDICATED THREAD NEEDS A LIFECYCLE CONTRACT, not only a sleeper seam.
std::thread::Builder::spawn CAN FAIL, but spawn_drivers returns () and main proceeds straight to
serve (lib.rs:2437, main.rs:71) - a failed safety-thread spawn would leave a node serving with NO
Lockdown driver, the worst possible silent failure. Spawn failure MUST be fatal BEFORE serving.
Also preserve: the immediate first tick, the absolute non-reset cadence (tokio::time::interval's
current behaviour), and the driver's spawn CONDITIONS (backend present + channel mode,
lib.rs:2437-2449). Note the moved loop body is lockdown_tick_with_lockdown_net (heartbeat + panic
net), NOT bare lockdown_tick. The replacement test needs deterministic termination: the current one
aborts both live tasks (server.rs:1058, 1115), which a thread cannot be.

B2. [P2, CODEX] THE HEARTBEAT'S SEMANTICS CHANGE, NOT JUST ITS TEST MECHANISM - this bead
understated it. last_deadline_tick currently claims to detect a runtime that has stopped scheduling
(lib.rs:958, DESIGN.md:113). An INDEPENDENT OS THREAD KEEPS ADVANCING THROUGH EXACTLY THAT
CONDITION, so the heartbeat stops being evidence the runtime is alive. Decide deliberately what the
heartbeat now attests and rewrite its contract. More docs go stale than the two named above:
lib.rs:2570, server.rs:1032, and SBOM-AND-DEPENDENCY-POLICY.md:67.

B3. [P3, CODEX] Cited range short: the watchtower driver spans watchtower.rs:542-598, not 541-575.

CONFIRMED CORRECT (Fable, verified line-for-line): the full site list; the server.rs:1040
description in every particular (start_paused, task-spawned driver, tokio::time::advance, and the
armed-vs-idle same-bucket assertion at server.rs:1104-1107); and the fire-driver split - fire_tick's
lock touches all sit in sync stretches between existing awaits, so each region including the release
block wraps INTACT in a spawn_blocking closure. Fable's independent sweep found no unlisted
async-context lock site and no other production spawn of the driver.

title: Flaky: retry_fails_over_from_a_dead_endorsed_endpoint_to_a_live_one assumes a released ephemeral port stays unbound
description:
FOUND 2026-08-04 by Claude Fable during the btc-policy-9zs multi-reviewer loop: one failure in four
full-workspace runs. PRE-EXISTING — the 9zs diff touches neither this test nor the code path it
exercises.

THE FAILURE: `channel::net::retry_fails_over_from_a_dead_endorsed_endpoint_to_a_live_one`
(crates/vault-node/src/channel.rs, the `net` test module) failed with
`partial permanently rejected: WRONG_MANIFEST`.

THE MECHANISM: the test binds three ephemeral ports, drops two of them, and then assumes the
"dead" port STAYS unbound for the duration. Under parallel `cargo test` load another test's server
can bind that just-released port and answer the request — with a different manifest, hence
WRONG_MANIFEST rather than the connection failure the test is written to expect. Classic
bind-then-release-then-assume-dead race; it gets more likely the more tests run concurrently and
the faster the box.

WHY IT IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN TOLERATING: it produces a CONFUSING red. The symptom
(WRONG_MANIFEST) points at manifest handling, which is a crown-jewel-adjacent area, so whoever
hits it burns time in the wrong place before concluding it was a port race. A red that misdirects
is worse than a red that is merely noisy — and this repo has one precedent already
(btc-policy-rt0), where a flaky red was rationalised as expected and left open for days.

LIKELY FIXES, in order of preference: (a) hold the "dead" socket bound but non-accepting so the
port cannot be reused, and assert on connect/read failure rather than on a bind failure;
(b) point the dead endpoint at a reserved-but-closed port the harness owns for the whole run;
(c) if neither is workable, make the assertion tolerate WRONG_MANIFEST as an alternative
dead-endpoint symptom and say in a comment why that is sound — but prefer (a), since (c) weakens
what the test proves.

VERIFY: the test passes 20 consecutive full-workspace runs under `cargo test --workspace` on a
loaded box. State which fix was taken and why the port can no longer be stolen.

title: Operator CLI slice: 'refresh' — the pin-less self-spend that resets the recovery timelock
description:
SPLIT OUT OF btc-policy-mby 2026-07-30 (codex+Fable bead review). Slice 2 of 4. DEPENDS ON the mby core substrate.

WHY IT IS ITS OWN SLICE: refresh is a DISTINCT REQUEST TYPE, not a variant of spend. ADR-0012 defines the pin-less RefreshRequest { refresh, nonce, expiry, policy_version } against SpendRequest's { spend, escape, pin, ... }; it carries no pin and no mandatory escape, it releases immediately rather than serving the Hold, and it has its own refusal codes (REFRESH_TOO_SOON, REFRESH_FEE_EXCEEDS_CAP, REFRESH_SUBORDINATED) and its own ADR-0013 bounds.

WHY IT MATTERS MOST: without refresh the recovery branch matures and the 2-of-3 recovery keyset -- distributed to THIRD PARTIES by design, since it doubles as the inheritance mechanism -- becomes a complete authorization path needing no PIN, no user key, no Hold, no allowlist and no federation. ADR-0012 quietly assumes this command exists. btc-policy-msj (the maturity countdown and nags) depends on this slice specifically.

DELIVER: 'refresh' against a sealed vault -- select coins, compose the self-spend, honour the ADR-0013 minimum-interval and fee bounds, user-sign through the core's signing seam, relay, watch to confirmation. Decide and document the REFRESH STRATEGY the design left open (DESIGN.md 'Refresh batching and privacy'): consolidate UTXOs per refresh (cheaper, worse privacy, larger single-coin exposure) versus refresh-in-place per coin (costlier, preserves the UTXO set). Pick one, state why, and make it configurable if the argument is close.

VERIFY: a regtest vault with coins of mixed age is refreshed and every coin's relative timelock demonstrably resets; REFRESH_TOO_SOON is returned and handled when the minimum interval is not met; a refresh racing a pending hot spend behaves per ADR-0013's subordination rule rather than silently winning.

title: V0-2b: bind commitment to exact tx (version, nLockTime, nSequence)
description:
## Outcome
The Commitment (vault-proto) binds the EXACT unsigned transaction — version, nLockTime, and per-input nSequence — so commitment_id uniquely identifies a transaction. Prerequisite for the node channel (V0-8a): its candidate registry keys on commitment_id, and without this two distinct txs alias one candidate → non-combinable partials.

## Why this exists
Surfaced by the second-model bead audit (codex, 2026-07-16). V0-PLAN.md:13 lists V0-2b as a V0-8 feeder; DESIGN.md's "Transaction commitment" SUPERSEDED note names these three fields as MANDATORY. The current Commitment omits them, so commitment_id is not a unique tx identity — a real correctness blocker for V0-8a.

## Verification (ship gate)
Three mutation tests (version-only, nLockTime-only, single-input-nSequence-only each change the id); coordinator/node round-trip identical; existing anti-replay idempotency regression green; workspace tests + demo first-light green.

---
FULL TASK SPEC (self-contained executable memory; source task file is gitignored):

# V0-2b: bind the commitment to the EXACT unsigned transaction (version, nLockTime, per-input nSequence)

## Environment — read first
- No system C compiler. Run EVERY cargo/bitcoind command through the flake dev
  shell: `nix develop -c cargo test`, etc. Plain `cargo` fails.
- Authoritative: `docs/adr/0012-model-b-spend-and-duress-architecture.md` (the
  commitment must bind the exact unsigned transaction so two distinct
  transactions never share a commitment id) and `docs/DESIGN.md` "Transaction
  commitment" (the SUPERSEDED note names version/nLockTime/nSequence as
  MANDATORY additions). `docs/V0-PLAN.md:13` lists V0-2b as a feeder of V0-8.

## Why this exists (the bug it closes)
`crates/vault-proto/src/lib.rs` `Commitment` currently binds wallet_id, input
outpoints, outputs, fee, expiry, and policy_version — but NOT the transaction
`version`, `nLockTime`, or each input's `nSequence`. Two transactions that
differ ONLY in those fields therefore produce the **same `commitment_id`**.

This is load-bearing for the node channel (V0-8a, btc-policy-byf): that task
keys the candidate registry by `commitment_id` and verifies peer partials
against the node's own canonical view. If `commitment_id` does not uniquely
identify the exact unsigned transaction, two distinct transactions can **alias**
one candidate — a node could store/verify a partial against the wrong
transaction's sighash, and the channel could gather non-combinable partials.
V0-8a is not safe to build until this is closed.

## Required changes (`crates/vault-proto` + producers/consumers)
1. **Extend `Commitment`** with the transaction-level fields:
   - `version: i32` (tx version)
   - `lock_time: u32` (nLockTime)
   and **extend `CommitmentInput`** with:
   - `sequence: u32` (per-input nSequence)
2. **Extend `canonical_bytes`** to serialize the new fields at fixed width,
   big-endian, in a fixed position, consistent with the existing scheme
   (version + lock_time in the header region; each input's `sequence` alongside
   its txid/vout). The encoding stays greenfield-until-v1, but must round-trip
   byte-identically on coordinator and node (the existing T4 property).
3. **Update every producer**: wherever the coordinator/CLI builds a
   `Commitment` from a PSBT/unsigned tx, populate version/lock_time/sequence
   from the actual transaction (never defaults — read them from the tx).
4. **Update every consumer/check**: wherever `vault-node` re-derives or
   verifies a commitment (`commitment_of`, policy-core PSBT consistency), it
   must re-read these fields from ITS OWN copy of the unsigned transaction and
   include them — never trust a coordinator-supplied summary (the
   node-validates-own-source invariant).
5. **No behavior change to the sign decision** beyond tighter commitment
   identity: a spend that was accepted before is still accepted; only the
   commitment id now distinguishes transactions that were previously
   indistinguishable.

## Tests (`vault-proto` + `vault-node`)
- **Mutation tests (the point):** starting from one unsigned transaction,
  changing ONLY `version`, ONLY `nLockTime`, or ONLY a single input's
  `nSequence` each produces a DIFFERENT `commitment_id`. (Three separate tests;
  each field is load-bearing.)
- **Round-trip:** coordinator-built and node-rebuilt commitments over the same
  transaction produce identical `canonical_bytes` and `commitment_id` (T4).
- **Regression:** the existing anti-replay/idempotency tests still pass (an
  identical resubmission is still idempotent — same tx ⇒ same id).
- `nix develop -c cargo test --workspace` green; `demo first-light` exits 0.

## Scope guard
- Touch `crates/vault-proto/` and the producer/consumer call sites in
  `crates/vault-cli/` and `crates/vault-node/` (+ policy-core if it re-derives
  the commitment). Do NOT rework the HTTP layer (that is V0-8a0), the channel
  (V0-8a), or the demo beyond making it pass. Do NOT change any OTHER commitment
  field or the policy checks.
- Small, surgical migration. Target ≤ 300 lines incl tests.
- Do not run `rb-lite`, signal your own process tree, or touch `.rb-lite/`,
  `.ralph-burning/`, `.git/ralph-burning-live/`.

## Acceptance criteria
- `nix develop -c cargo fmt --check`, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo test
  --workspace` pass; `demo first-light` exits 0.
- `Commitment`/`CommitmentInput` bind version/nLockTime/nSequence; the three
  mutation tests prove each field changes the id; the round-trip test proves
  coordinator and node agree. The commitment now uniquely identifies the exact
  unsigned transaction — V0-8a's `commitment_id`-keyed candidate registry is
  safe to build on it.

title: Rollout stage 9 freeze: full Path suite on the real configuration, then external review #2
description:
Rollout ladder stage 9 (docs/ROLLOUT-PLAN.md), split out of u5r on 2026-07-29 so the gate location is unambiguous.

Stage 9 runs the FULL two-vault Path suite on the exact configuration an alpha would ship — many providers, sealed hosts, mainnet — and then FREEZES that artifact for external review #2 (the deployed system).

WHY IT IS ITS OWN RUNG, separate from the stage 6-8 work in u5r: bq6 (hardware signing) and gbw (frozen reproducible release) gate THIS rung, not the start of stage 6. Hanging them off the whole 6-9 bead was ambiguous — read as 'cannot start' it pulled hardware signing before stage 6, contradicting the plan; read as 'cannot close' it said nothing about where in 6-9 it lands (Fable second-pass review Q3/Q4).

RESCOPED 2026-07-30 (owner decision: hardware signing is optional and postponed). This paragraph used to be a VALIDITY REQUIREMENT reading 'bq6 must be EXERCISED ON A SIGNET RUNG (6 or 7) before this stage'. It is now a RECOMMENDATION. ADR-0015 lines 86-95 deliberately do not require hardware signing for the capped rungs 3-8, and btc-policy-bq6 gates this bead and nothing earlier. This was the FIFTH bead carrying the 'from stage 7' claim; the other four (mby, u5r, 4y3, bq6) were corrected earlier the same day and this one was missed.

THE COST THE OLD REQUIREMENT WAS PROTECTING AGAINST IS REAL AND IS ACCEPTED, NOT DISMISSED: because bq6 now first runs here, the PSBT hand-off, the device-display trust boundary and the escape co-sign path all debut at the freeze rung, and stage 8's long soak will have exercised a spend path this stage replaces. So this stage must BUDGET FOR THAT rather than discover it: treat the hardware signer's first appearance as a material configuration change, and expect the Path suite here to find things the soak could not have. If bq6 does happen to land before stage 7, exercising it on a signet rung is preferable -- with a FRESH hardware-generated user key, never one previously exposed as software -- but that is an opportunity, not a gate.

THE CAPS LIFT HERE, NOT BEFORE. ADR-0015's dust caps carry stages 3-8; lifting them requires bq6 landed and review #2 remediated.

VERIFY: full Path suite on both vaults, on the shipping configuration, with the hardware signer in the loop; the frozen artifact's hashes match a rebuild on a second machine (gbw); review #2 findings remediated AND re-tested before stage 10 — a material finding means a new binary, which under ADR-0005 means a vault rotation and a fresh soak, so budget for that loop rather than assuming a clean pass.

title: V0-9 (slice): coordinator auth trust-root in manifest
description:
## V0-9 (minimal slice): coordinator auth trust-root — coordinator_auth_pubkey in the manifest; nodes verify coordinator-signed tagged requests over canonical bytes + nonce/expiry. Missing prerequisite surfaced by the 2026-07-17 spine audit (V0-8b cannot authenticate requests without it).

FULL TASK SPEC (self-contained; source task file gitignored):

# V0-9 (minimal slice): coordinator auth trust-root in the manifest

## Environment — read first
- No system C compiler. Run cargo/bitcoind via `nix develop -c ...`.
- **Minimal slice of V0-9** (surfaced by the 2026-07-17 spine audit as a missing
  prerequisite for V0-8b's coordinator-signed tagged requests). This builds ONLY
  the coordinator-auth trust-root; full provisioning UX (SSH deploy, backup
  ceremony) stays later V0-9 work. Authoritative: `docs/adr/0013-...` §4
  (manifest: `coordinator_auth_pubkey`), §2 (coordinator-signed requests), §7;
  `CONTEXT.md` (Manifest, Coordinator). The V0-8a channel already pins the
  per-node channel identities in a provisional manifest; this adds the
  coordinator's key to that same root.

## Outcome
Every node is sealed to a single **`coordinator_auth_pubkey`** in its immutable
(provisional) manifest, and can verify that a tagged request
(`SpendRequest`/`RefreshRequest`, ADR-0013 §2) is signed by that key over the
**full canonical request bytes** (incl. a fresh nonce + expiry). The coordinator
(vault-cli) holds the matching secret and signs every request. This is the trust
root V0-8b's Model-B spend path authenticates against.

## Why this exists
V0-8b requires coordinator-signed requests, but the config/manifest has no
coordinator key today (the provisional manifest hashes only channel membership).
Without this, a V0-8b implementer would have to invent where the key lives and
who can authorize requests — a security-relevant decision that must be pinned
once, here.

## Required changes (`crates/vault-node`, `crates/vault-proto`, `crates/vault-cli`, config)
1. **Manifest field:** add `coordinator_auth_pubkey` (33-byte compressed secp)
   to the `BaseManifest` (ADR-0013 §4) — it is part of the hashed structure, so
   changing it is a new vault. The `[channel]`/manifest config carries it.
2. **Request signing:** the coordinator signs
   `coord_sig = sign(coord_auth_sk, tagged_hash("btc-policy/coord-request/v0",
   canonical_bytes(request)))` where the request is the full tagged
   `SpendRequest{spend, escape, pin, nonce, expiry, policy_version}` or
   `RefreshRequest{refresh, nonce, expiry, policy_version}` (ADR-0013 §2). Define
   the canonical request serialization (fixed field order; the same
   length-prefix conventions the channel uses).
3. **Node verification:** a node rejects any request whose `coord_sig` does not
   verify against its manifest-pinned `coordinator_auth_pubkey`, OR whose `nonce`
   is seen, OR whose `expiry` is past / beyond `now + max_commitment_age_secs`
   (node's own clock). This is the coordinator-auth + freshness gate every
   request passes at ingress (before the pin).
4. **Demo provisioning:** `demo` generates the coordinator keypair once and
   provisions the same `coordinator_auth_pubkey` into every node's manifest, and
   the coordinator signs the requests it relays. (Regtest provisioning — no SSH.)
5. **Coordinator key lifecycle (ADR-0013 §7):** rotation = new vault (the key is
   in the immutable manifest). Document; no rotation mechanism is built.

## Tests
- A request correctly coord-signed over its canonical bytes verifies; a wrong
  key, a tampered field (any of spend/escape/pin/nonce/expiry), a stale expiry,
  or a replayed nonce → rejected.
- The manifest hash changes if `coordinator_auth_pubkey` changes (it is in the
  hashed BaseManifest).
- Demo provisions one coordinator root to all nodes; a request from a coordinator
  whose key is NOT in the manifest → rejected by every node.
- `demo first-light` exits 0 with coordinator-signed requests.

## Scope guard
- Touch `crates/vault-node/`, `crates/vault-proto/` (request types + coord-sig),
  `crates/vault-cli/` (sign + provision in demo), config. Do NOT build the
  Model-B combine/broadcast (V0-8b), duress (V0-4), SSH deploy / backup ceremony
  (later V0-9), or key rotation.
- Non-goals: multi-coordinator, key backup UX, HSM. Minimal correct trust root.
- Do not run `rb-lite`, signal your own process tree, or touch `.rb-lite/`,
  `.ralph-burning/`, `.git/ralph-burning-live/`, `.beads/`.

## Acceptance criteria
- fmt/clippy -D warnings/test --workspace pass; `demo first-light` exits 0.
- `coordinator_auth_pubkey` is in the immutable manifest; nodes verify
  coordinator-signed tagged requests over canonical bytes + nonce/expiry
  freshness; the demo provisions one root to all nodes. V0-8b can authenticate
  requests against this root.

title: validate_ancestors does one full getrawmempool per input parent (nvr follow-up)
description: Fable nvr review [P3-3], PRE-EXISTING (not introduced by btc-policy-nvr, whose fix removed the sibling pathology one level up). crates/vault-node/src/chain.rs ~366: whenever a ladder rung IS resident, every fire tick runs assemble_replacement_package -> validate_ancestors(.., false), which calls ChainBackend::mempool_transaction once PER INPUT'S PARENT purely to conclude 'absent => confirmed'. On the Core backend each of those is a FULL uncached getrawmempool. An escape sweeping K vault UTXOs therefore does K full mempool pulls per 1 Hz tick — potentially MORE than the up-to-4 that btc-policy-nvr just removed, and worst under the same congestion that makes the combine window tightest (measured context: signet's 72.2M-output UTXO set, docs/SIGNET-SPEND-RECORD.md). FIX: reuse the batched ChainBackend::mempool_resident added by nvr, or add a membership-set variant (e.g. mempool_contains(&[Txid]) -> HashSet<Txid>) so the ancestry walk resolves every parent against ONE snapshot. Same constraints as nvr: semantics must be identical (a parent absent from the mempool still means confirmed), one snapshot is MORE coherent than N successive ones, and the escape fire path is crown-jewel code — the resident rung is what the replacement's ancestry proof is built against. Gates: fmt/clippy-D/workspace tests, attack 16/16, all 3 demos, plus a call-count assertion proving the collapse (regtest timing proves nothing here).
